128pub(crate) async fn yield_once() {
129    let mut yielded = false;
130    std::future::poll_fn(|context| {
131        if yielded {
132            Poll::Ready(())
133        } else {
134            yielded = true;
135            context.waker().wake_by_ref();
136            Poll::Pending
137        }
138    })
139    .await;
140}

142#[derive(Debug)]
143struct InodePool {
144    // TODO(T87258449): merge these two maps:
145    inodes: HashMap<RawInode, DetInode>,
146    detinodes_info: HashMap<DetInode, DetInodeInfo>,
147    /// Counter backing the minted [`DetInode`]s. Deliberately a plain integer:
148    /// it is the *source* of deterministic inodes, not one itself, and typing
149    /// it `RawInode` previously blurred that distinction.
150    ///
151    /// It counts *requests*, not distinct host inodes: see [`Self::add_inode`].
152    next_inode: u64,
153    /// Virtual mtimes set (by a write or `utimensat`) on host inodes that have
154    /// no deterministic number yet. Setting an mtime does not number the file:
155    /// whether those calls reach the pool depends on host state (see
156    /// [`Self::set_mtime`]), so they must not consume counter values. The
157    /// file's first numbering request takes the pending mtime.
158    pending_mtimes: HashMap<RawInode, LogicalTime>,
159    /// Mappings whose file lost its last name (see [`Self::retire`]), kept
160    /// for the descriptors that can still reach it.
161    retired: HashMap<RawInode, DetInode>,
162    /// Files that lost their last name before anything numbered them, with
163    /// the virtual mtime a write through a remaining descriptor set, if any.
164    /// A descriptor sighting numbers such a file as retired, and a later name
165    /// is another file (see [`Self::forget_retired`]), so the next file the
166    /// host gives the inode inherits neither the number nor the mtime.
167    retired_unnumbered: HashMap<RawInode, Option<LogicalTime>>,
168    /// When each retired inode, numbered or not, was retired: the value of
169    /// `retirements` then. A directory snapshot taken before that cannot show
170    /// a new file under the inode (see [`InodeSighting::Listed`]).
171    retired_at: HashMap<RawInode, u64>,
172    /// How many retirements there have been. Each follows a guest's removal
173    /// of a last name, so the count is the guest's, like the counter.
174    retirements: u64,
175    /// Every file that has held each host inode, oldest first, kept after a
176    /// later file discards a retirement: a directory snapshot taken while an
177    /// earlier file held the inode must still name that file (codex
178    /// re-review of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849>, P1).
179    generations: HashMap<RawInode, Vec<Generation>>,
180    /// How many history records the snapshot lookups have examined, for the
181    /// test that bounds the lookup's cost.
182    #[cfg(test)]
183    listed_probes: u64,
184    /// How many retired mappings a later sighting showed the host had given to
185    /// another file (see [`Self::forget_retired`]). Diagnostic only: it
186    /// follows host state and never reaches the guest.
187    reused: u64,
188    /// The key each procfs host inode, and each procfs path key, is pooled
189    /// under (see [`Self::procfs_key`]): the host inode its entry was first
190    /// numbered under. Every value is also its own key.
191    procfs_keys: HashMap<RawInode, RawInode>,
192    /// For each thread ID, the value of `threads_counted` just after each
193    /// guest thread given that ID was counted, in order (see
194    /// [`Self::count_incarnation`]).
195    incarnations: HashMap<i32, Vec<u64>>,
196    /// How many guest threads have been counted (see
197    /// [`Self::count_incarnation`]).
198    threads_counted: u64,
199    /// The state Linux keeps on a per-process `/proc` file's inode that
200    /// Detcore keeps for the files it renders, by their inode number (see
201    /// [`Self::rendered_file_state`]).
202    rendered_file_states: HashMap<u64, crate::procfs::listing::RenderedFileState>,
203}
204
205/// How a numbering request reached its file, which decides whether a retired
206/// mapping (see `InodePool::retire`) answers it.
207#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
208pub enum InodeSighting {
209    /// Through a descriptor without a link count, or a stat that reports no
210    /// link (`fstat` after `unlink`, `/proc/self/fd/N` of an unlinked file).
211    /// Either can reach the file a retired mapping describes.
212    Descriptor,
213    /// A file that has a name: a directory entry read now, or any stat that
214    /// reports a nonzero `st_nlink`. A retired file has no link and can never
215    /// get one back, so this is another file that the host gave the freed
216    /// inode.
217    Name,
218    /// A directory entry from a snapshot taken when there had been this many
219    /// retirements. The snapshot can be older than the entry's removal: a
220    /// stream reads the whole directory at its first `getdents` and returns
221    /// the rest later (codex review of
222    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849>, P1). So it shows a
223    /// new file only for an inode retired before it was taken.
224    Listed(u64),
225}
226
227/// What a directory snapshot records of the inode pool when it is taken, so
228/// that the entries it returns later are numbered as they were then.
229#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
230pub struct SnapshotMark {
231    /// How many retirements there had been (see [`InodeSighting::Listed`]):
232    /// an entry can be returned after its file's last name is gone.
233    pub retirements: u64,
234    /// How many guest threads had been counted (see
235    /// `InodePool::count_incarnation`): an entry can be returned after a task
236    /// it names exited and a new thread took its ID.
237    pub threads_counted: u64,
238}

240/// One file that held a host inode (see `InodePool::generations`). It held
241/// the inode from just after the previous file's retirement until its own.
242#[derive(Debug)]
243struct Generation {
244    /// Its number, or `None` while nothing has numbered it.
245    number: Option<DetInode>,
246    /// The retirement count at which it lost its last name, if it has.
247    retired: Option<u64>,
248    /// The mtime a write left on it before anything numbered it.
249    pending: Option<LogicalTime>,
250}

252/// Everything we know (globally) about a DetInode.
253#[derive(Debug)]
254struct DetInodeInfo {
255    /// The virtual mtime, or `None` while no stat has observed the file and no
256    /// write or explicit time update has set it. Many paths (open, read,
257    /// getdents) mint a DetInode before any stat, so the first-seen policy is
258    /// applied at the first stat rather than at minting; otherwise whether a
259    /// file kept a canonical mtime would depend on which syscall touched it
260    /// first. An unresolved mtime reads as the epoch.
261    mtime: Option<LogicalTime>,
262}
263
264/// Whole-second host mtimes, with a zero nanosecond part, that a file keeps
265/// when Hermit first sees it, instead of having its mtime replaced by the
266/// epoch (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3639>).
267///
268/// These values are canonical and content-independent: they are written
269/// deliberately by tools that erase timestamps, so they carry no host clock
270/// or run-specific information. Revealing them makes whether a file's host
271/// mtime is canonical part of Hermit's input, like the file's contents: a
272/// guest that rewrites the host mtime of an input file (`touch f` after
273/// `stat f` on a canonical file) changes the input of the next run, exactly
274/// as rewriting its contents would.
275/// - `1` (1970-01-01T00:00:01Z) is the mtime of every file and directory in
276///   the Nix store (seconds 1, nanoseconds 0). nixpkgs' stdenv derives
277///   `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the newest source mtime, so reporting the epoch
278///   instead moves embedded build timestamps away from a native build's.
279/// - `0` is what `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` tooling and archive normalizers write.
280///
281/// Matching is exact. A non-zero nanosecond part, or any other second, is a
282/// real timestamp, and the file gets the epoch as before.
283pub const CANONICAL_FILE_MTIME_SECONDS: [i64; 2] = [0, 1];
284
285/// What a syscall observed about a file's host mtime, already reduced to the
286/// only part the virtual mtime may depend on.
287#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
288pub enum ObservedMtime {
289    /// The caller did not read the file's metadata (open, read, getdents...).
290    Unobserved,
291    /// A stat observed a host mtime that is a real timestamp.
292    HostSpecific,
293    /// A stat observed one of [`CANONICAL_FILE_MTIME_SECONDS`], which is kept.
294    Canonical(LogicalTime),
295}
296
297impl ObservedMtime {
298    /// Classify a host mtime that a stat reported.
299    pub fn from_host_mtime(tv_sec: i64, tv_nsec: i64) -> Self {
300        match u64::try_from(tv_sec) {
301            Ok(secs) if tv_nsec == 0 && CANONICAL_FILE_MTIME_SECONDS.contains(&tv_sec) => {
302                ObservedMtime::Canonical(LogicalTime::from_secs(secs))
303            }
304            _ => ObservedMtime::HostSpecific,
305        }
306    }
307
308    /// The virtual mtime to assign to a file whose mtime is still unresolved:
309    /// a canonical value is kept, a real timestamp becomes the epoch, and no
310    /// observation leaves it unresolved.
311    fn first_seen_mtime(self, epoch: LogicalTime) -> Option<LogicalTime> {
312        match self {
313            ObservedMtime::Unobserved => None,
314            ObservedMtime::HostSpecific => Some(epoch),
315            ObservedMtime::Canonical(mtime) => Some(mtime),
316        }
317    }
318}

369
370impl InodePool {
371    fn new() -> Self {
372        InodePool {
373            inodes: HashMap::new(),
374            detinodes_info: HashMap::new(),
375            // Above the fixed stdio inodes (`DET_SPECIAL_INODE_OFFSET`), so a
376            // pooled number can never collide with one of them.
377            next_inode: crate::consts::DET_INODE_OFFSET.as_raw(),
378            pending_mtimes: HashMap::new(),
379            retired: HashMap::new(),
380            retired_unnumbered: HashMap::new(),
381            retired_at: HashMap::new(),
382            retirements: 0,
383            generations: HashMap::new(),
384            #[cfg(test)]
385            listed_probes: 0,
386            reused: 0,
387            procfs_keys: HashMap::new(),
388            incarnations: HashMap::new(),
389            threads_counted: 0,
390            rendered_file_states: HashMap::new(),
391        }
392    }
393
394    /// How many guest threads have been given task ID `tid` in this run (see
395    /// [`Self::count_incarnation`]): the incarnation of the one holding it
396    /// now, 0 for an ID no guest thread has held.
397    fn incarnation(&self, tid: i32) -> u32 {
398        self.incarnations.get(&tid).map_or(0, |counted| {
399            u32::try_from(counted.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
400        })
401    }
402
403    /// What Detcore's process table says of the task `named` and its thread
404    /// `thread` (`existence`: `Scheduler::procfs_task`'s whether it exists
405    /// and whether it has exited), with the incarnation each number has now
406    /// ([`Self::incarnation`]).
407    fn procfs_task_answer(
408        &self,
409        named: DetTid,
410        thread: Option<DetTid>,
411        (exists, without_mm): (bool, bool),
412    ) -> crate::procfs::listing::ProcfsTaskAnswer {
413        crate::procfs::listing::ProcfsTaskAnswer {
414            exists,
415            without_mm,
416            process_incarnation: self.incarnation(named.as_raw()),
417            thread_incarnation: thread.map(|thread| self.incarnation(thread.as_raw())),
418        }
419    }
420
421    /// Apply `change` to the state of the rendered per-process `/proc` file
422    /// numbered `inode`, and return the state. Every change comes in its
423    /// guest thread's turn, so their order is the scheduler's.
424    ///
425    /// Only a file whose owner wrote its state (an mtime, a write hint) has
426    /// an entry; a read of any other inserts none. Entries are kept for the
427    /// run: a per-process inode names one task generation
428    /// (`procfs_inode::per_process_inode`), and a descriptor or a directory
429    /// of a task that is gone can still reach its file (an `fstat` of a
430    /// descriptor kept past a reap reads its mtime), so no entry can be
431    /// retired exactly. The table holds one entry per per-process inode whose
432    /// owner set a time or a hint, and an inode is a spelling's identity
433    /// (`procfs_inode::per_process_inode`): for a thread group of N threads,
434    /// up to `(N + N²) × PER_PROCESS_NAMES.len()` inodes per group of task
435    /// generations (N process spellings, N² `/proc/<n>/task/<m>` spellings,
436    /// `procfs::per_process_path`), and only those the guest wrote.
437    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#4213): Review the per-inode mtime and write-hint
438    // state Detcore keeps for its rendered per-process files, in the global
439    // tool, changed in the changing thread's turn.
440    fn rendered_file_state(
441        &mut self,
442        inode: u64,
443        change: crate::procfs::listing::RenderedFileChange,
444    ) -> crate::procfs::listing::RenderedFileState {
445        use crate::procfs::listing::RenderedFileChange;
446        let state = match change {
447            RenderedFileChange::Read => {
448                return self
449                    .rendered_file_states
450                    .get(&inode)
451                    .copied()
452                    .unwrap_or_default();
453            }
454            _ => self.rendered_file_states.entry(inode).or_default(),
455        };
456        match change {
457            RenderedFileChange::Read => {}
458            RenderedFileChange::Mtime(seconds, nanoseconds) => {
459                state.mtime = Some((seconds, nanoseconds));
460            }
461            RenderedFileChange::WriteHint(hint) => state.write_hint = hint,
462        }
463        *state
464    }
465
466    /// The key to pool the procfs entry at host inode `host` under, given the
467    /// key of the path it was reached by (see [`Self::procfs_path_key`]).
468    ///
469    /// Linux numbers per-process procfs entries when it builds their
470    /// dentries, and builds an evicted one again under a new host inode
471    /// (see `procfs_inode`). A host inode the pool has seen keeps its key,
472    /// so aliases (`/proc/<pid>/net/tcp` and `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/net/tcp`
473    /// are one inode) and sightings without a path agree. A host inode the
474    /// pool has not seen, reached by a path that already named an entry, is
475    /// that entry rebuilt: it takes the entry's key, and with it its number
476    /// and virtual mtime. Consumes no counter value.
477    fn procfs_key(&mut self, host: RawInode, path: RawInode) -> RawInode {
478        let key = match self.procfs_keys.get(&host) {
479            Some(key) => *key,
480            None if self.inodes.contains_key(&host)
481                || self.retired.contains_key(&host)
482                || self.retired_unnumbered.contains_key(&host) =>
483            {
484                host
485            }
486            None => self.procfs_keys.get(&path).copied().unwrap_or(host),
487        };
488        self.procfs_keys.insert(host, key);
489        self.procfs_keys.insert(path, key);
490        // A write through a descriptor nothing had registered left its mtime
491        // under the host inode.
492        if key != host
493            && let Some(mtime) = self.pending_mtimes.remove(&host)
494        {
495            self.set_mtime(key, mtime);
496        }
497        key
498    }
499
500    /// The key `raw_inode` is pooled under: its procfs key if it has one
501    /// (see [`Self::procfs_key`]), otherwise itself.
502    fn key(&self, raw_inode: RawInode) -> RawInode {
503        self.procfs_keys
504            .get(&raw_inode)
505            .copied()
506            .unwrap_or(raw_inode)
507    }
508
509    /// Counts a new guest thread with thread ID `tid`. A process or thread
510    /// ID the kernel gives out again names a new task, and Linux drops the
511    /// old task's procfs entries when it exits, so the new task's entries
512    /// are new files (see [`Self::procfs_path_key`]).
513    fn count_incarnation(&mut self, tid: i32) {
514        self.threads_counted += 1;
515        self.incarnations
516            .entry(tid)
517            .or_default()
518            .push(self.threads_counted);
519    }
520
521    /// The path key of the procfs entry `name`: the key of its path, salted
522    /// with the incarnation of each task the path names (see
523    /// [`Self::count_incarnation`]), so that an entry of a task whose ID was
524    /// reused does not adopt the number of the old task's entry, which a
525    /// descriptor may still hold. An entry of a directory snapshot names the
526    /// incarnation that held the ID when the snapshot was taken.
527    fn procfs_path_key(&self, name: &ProcfsName) -> RawInode {
528        name.tasks.iter().fold(name.path, |key, task| {
529            let counted = self.incarnations.get(task).map_or(&[][..], Vec::as_slice);
530            let incarnation = match name.threads_counted {
531                Some(snapshot) => counted.partition_point(|at| *at <= snapshot),
532                None => counted.len(),
533            };
534            match u32::try_from(incarnation).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) {
535                0 => key,
536                incarnation => procfs_inode::with_incarnation(key, *task, incarnation),
537            }
538        })
539    }
540
541    // Allocate the next deterministic inode.  This takes the raw-inode and
542    // can return an existing mapping or extend the mapping by creating a
543    // new deterministic inode. Minted numbers are strictly increasing and
544    // never handed out twice.
545    //
546    // Host inode reuse: a filesystem such as ext4 or XFS gives a freed
547    // `(dev, ino)` to a new file, and whether it does differs between runs
548    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3840). A file's mapping, or
549    // its pending mtime if nothing numbered it yet, is retired when the guest
550    // removes its last name (`Self::retire`). A `Name` sighting of a retired
551    // `(dev, ino)` discards it, so the new file is numbered by this request
552    // in every run, reused or not, and inherits no mtime. A `Descriptor`
553    // sighting still gets the retired number: an unlinked file reached through
554    // a descriptor keeps its inode number, as on Linux, and a descriptor to a
555    // new file was opened by name, which discarded the retired mapping
556    // (`Self::forget_retired`).
557    //
558    // Still only contained, not handled: a file that never had a name
559    // (`O_TMPFILE`, never linked) is never retired, nor is a file that
560    // disappears without the guest removing its name (another process
561    // deletes it, or its filesystem is unmounted). A named file the host
562    // gives such a file's freed inode inherits its number and mtime.
563    //
564    // Every call consumes the next counter value, whether or not it mints.
565    // Whether a host inode is "new" depends on host state the guest does not
566    // control (a file replaced by another process, an inode the filesystem
567    // reused, a hard link), while the sequence of requests is the guest's
568    // own. Counting only mints let one such host-dependent sighting shift the
569    // number of every file minted after it, on every device
570    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2897); counting requests
571    // confines the difference to the file whose host identity differed.
572    // Numbers stay unique and increasing, just not dense.
573    //
574    // Also return the virtual mtime. When it is still unresolved, `observed`
575    // resolves it under the first-seen policy (see `ObservedMtime`); an
576    // unresolved mtime reads as `epoch`.
577    fn add_sighted_inode(
578        &mut self,
579        raw_inode: RawInode,
580        observed: ObservedMtime,
581        epoch: LogicalTime,
582        sighting: InodeSighting,
583    ) -> (DetInode, LogicalTime) {
584        let raw_inode = self.key(raw_inode);
585        let ordinal = self.next_inode;
586        self.next_inode += 1;
587        match sighting {
588            InodeSighting::Name => self.forget_retired(raw_inode),
589            InodeSighting::Listed(snapshot) => {
590                if let Some(answer) = self.listed_generation(raw_inode, snapshot, ordinal) {
591                    let mtime = self
592                        .detinodes_info
593                        .get_mut(&answer)
594                        .expect("Internal invariant broken, det_ino missing entry");
595                    if mtime.mtime.is_none() {
596                        mtime.mtime = observed.first_seen_mtime(epoch);
597                    }
598                    return (answer, mtime.mtime.unwrap_or(epoch));
599                }
600                if self
601                    .retired_at
602                    .get(&raw_inode)
603                    .is_some_and(|retired| *retired < snapshot)
604                {
605                    self.forget_retired(raw_inode);
606                }
607            }
608            InodeSighting::Descriptor => {}
609        }
610        let dino = match self
611            .inodes
612            .get(&raw_inode)
613            .or_else(|| self.retired.get(&raw_inode))
614        {
615            Some(dino) => *dino,
616            None => {
617                // THE determinization boundary: the single place a host inode
618                // is deliberately mapped to a deterministic one. The value is
619                // minted from a monotonic counter, never derived from the host
620                // inode's bits.
621                let new = DetInode::mint(ordinal);
622                // A file whose last name went away before it was numbered,
623                // reached through a descriptor, is numbered as retired.
624                let mtime = match self.retired_unnumbered.remove(&raw_inode) {
625                    Some(mtime) => {
626                        self.retired.insert(raw_inode, new);
627                        if let Some(last) = self
628                            .generations
629                            .get_mut(&raw_inode)
630                            .and_then(|generations| generations.last_mut())
631                        {
632                            last.number = Some(new);
633                        }
634                        mtime
635                    }
636                    None => {
637                        assert!(self.inodes.insert(raw_inode, new).is_none());
638                        self.generations
639                            .entry(raw_inode)
640                            .or_default()
641                            .push(Generation {
642                                number: Some(new),
643                                retired: None,
644                                pending: None,
645                            });
646                        self.pending_mtimes.remove(&raw_inode)
647                    }
648                };
649                let prev = self.detinodes_info.insert(new, DetInodeInfo { mtime });
650                assert!(prev.is_none()); // Should not have been previously used.
651                new
652            }
653        };
654        let info = self
655            .detinodes_info
656            .get_mut(&dino)
657            .expect("Internal invariant broken, det_ino missing entry");
658        if info.mtime.is_none() {
659            info.mtime = observed.first_seen_mtime(epoch);
660        }
661        (dino, info.mtime.unwrap_or(epoch))
662    }
663
664    /// [`Self::add_sighted_inode`] for a [`InodeSighting::Descriptor`].
665    fn add_inode(
666        &mut self,
667        raw_inode: RawInode,
668        observed: ObservedMtime,
669        epoch: LogicalTime,
670    ) -> (DetInode, LogicalTime) {
671        self.add_sighted_inode(raw_inode, observed, epoch, InodeSighting::Descriptor)
672    }
673
674    // Set a file's virtual mtime, replacing whatever the first-seen policy
675    // chose or would choose. This never consumes a counter value: its callers
676    // (a write's mtime bump, `utimensat`) reach the pool or not depending on
677    // host state, such as whether the target's host identity held still
678    // during the call, and a request counted here would shift the number of
679    // every file numbered after it. A file not yet numbered keeps the mtime
680    // pending until its first numbering request.
681    fn set_mtime(&mut self, raw_inode: RawInode, mtime: LogicalTime) {
682        let raw_inode = self.key(raw_inode);
683        // A retired file is written through a descriptor opened before its
684        // last name went away; a new file's descriptor was opened by name,
685        // which discarded the retired mapping.
686        match self
687            .inodes
688            .get(&raw_inode)
689            .or_else(|| self.retired.get(&raw_inode))
690        {
691            Some(dino) => {
692                self.detinodes_info
693                    .get_mut(dino)
694                    // TODO(T87258449): remove this `expect`:
695                    .expect("Invariant violation: det inode missing from map.")
696                    .mtime = Some(mtime);
697            }
698            None => match self.retired_unnumbered.get_mut(&raw_inode) {
699                Some(retired) => {
700                    *retired = Some(mtime);
701                    // Also in its history record, which a directory snapshot
702                    // consults once the host has reused the inode (claude
703                    // re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849).
704                    if let Some(last) = self
705                        .generations
706                        .get_mut(&raw_inode)
707                        .and_then(|generations| generations.last_mut())
708                    {
709                        last.pending = Some(mtime);
710                    }
711                }
712                None => {
713                    self.pending_mtimes.insert(raw_inode, mtime);
714                }
715            },
716        }
717    }
718
719    /// The file behind `raw_inode` lost its last name (an `unlink`,
720    /// `rmdir` or replacing `rename` removed it). Its number stays for the
721    /// descriptors that can still reach it, but a later [`InodeSighting::Name`]
722    /// of `raw_inode` is another file. Consumes no counter value: whether a
723    /// removal reaches here follows host state (its `st_nlink`), and must not
724    /// shift other files' numbers.
725    fn retire(&mut self, raw_inode: RawInode) {
726        let raw_inode = self.key(raw_inode);
727        let stamp = self.retirements;
728        self.retired_at.insert(raw_inode, stamp);
729        self.retirements += 1;
730        let generations = self.generations.entry(raw_inode).or_default();
731        match self.inodes.remove(&raw_inode) {
732            Some(dino) => {
733                self.retired.insert(raw_inode, dino);
734                match generations.last_mut() {
735                    Some(last) if last.number == Some(dino) && last.retired.is_none() => {
736                        last.retired = Some(stamp);
737                    }
738                    _ => generations.push(Generation {
739                        number: Some(dino),
740                        retired: Some(stamp),
741                        pending: None,
742                    }),
743                }
744            }
745            // Nothing numbered it yet, but a write may have left a pending
746            // mtime, which must stay with this file (claude review of
747            // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849, P2-2).
748            None => {
749                let pending = self.pending_mtimes.remove(&raw_inode);
750                self.retired_unnumbered.insert(raw_inode, pending);
751                generations.push(Generation {
752                    number: None,
753                    retired: Some(stamp),
754                    pending,
755                });
756            }
757        }
758    }
759
760    /// The number of the file that held `raw_inode` when a directory snapshot
761    /// was taken after `snapshot` retirements, if that file has since lost its
762    /// last name. A file that held it then and was never numbered is numbered
763    /// now, as `ordinal`. `None` when the inode's holder at the snapshot still
764    /// holds it, or nothing ever retired one of its holders, so that the
765    /// current file answers.
766    ///
767    /// A file held the inode from just after the previous holder's retirement
768    /// (the host cannot reuse an inode before it is freed) through its own:
769    /// the retirement with stamp `r` happened when the count was `r`, so a
770    /// snapshot that saw it still named has `snapshot <= r`.
771    fn listed_generation(
772        &mut self,
773        raw_inode: RawInode,
774        snapshot: u64,
775        ordinal: u64,
776    ) -> Option<DetInode> {
777        let generations = self.generations.get_mut(&raw_inode)?;
778        // Holders are retired in order and the stamps only grow, and only the
779        // last can still hold the inode, so the stamps are sorted. A snapshot
780        // newer than the last retirement saw the current holder, the common
781        // case, answered without a search; an older one finds its holder by
782        // binary search: the first holder retired at or after the snapshot.
783        // The previous holder was retired before the snapshot, so this one
784        // held the inode then (codex re-check of
785        // <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849>: a scan from the
786        // oldest made churn on one inode quadratic).
787        let last_retired = match generations.last()?.retired {
788            Some(retired) => Some(retired),
789            None => generations.iter().rev().nth(1).and_then(|g| g.retired),
790        };
791        if last_retired.is_none_or(|retired| snapshot > retired) {
792            return None;
793        }
794        #[cfg(test)]
795        let mut probes = 0;
796        let index = generations.partition_point(|generation| {
797            #[cfg(test)]
798            {
799                probes += 1;
800            }
801            generation.retired.is_some_and(|retired| retired < snapshot)
802        });
803        #[cfg(test)]
804        {
805            self.listed_probes += probes;
806        }
807        // The holder at the snapshot still holds the inode: the current file
808        // answers.
809        generations.get(index)?.retired?;
810        let current = index + 1 == generations.len();
811        let generation = &mut generations[index];
812        if let Some(number) = generation.number {
813            return Some(number);
814        }
815        let new = DetInode::mint(ordinal);
816        generation.number = Some(new);
817        let mut mtime = generation.pending;
818        // The latest holder, still retired and reached first by this entry, is
819        // numbered as a descriptor would number it.
820        if current && let Some(pending) = self.retired_unnumbered.remove(&raw_inode) {
821            self.retired.insert(raw_inode, new);
822            mtime = pending;
823        }
824        let prev = self.detinodes_info.insert(new, DetInodeInfo { mtime });
825        assert!(prev.is_none()); // Should not have been previously used.
826        Some(new)
827    }
828
829    /// `raw_inode` names a file that has a name, or that was just created
830    /// (an `open` that found it linked, or `O_TMPFILE`), so a retired mapping
831    /// of it described a file the host has freed: discard it. Consumes no
832    /// counter value.
833    fn forget_retired(&mut self, raw_inode: RawInode) {
834        let raw_inode = self.key(raw_inode);
835        self.retired_at.remove(&raw_inode);
836        // Its number and mtime stay in `generations` and `detinodes_info` for
837        // directory snapshots taken while it held the inode.
838        if self.retired.remove(&raw_inode).is_some() {
839            self.reused += 1;
840        }
841        if self.retired_unnumbered.remove(&raw_inode).is_some() {
842            self.reused += 1;
843        }
844    }
845}
846
847// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
848// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1056): Deterministic remapping of device numbers (st_dev).
849/// Deterministic remapping of device numbers (`st_dev`).
850///
851/// The kernel assigns anonymous block-device numbers to filesystems without a
852/// backing block device (procfs, sysfs, tmpfs, devpts) from a global,
853/// host-wide counter (`get_anon_bdev`). The raw `st_dev` a guest observes for
854/// such a filesystem therefore drifts between otherwise-identical runs — and
855/// even between the two runs of `--verify`, because the first run's mounts are
856/// still live when the second run mounts fresh copies, so the second run's
857/// procfs gets a different anonymous device number. That leaked host state into
858/// a guest-visible `stat`/`statx` field.
859///
860/// We replace each distinct raw device number with a strictly-increasing
861/// synthetic id assigned in first-observation order. Both `stat`/`statx` and a
862/// virtualized mountinfo snapshot use this pool. A mountinfo read intentionally
863/// pre-populates it in that snapshot's row order, and later metadata syscalls
864/// reuse those assignments.
865///
866/// This guarantees identity consistency within one Detcore run. It is not an
867/// unconditional cross-machine guarantee: hosts with different filesystem
868/// layouts can expose different device equivalence classes or first-observation
869/// order. The remapping still preserves distinctness and equality within the
870/// run, so `find -xdev`, `du -x`, and `(st_dev, st_ino)` checks behave
871/// consistently with the mountinfo device column.
872#[derive(Debug)]
873struct DevicePool {
874    devices: HashMap<u64, u64>,
875    next_device: u64,
876}
877
878/// Run-global guest-visible mount IDs, shared by `/proc/*/mountinfo` and
879/// `/proc/*/fdinfo/*`.
880///
881/// Linux gives pseudo filesystems such as pipefs, sockfs, anon_inodefs, nsfs,
882/// and pidfs their own mount IDs without listing those mounts in
883/// `/proc/*/mountinfo`. The raw numbers are host-assigned. Preserve equality
884/// and distinctness by keying on the raw mount ID, and number raw IDs in the
885/// order the guest first observes them: an fdinfo read assigns its one ID, and
886/// a mountinfo read assigns its not-yet-numbered row and parent IDs in row
887/// order. The namespace's row order is kept only to validate later views.
888///
889/// Numbering must not depend on mounts the guest never observed. A run's mount
890/// namespace starts as a copy of the host's, so its row count changes with
891/// unrelated host activity, such as another process's loop mount under a
892/// shared-propagation directory. Numbering by position in that table made the
893/// fdinfo `mnt_id` of a pipe or of `/dev/null`, neither of which mountinfo
894/// lists, differ between two runs of the same guest.
895#[derive(Debug)]
896enum MountIdPool {
897    Uninitialized,
898    Invalid,
899    Ready {
900        /// Raw mount ID to guest-visible mount ID, for every raw ID numbered
901        /// so far. `mount_ids[&assignment_order[i]] == i + 1`.
902        mount_ids: BTreeMap<u64, u64>,
903        /// Raw mount IDs in the order they were numbered.
904        assignment_order: Vec<u64>,
905        /// The namespace's raw row/parent order. Validation only.
906        mountinfo_order: Vec<u64>,
907        allow_visible_subsets: bool,
908    },
909}
910
911/// The raw identity orders observed by the producer and required to reconstruct
912/// the same guest-visible mount IDs during replay.
913pub struct MountIdentityProvenance {
914    /// The namespace's raw mountinfo row/parent order, which later mountinfo
915    /// views are validated against.
916    pub mountinfo_order: Vec<u64>,
917    /// Raw mount IDs in the order the run numbered them.
918    pub assignment_order: Vec<u64>,
919}
920
921impl MountIdPool {
922    fn from_config(mount_ids: &[u64], captured: bool, assignment_order: &[u64]) -> Self {
923        if !captured {
924            if !mount_ids.is_empty() || !assignment_order.is_empty() {
925                return Self::Invalid;
926            }
927            return Self::Uninitialized;
928        }
929        Self::from_orders(mount_ids, assignment_order, true).unwrap_or(Self::Invalid)
930    }
931
932    fn from_orders(
933        mount_ids: &[u64],
934        assignment_order: &[u64],
935        allow_visible_subsets: bool,
936    ) -> Option<Self> {
937        let mut seen_rows = BTreeSet::new();
938        if !mount_ids.iter().all(|raw| seen_rows.insert(*raw)) {
939            return None;
940        }
941        // A recorded assignment may include IDs mountinfo does not list, such
942        // as pipefs. It may include raw 0 only if the namespace order names 0
943        // as a row or parent: an fdinfo zero is the anonymous class and is
944        // never numbered, and a mountinfo zero must pass order validation.
945        if assignment_order.contains(&0) && !seen_rows.contains(&0) {
946            return None;
947        }
948        let mut mappings = BTreeMap::new();
949        for (index, raw) in assignment_order.iter().enumerate() {
950            let virtual_mount_id = u64::try_from(index).ok()?.checked_add(1)?;
951            if mappings.insert(*raw, virtual_mount_id).is_some() {
952                return None;
953            }
954        }
955        Some(Self::Ready {
956            mount_ids: mappings,
957            assignment_order: assignment_order.to_vec(),
958            mountinfo_order: mount_ids.to_vec(),
959            allow_visible_subsets,
960        })
961    }
962
963    fn validate_mountinfo_order(&mut self, mountinfo_order: &[u64]) -> bool {
964        if matches!(self, Self::Uninitialized) {
965            *self = Self::from_orders(mountinfo_order, &[], false).unwrap_or(Self::Invalid);
966        }
967        let Self::Ready {
968            mountinfo_order: expected,
969            allow_visible_subsets,
970            ..
971        } = self
972        else {
973            return false;
974        };
975        if *allow_visible_subsets {
976            mount_ids_are_ordered_subset(mountinfo_order, expected)
977        } else {
978            mountinfo_order == expected
979        }
980    }
981
982    /// Return the guest-visible ID for `raw_mount_id`, numbering it next if
983    /// this is its first observation. The pool must be `Ready`.
984    fn assign(&mut self, raw_mount_id: u64) -> Option<u64> {
985        let Self::Ready {
986            mount_ids,
987            assignment_order,
988            ..
989        } = self
990        else {
991            return None;
992        };
993        if let Some(virtual_mount_id) = mount_ids.get(&raw_mount_id) {
994            return Some(*virtual_mount_id);
995        }
996        let virtual_mount_id = u64::try_from(assignment_order.len()).ok()?.checked_add(1)?;
997        mount_ids.insert(raw_mount_id, virtual_mount_id);
998        assignment_order.push(raw_mount_id);
999        Some(virtual_mount_id)
1000    }
1001
1002    fn determinize(&mut self, raw_mount_id: u64, mountinfo_order: Option<&[u64]>) -> Option<u64> {
1003        // Linux uses zero for anonymous objects such as memfd. It is one
1004        // equivalence class regardless of Detcore's descriptor classification.
1005        if raw_mount_id == 0 {
1006            return Some(0);
1007        }
1008        if let Some(order) = mountinfo_order {
1009            if !self.validate_mountinfo_order(order) {
1010                return None;
1011            }
1012        } else if matches!(self, Self::Uninitialized) {
1013            return None;
1014        }
1015        self.assign(raw_mount_id)
1016    }
1017
1018    /// Validate one mountinfo snapshot and return the guest-visible ID of each
1019    /// entry of `observation_order`, numbering unseen entries in that order.
1020    ///
1021    /// `mountinfo_order` is the snapshot's canonical order, checked against
1022    /// the namespace order. `observation_order` is the same set of raw IDs in
1023    /// the order the view presents them (rows, then parent-only IDs). Only it
1024    /// decides numbering, so a captured namespace order that the guest cannot
1025    /// see never changes a guest-visible number.
1026    fn resolve_mountinfo(
1027        &mut self,
1028        mountinfo_order: &[u64],
1029        observation_order: &[u64],
1030    ) -> Option<Vec<u64>> {
1031        let entries = mountinfo_order.iter().copied().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
1032        let mut observed = BTreeSet::new();
1033        if entries.len() != mountinfo_order.len()
1034            || observation_order.len() != mountinfo_order.len()
1035            || !observation_order
1036                .iter()
1037                .all(|raw| entries.contains(raw) && observed.insert(*raw))
1038        {
1039            return None;
1040        }
1041        if !self.validate_mountinfo_order(mountinfo_order) {
1042            return None;
1043        }
1044        observation_order
1045            .iter()
1046            .map(|raw| self.assign(*raw))
1047            .collect()
1048    }
1049
1050    fn provenance(&self) -> Result<Option<MountIdentityProvenance>, &'static str> {
1051        match self {
1052            Self::Uninitialized => Ok(None),
1053            Self::Invalid => Err("mount identity provenance is invalid"),
1054            Self::Ready {
1055                mountinfo_order,
1056                assignment_order,
1057                ..
1058            } => Ok(Some(MountIdentityProvenance {
1059                mountinfo_order: mountinfo_order.clone(),
1060                assignment_order: assignment_order.clone(),
1061            })),
1062        }
1063    }
1064}
1065
1066impl Default for DevicePool {
1067    fn default() -> Self {
1068        DevicePool::new()
1069    }
1070}
1071
1072impl DevicePool {
1073    fn new() -> Self {
1074        // Start at 1 so no file reports st_dev == 0, which some tools treat as
1075        // "no device".
1076        DevicePool {
1077            devices: HashMap::new(),
1078            next_device: 1,
1079        }
1080    }
1081
1082    /// The pool of a run whose guest mount namespace is this process's: its
1083    /// procfs device reports Detcore's procfs device, as the procfs files
1084    /// Detcore renders do (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213>).
1085    /// Outside record and replay, the process holding the global state is in
1086    /// the guest's mount namespace on every backend. Replay's tracer is not,
1087    /// and its devices are the recording's, so record and replay number
1088    /// devices as before ([`Self::new`]).
1089    fn for_this_mount_namespace() -> Self {
1090        let mut pool = Self::new();
1091        match std::fs::metadata("/proc") {
1092            Ok(proc) => {
1093                pool.devices.insert(
1094                    std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt::dev(&proc),
1095                    procfs_inode::VIRTUAL_PROC_DEVICE,
1096                );
1097            }
1098            Err(error) => warn!(
1099                "[detcore] /proc could not be read, so its device is numbered when first seen: {error}"
1100            ),
1101        }
1102        pool
1103    }
1104
1105    /// Return the deterministic device id for `raw_device`, allocating a new one
1106    /// (in first-observation order) the first time a raw device is seen. The
1107    /// procfs device is never allocated to another device.
1108    fn determinize(&mut self, raw_device: u64) -> u64 {
1109        match self.devices.get(&raw_device) {
1110            Some(dev) => *dev,
1111            None => {
1112                if self.next_device == procfs_inode::VIRTUAL_PROC_DEVICE {
1113                    self.next_device += 1;
1114                }
1115                let new = self.next_device;
1116                self.next_device += 1;
1117                self.devices.insert(raw_device, new);
1118                new
1119            }
1120        }
1121    }
1122}
1123
1124/// Global state associated with the detcore tool.
1125///
1126/// This is a singleton, and the one object of this type lives inside a central
1127/// address space, generally the "tracer" in a Reverie backend.
1128#[derive(Debug)]
1129pub struct GlobalState {
1130    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
1131
1132    inodes: Arc<Mutex<InodePool>>,
1133
1134    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1135    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1056): Deterministic st_dev remapping state.
1136    devices: Arc<Mutex<DevicePool>>,
1137
1138    /// Shared fdinfo mount-ID equivalence classes for this Detcore run.
1139    mount_ids: Mutex<MountIdPool>,
1140
1141    // next port to use if input port is 0
1142    next_port: AtomicU16,
1143
1144    // used ports
1145    used_ports: Mutex<HashSet<u16>>,
1146
1147    // Unsupported syscall names observed across every process in this run.
1148    unsupported_syscalls: Mutex<BTreeSet<String>>,
1149
1150    // Why the fail-closed policy ended the run, from the Tool image that
1151    // refused (`GlobalRequest::PolicyRefusal`); the first report is kept.
1152    policy_refusal: Mutex<Option<String>>,
1153
1154    // The host identity of each file the guest opened in this run, in the
1155    // order the opens were reported, when `Config::record_host_inputs` is set
1156    // (see `detcore_model::host_input`). Written to `Config::host_input_log`
1157    // when the run ends normally; dropped with this state otherwise.
1158    host_inputs: Mutex<Vec<HostInputRecord>>,
1159
1160    // The paths the guest itself rebound in its file namespace in this run,
1161    // when `Config::record_host_inputs` is set (see
1162    // `detcore_model::host_input::HostMutationRecord`). Written beside
1163    // `host_inputs`.
1164    host_mutations: Mutex<BTreeSet<String>>,
1165
1166    // The canonical models of open file descriptions that several guest
1167    // processes share (see `crate::shared_open_files`). Locked after `sched`,
1168    // never before it.
1169    shared_open_files: Arc<Mutex<SharedOpenFileStore>>,
1170
1171    // Optional append-only sink shared by DBT fork descendants.
1172    unsupported_syscall_report_fd: Option<Mutex<File>>,
1173
1174    // Open file description to bound port.
1175    open_file_to_port: Mutex<HashMap<OpenFileId, u16>>,
1176
1177    port_start_range: AtomicU16,
1178    port_end_range: AtomicU16,
1179
1180    // False initially after fork, and true when we begin executing the guest binary.
1181    past_first_execve: AtomicBool,
1182    /// Unlike the logging flag above, this changes only at successful image completion.
1183    initial_descriptor_image_complete: AtomicBool,
1184    /// Actual controller input, held only until the registered root image
1185    /// consumes it. The lease keeps its raw identity live, not guest-visible.
1186    inherited_input: Mutex<Option<PendingInheritedInput>>,
1187
1188    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1189    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1154): Review the SaBRe exec descriptor-status handoff.
1190    /// Pre-exec identity and descriptor state awaiting a successful image transition.
1191    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1173): Review SaBRe exec incarnation fencing.
1192    pending_exec_states: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, PendingExecState>>>,
1193    // Installed only by the trusted watched native launcher, never by an RPC.
1194    native_exec_registry: OnceLock<Mutex<native_exec::NativeExecRegistry>>,
1195    /// Successful identity transfers whose RPC acknowledgment may still be in flight.
1196    /// Nesting either exec map with global_time requires holding sched first;
1197    /// the scheduler mutex serializes their inner lock orders. Process
1198    /// cleanup also holds sched before acquiring these stores.
1199    completed_exec_transfers: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, exec_identity::ExecTransferReceipt>>>,
1200
1201    /// Descriptor state retained after the one-shot scheduler transition is consumed.
1202    post_exec_fd_blocking: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetTid, ExecFdState>>>,
1203
1204    /// The image each guest process executes, as its last successful exec
1205    /// recorded and the kernel's link confirmed (`crate::exec_record`), for
1206    /// another process's `/proc/<pid>/exe`. A new process starts with its
1207    /// creator's; the record goes with the process.
1208    exec_images: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, crate::exec_record::ExecRecord>>>,
1209    /// The registered root thread, whose first image
1210    /// `Config::launch_image` names, and whether that image was completed.
1211    root_dettid: OnceLock<DetTid>,
1212    root_image_marked: AtomicBool,
1213    /// The device and inode of `Config::launch_image`'s launcher, read once.
1214    launcher_identity: OnceLock<Option<(u64, u64)>>,
1215
1216    sched_handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>,
1217
1218    /// Global time is a *volatile* vector clock of individual thread progress. Each
1219    /// thread can independently update its own progress, even (potentially) asynchronously.
1220    ///
1221    /// LockOrdering: this lock can be acquired while holding the sched lock (but not vice
1222    /// versa).
1223    //
1224    // TODO: it would be more future-proof to provide a non-blocking way to retrieve a
1225    // (nondeterministic) monotonic lower bound on global time.
1226    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
1227
1228    /// Just cache the config so we can access it from everywhere.
1229    cfg: Config,
1230
1231    /// Storage for the preemption record read from `replay_preemptions_from`.
1232    preemptions_to_replay: Option<PreemptionReader>,
1233
1234    /// The start is when we construct the global state.  Close enough.
1235    realtime_start: SystemTime,
1236
1237    /// External network record or replay state, present only when a network
1238    /// trace mode is configured. Every operation reads global time under this
1239    /// lock, so an input's release point is fixed by the schedule alone.
1240    network: Option<Mutex<NetworkEngine>>,
1241}
1242
1243/// The stores a process's physical exit must clean up, shared with the
1244/// GlobalState that owns them, so that the cleanup can run as one step under
1245/// the scheduler lock. Locked after `sched`, never before it, as every other
1246/// nested user of these stores does.
1247#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
1248struct ProcessExitCleanup {
1249    shared_open_files: Arc<Mutex<SharedOpenFileStore>>,
1250    pending_exec_states: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, PendingExecState>>>,
1251    completed_exec_transfers: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, exec_identity::ExecTransferReceipt>>>,
1252    post_exec_fd_blocking: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetTid, ExecFdState>>>,
1253    exec_images: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<DetPid, crate::exec_record::ExecRecord>>>,
1254}
1255
1256impl ProcessExitCleanup {
1257    /// Complete the exit `watch` observed, unless a later registration has
1258    /// replaced it. Nothing calls this in production yet; the daemon-point
1259    /// observation of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362> part 2
1260    /// will (2ee7190125's free-running observer was reverted).
1261    #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
1262    fn complete_observed_locked(
1263        &self,
1264        sched: &mut Scheduler,
1265        watch: &Arc<crate::scheduler::ProcessExitWatch>,
1266    ) -> Option<(bool, Option<String>)> {
1267        if !sched.process_exit_watch_is_current(watch) {
1268            return None;
1269        }
1270        sched.finish_process_exit_watch(watch);
1271        Some(self.complete_locked(sched, watch.process, true))
1272    }
1273
1274    fn complete_locked(
1275        &self,
1276        sched: &mut Scheduler,
1277        process: DetPid,
1278        consume_unreported: bool,
1279    ) -> (bool, Option<String>) {
1280        let loss = (consume_unreported && sched.has_unreported_exit(process)).then(|| {
1281            let reason = format!(
1282                "process {process} exited without deregistering; its exit was not scheduled"
1283            );
1284            // Publish refusal before cancellation can wake a request. Normal
1285            // deregistration and this entire operation share the sched lock.
1286            crate::detlog::record_determinism_loss(&reason);
1287            reason
1288        });
1289        self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().remove(&process);
1290        self.completed_exec_transfers
1291            .lock()
1292            .unwrap()
1293            .remove(&process);
1294        self.post_exec_fd_blocking.lock().unwrap().remove(&process);
1295        self.exec_images.lock().unwrap().remove(&process);
1296        if consume_unreported {
1297            let consumed = sched.consume_unreported_exit(process);
1298            debug_assert_eq!(consumed, loss.is_some());
1299        }
1300        self.shared_open_files
1301            .lock()
1302            .unwrap()
1303            .end_leases_of(process);
1304        (sched.complete_physical_process_exit(process), loss)
1305    }
1306}

1319        if let Some(message) =
1320            format_unsupported_syscall_warning(&self.unsupported_syscalls.lock().unwrap())

1327
1328impl GlobalState {
1329    /// Ordinary RPC mutation must linearize before terminal publication under
1330    /// the same mutex as scheduler grants. A losing callback stays pending for
1331    /// the backend's failure subscription to drop; no normal reply is invented.
1332    /// Consuming exit RPCs retain their existing validation/accounting path.
1333    async fn lock_rpc_scheduler(
1334        &self,
1335        consuming_cleanup: bool,
1336    ) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Scheduler> {
1337        std::future::poll_fn(|_| {
1338            let sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
1339            if !consuming_cleanup && sched.backend_failed() {
1340                Poll::Pending
1341            } else {
1342                Poll::Ready(sched)
1343            }
1344        })
1345        .await
1346    }
1347
1348    /// The deterministic numbers of the files whose last name the run removed
1349    /// while they were numbered and that no later name showed to be reused
1350    /// (see `InodePool::retire`), in increasing order. Diagnostic, for tests
1351    /// of the removal paths (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3840>).
1352    pub fn retired_inodes(&self) -> Vec<DetInode> {
1353        let mut retired: Vec<DetInode> = self
1354            .inodes
1355            .lock()
1356            .unwrap()
1357            .retired
1358            .values()
1359            .copied()
1360            .collect();
1361        retired.sort();
1362        retired
1363    }
1364
1365    /// How many retired inode numbers a later name or `open` showed the host
1366    /// had given to another file. Diagnostic, for tests that make a host reuse
1367    /// an inode (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3840>).
1368    pub fn reused_inode_count(&self) -> u64 {
1369        self.inodes.lock().unwrap().reused
1370    }
1371
1372    /// Return the producer-observed mount identity order after a run.
1373    ///
1374    /// The first vector is the exact mountinfo row/parent order. The second is
1375    /// the order in which the run numbered raw mount IDs.
1376    pub fn mount_identity_provenance(
1377        &self,
1378    ) -> Result<Option<MountIdentityProvenance>, &'static str> {
1379        self.mount_ids.lock().unwrap().provenance()

1381
1382    /// A global state with no scheduler task, for unit tests elsewhere in the
1383    /// crate that send RPCs to it directly.
1384    #[cfg(test)]
1385    pub(crate) fn for_tests(cfg: &Config) -> Self {
1386        Self::initialize(cfg, false)
1387    }
1388
1389    fn initialize(cfg: &Config, spawn_scheduler: bool) -> Self {
1390        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(cfg)));
1391        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(cfg)));
1392        let process_exit_cleanup = ProcessExitCleanup::default();
1393        let handle = if cfg.sequentialize_threads && spawn_scheduler {
1394            // Announce before spawning, not from inside the spawned task. The
1395            // task's first poll is unordered with respect to the rest of this
1396            // bootstrap, so emitting there raced the root thread's seeding
1397            // lines and produced a nondeterministic INFO stream. Emitting here
1398            // sequences it: `Scheduler::new`'s SCHEDRAND line above, then this,
1399            // then the root `ThreadState::new` seeding lines.
1400            info!("[scheduler] daemon task starting up, waiting for guest thread start..");
1401            Some(tokio::spawn(sched_loop(sched.clone(), global_time.clone())))
1402        } else {
1403            None
1404        };
1405
1406        let preemptions_to_replay: Option<PreemptionReader> = cfg
1407            .replay_preemptions_from
1408            .as_ref()
1409            .map(|path| PreemptionReader::new(path));
1410        let range = Self::read_port_range();
1411        let network = Self::network_engine(cfg).map(Mutex::new);
1412
1413        let unsupported_syscall_report_fd = cfg.unsupported_syscall_report_fd.and_then(|fd| {
1414            // This writer is internal controller state. In an in-process DBT
1415            // runtime it must not leak into the next guest image across exec
1416            // (hence F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC), and it must not perturb the descriptor
1417            // namespace the *current* guest observes. The backend places the
1418            // report fd itself high, out of the guest's working range (e.g. 199
1419            // for the DBT backend). Duplicating with a min hint of `fd` keeps
1420            // this private copy up in that same reserved band instead of
1421            // grabbing the lowest free descriptor (fd 3), which would shift
1422            // every fd the guest subsequently opens and diverge from the golden
1423            // ptrace reference (where this fd is unset and no dup happens).
1424            let duplicate = unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, fd) };
1425            if duplicate == -1 {
1426                warn!(
1427                    "failed to duplicate unsupported-syscall report fd {fd}: {}",
1428                    std::io::Error::last_os_error()
1429                );
1430                None
1431            } else {
1432                // SAFETY: dup returned a new owned descriptor.
1433                Some(Mutex::new(unsafe { File::from_raw_fd(duplicate) }))
1434            }
1435        });
1436
1437        Self {
1438            sched,
1439            next_port: AtomicU16::new(range[0]),
1440            used_ports: Mutex::new(HashSet::new()),
1441            unsupported_syscalls: Mutex::new(BTreeSet::new()),
1442            policy_refusal: Mutex::new(None),
1443            host_inputs: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
1444            host_mutations: Mutex::new(BTreeSet::new()),
1445            shared_open_files: process_exit_cleanup.shared_open_files,
1446            unsupported_syscall_report_fd,
1447            port_start_range: AtomicU16::new(range[0]),
1448            port_end_range: AtomicU16::new(range[1]),
1449            open_file_to_port: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
1450            past_first_execve: AtomicBool::new(false),
1451            initial_descriptor_image_complete: AtomicBool::new(false),
1452            inherited_input: Mutex::new(None),
1453            pending_exec_states: process_exit_cleanup.pending_exec_states,
1454            completed_exec_transfers: process_exit_cleanup.completed_exec_transfers,
1455            post_exec_fd_blocking: process_exit_cleanup.post_exec_fd_blocking,
1456            exec_images: process_exit_cleanup.exec_images,
1457            root_dettid: OnceLock::new(),
1458            root_image_marked: AtomicBool::new(false),
1459            launcher_identity: OnceLock::new(),
1460            native_exec_registry: OnceLock::new(),
1461            inodes: Arc::new(Mutex::new(InodePool::new())),
1462            // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1463            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1056): Deterministic st_dev remapping state.
1464            devices: Arc::new(Mutex::new(if cfg.recordreplay_modes {
1465                DevicePool::new()
1466            } else {
1467                DevicePool::for_this_mount_namespace()
1468            })),
1469            mount_ids: Mutex::new(MountIdPool::from_config(
1470                &cfg.mountinfo_mount_ids,
1471                cfg.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured,
1472                &cfg.mount_id_assignment_order,
1473            )),
1474            sched_handle: handle,
1475            cfg: cfg.clone(),
1476            realtime_start: SystemTime::now(),
1477            global_time,
1478            preemptions_to_replay,
1479            network,
1480        }
1481    }
1482
1483    /// The network engine for the configured trace mode. The CLI validates a
1484    /// replay trace before launch; failing here is a backstop.
1485    fn network_engine(cfg: &Config) -> Option<NetworkEngine> {
1486        let path = cfg.network_trace.path.as_ref();
1487        match cfg.network_trace.mode {
1488            NetworkTraceMode::Off => None,
1489            NetworkTraceMode::Record => Some(NetworkEngine::new_record(cfg.epoch)),
1490            NetworkTraceMode::Replay => {
1491                let path = path.expect("network trace replay requires a trace path");
1492                let trace = File::open(path)
1493                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
1494                    .and_then(|mut file| {
1495                        NetworkTraceV2::read_framed(&mut file).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
1496                    })
1497                    .unwrap_or_else(|error| {
1498                        panic!("cannot read network trace {}: {error}", path.display())
1499                    });
1500                Some(NetworkEngine::new_replay(trace))
1501            }
1502        }
1503    }
1504
1505    /// Write the network trace of a record run, or check that a replay used
1506    /// the whole recording. Returns the refusal a replay ends with.
1507    fn finish_network_trace(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
1508        let engine = self.network.take()?;
1509        let engine = engine.into_inner().unwrap();
1510        if !engine.is_record() {
1511            return engine
1512                .finish_replay()
1513                .err()
1514                .map(|error| format!("hermit: {error}. {}", error.remedy()));
1515        }
1516        let path = self
1517            .cfg
1518            .network_trace
1519            .path
1520            .as_ref()
1521            .expect("network trace recording requires a trace path");
1522        // Encode before opening the output, so a trace that cannot be encoded
1523        // leaves the file as it was instead of truncated.
1524        let result = engine
1525            .finish()
1526            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
1527            .and_then(|trace| trace.encode_framed().map_err(|error| error.to_string()))
1528            .and_then(|bytes| {
1529                let mut file = File::create(path).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
1530                file.write_all(&bytes).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
1531            });
1532        if let Err(error) = result {
1533            panic!("cannot write network trace {}: {error}", path.display());
1534        }
1535        None
1536    }
1537
1538    /// Initializes global state whose sequential scheduler is driven by an
1539    /// external backend executor.
1540    pub fn init_for_external_scheduler(cfg: &Config) -> Self {
1541        assert!(
1542            cfg.sequentialize_threads,
1543            "an external scheduler is only meaningful when threads are sequentialized"
1544        );
1545        Self::initialize(cfg, false)
1546    }
1547
1548    /// Returns the sequential scheduler loop for a backend-owned executor to run.
1549    ///
1550    /// This is deliberately not an `async fn`: the announcement is logged when
1551    /// this is called, not when the returned future is first polled. A backend
1552    /// can then order it ahead of anything it releases before polling (DBT
1553    /// publishes `READY_IMAGE`, which lets the root guest thread log its
1554    /// seeding lines). See <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3463>.
1555    pub fn run_external_scheduler(
1556        &self,
1557        observer: Arc<dyn Fn(&'static str) + Send + Sync>,
1558    ) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + use<> {
1559        // Emitted at the call site for the same reason as the spawned path in
1560        // `initialize`, so both ways of starting the daemon place this line at
1561        // a deterministic point in the caller's program order.
1562        info!("[scheduler] daemon task starting up, waiting for guest thread start..");
1563        sched_loop_external(self.sched.clone(), self.global_time.clone(), observer)
1564    }
1565
1566    /// Reports that a backend supervisor received a process's final kernel exit status.
1567    ///
1568    /// This records a barrier observation when the backend advertises physical-exit
1569    /// reporting or asynchronous exit completion; it is a no-op for ptrace, DBT and KVM.
1570    /// The exact process's barrier is released at this physical-waitability boundary.
1571    ///
1572    /// With asynchronous exit completion, registrations the process did not deregister
1573    /// itself are retired here first, in the same locked step, and a determinism loss is
1574    /// recorded: such a process died without finishing its exit hook, at a moment the host
1575    /// chose, so the run must not be compared.
1576    pub fn complete_physical_process_exit(&self, raw_pid: i32) {
1577        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(raw_pid);
1578        let (completed, loss) = {
1579            let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
1580            self.process_exit_cleanup().complete_locked(
1581                &mut sched,
1582                detpid,
1583                self.cfg.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously,
1584            )
1585        };
1586        if completed {
1587            trace!(
1588                "[detcore, dpid {}] backend completed final physical process exit",
1589                detpid
1590            );
1591        }
1592        if let Some(loss) = loss {
1593            crate::detlog::write_loss_notice(&loss);
1594        }
1595    }
1596
1597    fn process_exit_cleanup(&self) -> ProcessExitCleanup {
1598        ProcessExitCleanup {
1599            shared_open_files: self.shared_open_files.clone(),
1600            pending_exec_states: self.pending_exec_states.clone(),
1601            completed_exec_transfers: self.completed_exec_transfers.clone(),
1602            post_exec_fd_blocking: self.post_exec_fd_blocking.clone(),
1603            exec_images: self.exec_images.clone(),
1604        }
1605    }
1606
1607    /// The device and inode of the launcher `Config::launch_image` names,
1608    /// the file the kernel's `exe` link names in a launched guest's place.
1609    fn launcher_identity(&self) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
1610        *self.launcher_identity.get_or_init(|| {
1611            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
1612            let launcher = self.cfg.launch_image.as_ref()?.launcher.as_ref()?;
1613            let meta = std::fs::metadata(launcher).ok()?;
1614            Some((meta.dev(), meta.ino()))
1615        })
1616    }
1617
1618    /// Answers a control message about a shared open file description. Only
1619    /// the thread that holds the scheduler's serial grant may send one, so
1620    /// access to a shared description is exclusive and happens in canonical
1621    /// order (`crate::shared_open_files`).
1622    ///
1623    /// A refusal is an infrastructure failure, not something the guest's
1624    /// syscall can report: the caller's process stops, and this reports a
1625    /// backend failure, which ends the whole run before any further grant.
1626    fn shared_open_file_control(
1627        &self,
1628        thread: DetTid,
1629        control: OpenFileControl,
1630    ) -> Result<OpenFileControlReply, SharedOpenFileError> {
1631        // The refusal and the failure it reports are one locked step, so the
1632        // scheduler can grant no other thread in between.
1633        let (result, wakes) = {
1634            let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
1635            let process = sched.registered_process(thread);
1636            let result = if !sched.holds_serial_grant(thread) {
1637                Err(SharedOpenFileError(format!(
1638                    "thread {thread} sent {control:?} without holding the serial grant"
1639                )))
1640            } else if let Some(process) = process {
1641                self.shared_open_files
1642                    .lock()
1643                    .unwrap()
1644                    .handle(process, thread, control)
1645            } else {
1646                Err(SharedOpenFileError(format!(
1647                    "thread {thread} belongs to no registered process"
1648                )))
1649            };
1650            let wakes = result.as_ref().err().map(|error| {
1651                tracing::error!("[detcore] shared open file control refused: {error}");
1652                let wake = sched.report_backend_failure(reverie::BackendFailure {
1653                    pid: reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.unwrap_or(thread).as_raw()),
1654                    tid: Tid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
1655                    phase: "shared open file control",
1656                });
1657                (wake, sched.take_signal_failure_wakes())
1658            });
1659            (result, wakes)
1660        };
1661        // Notified after the lock is released, as `report_backend_failure`
1662        // does.
1663        if let Some((wake, deferred)) = wakes {
1664            for wake in deferred {
1665                let _ = wake.send(());
1666            }
1667            if let Some(wake) = wake {
1668                let _ = wake.send(());
1669            }
1670        }
1671        result
1672    }
1673
1674    /// Releases all physical-process-exit barriers after a backend supervisor has drained every
1675    /// tracee and no guest thread can race another lifecycle event.
1676    pub fn release_all_physical_process_exits(&self) {
1677        self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().clear();
1678        self.completed_exec_transfers.lock().unwrap().clear();
1679        self.post_exec_fd_blocking.lock().unwrap().clear();
1680        self.exec_images.lock().unwrap().clear();
1681        let released = self
1682            .sched
1683            .lock()
1684            .unwrap()
1685            .release_all_physical_process_exits();
1686        if released != 0 {
1687            trace!("released {released} final physical process-exit barrier(s)");
1688        }
1689    }
1690
1691    /// Why the fail-closed policy ended the run, when a Tool image reported
1692    /// it before exiting (`GlobalRequest::PolicyRefusal`).
1693    pub fn policy_refusal(&self) -> Option<String> {
1694        self.policy_refusal.lock().unwrap().clone()
1695    }
