1697    /// Unrecoverable fatal erorr. Bring things to a close cleanly, but as quickly as
1698    /// possible.
1699    pub fn force_shutdown_with_error(&self) {
1700        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
1701        let sched = loop {
1702            if start.elapsed().as_millis() > 1000 {
1703                eprintln!(
1704                    "Could not acquire scheduler lock during forced shutdown (timeout)... proceeding anyway."
1705                );
1706                return;
1707            }
1708            match self.sched.try_lock() {
1709                Ok(guard) => {
1710                    break guard;
1711                }
1712                Err(std::sync::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => {
1713                    std::thread::yield_now();
1714                    continue;
1715                }
1716                Err(e) => {
1717                    eprintln!(
1718                        "Could not acquire scheduler lock during forced shutdown ({})... proceeding anyway.",
1719                        e
1720                    );
1721                    return;
1722                }
1723            }
1724        };
1725        info!("Scheduler state at exit:\n{}", sched.full_summary());
1726    }
1727
1728    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1729    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-744): Review explicit abnormal-backend scheduler cancellation.
1730    /// Cancels the internally spawned scheduler task after a backend guest exits abnormally.
1731    ///
1732    /// External-scheduler states do not own a task and are left unchanged.
1733    pub async fn cancel_internal_scheduler(&mut self) {
1734        if let Some(handle) = self.sched_handle.take() {
1735            handle.abort();
1736            match handle.await {
1737                Ok(()) => {}
1738                Err(error) if error.is_cancelled() => {}
1739                Err(error) => panic!("cancelled scheduler task panicked: {error}"),
1740            }
1741        }
1742    }
1743
1744    /// Consume failed-run state after the scheduler has naturally finished.
1745    ///
1746    /// A failed run has no successful run summary. Preserve the scheduler's
1747    /// join error and any requested partial preemption recording's write error
1748    /// for the caller, without allowing either to replace the backend failure.
1749    pub async fn clean_up_after_backend_failure(mut self) -> BackendFailureCleanup {
1750        let scheduler = if let Some(handle) = self.sched_handle.take() {
1751            handle.await
1752        } else {
1753            Ok(())
1754        };
1755        // A scheduler panic can poison this mutex. Its JoinError is returned
1756        // below; recovering only to finish output must not replace that error.
1757        let writer = self
1758            .sched
1759            .lock()
1760            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
1761            .preemption_writer
1762            .take();
1763        let preemption_recording = if self.cfg.record_preemptions_to.is_some() {
1764            writer.map_or(Ok(()), |writer| writer.flush())
1765        } else {
1766            // The writer's destination is fixed from this same configuration.
1767            // In-memory-only recordings have no Drop write to finish.
1768            drop(writer);
1769            Ok(())
1770        };
1771        BackendFailureCleanup {
1772            scheduler,
1773            preemption_recording,
1774        }
1775    }
1776
1777    /// Shut down anything running, in particular wait on the scheduler.
1778    ///
1779    /// This is basically the destructor for the global state, but is here rather than in the
1780    /// Drop instance so that it can be async, and is more explicitly sequenced in the program.
1781    ///
1782    /// Print a summary of the execution, typically called when it is complete.
1783    ///
1784    /// If the boolean argument is true, print to stderr, otherwise only print the summary
1785    /// to the log.
1786    pub async fn clean_up(self, to_stderr: bool, print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>) {
1787        self.clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(to_stderr, print_summary_to_json_file, None)
1788            .await
1789    }
1790
1791    /// [`Self::clean_up`], also carrying the backend's dispatch record into the
1792    /// machine-readable summary. The human-readable report, including the INFO
1793    /// view `--verify` compares, never shows it.
1794    pub async fn clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(
1795        mut self,
1796        to_stderr: bool,
1797        print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
1798        dispatch_stats: Option<reverie::DispatchStats>,
1799    ) {
1800        if let Some(handle) = self.sched_handle.take() {
1801            debug!("Global state cleanup, confirming scheduler has shut down...");
1802            handle.await.expect("Global scheduler clean shutdown");
1803            debug!("Global state cleanup, continuing...");
1804        }
1805        let network_refusal = self.finish_network_trace();
1806        let banner =
1807            "  ------------------------------ hermit run report ------------------------------";
1808        let recording_destination = self.cfg.record_preemptions_to.clone();
1809        // The run is over: write what it opened for --verify.
1810        if let Some(log) = &self.cfg.host_input_log {
1811            crate::host_inputs::write(
1812                log,
1813                &self.host_inputs.lock().unwrap(),
1814                &self.host_mutations.lock().unwrap(),
1815            );
1816        }
1817        let (mut summary, info_reprio_descrip) = self.into_run_summary_for_log().unwrap();
1818        summary.dispatch_stats = dispatch_stats;
1819
1820        // Print machine-readable summary:
1821        if let Some(path) = print_summary_to_json_file {
1822            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&summary).unwrap();
1823            fs::write(path, json + "\n").unwrap();
1824        }
1825
1826        // Print human-readable summary:
1827        if to_stderr {
1828            // In this case, print summary irrespective of logging level.
1829            // TODO: output summary in machine-readable, JSON form.
1830            //
1831            // NOT `eprint!`: a guest that set O_NONBLOCK on the inherited fd 2
1832            // makes `write_all` fail with EAGAIN here, which panics the print
1833            // macro and loses both the summary and the panic message. See
1834            // `crate::util::RetryingStderr`.
1835            {
1836                use std::io::Write;
1837                let _ = write!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{}\n{}", banner, summary);
1838            }
1839        } else {
1840            // Separate out the nondeterministic bits and print them at debug level:
1841            let rt = summary.realtime_elapsed.take();
1842            log_run_summary(
1843                banner,
1844                &summary,
1845                info_reprio_descrip.as_deref(),
1846                recording_destination.as_deref(),
1847            );
1848            if let Some(x) = rt {
1849                debug!("Nondeterministic realtime elapsed: {:?}", x);
1850            }
1851        }
1852        // After the report, so a refused replay still describes the run.
1853        if let Some(refusal) = network_refusal {
1854            {
1855                use std::io::Write;
1856                let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
1857            }
1858            std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
1859        }
1860    }
1861
1862    #[cfg(test)]
1863    fn into_run_summary(self) -> anyhow::Result<RunSummary> {
1864        self.into_run_summary_for_log().map(|(summary, _)| summary)
1865    }
1866
1867    fn into_run_summary_for_log(self) -> anyhow::Result<(RunSummary, Option<String>)> {
1868        // First, the scheduler can generate part of the summary (and flush once).
1869        let (mut summary, info_reprio_descrip) = {
1870            let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
1871            sched.generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(self.cfg.record_preemptions_to.as_ref())?
1872        };
1873        // Second, we fill in the rest based on global state.
1874        // Record configuration and the runtime's timer mechanism, not whether
1875        // a timer is currently armed or has delivered an event. This metadata
1876        // stays separate from the INFO guest-behavior view.
1877        summary.preemption = Some(PreemptionSummary {
1878            max_timeslice_ns: self.cfg.max_timeslice.map(|maximum| maximum.get()),
1879            timer_enabled: Some(
1880                self.cfg.max_timeslice.is_some()
1881                    && self.cfg.backend.delivers_preemption_timer_events,
1882            ),
1883        });
1884        //
1885        // Real time report:
1886        // N.B.: We don't have a job-level exit hook atm (T76248597), so we use the
1887        // CURRENT time -- that we are calling summarize -- as the end time:
1888        summary.realtime_elapsed = Some(self.realtime_start.elapsed()?);
1889
1890        if self.cfg.virtualize_time {
1891            let final_time = self.global_time.lock().unwrap();
1892            summary.virttime_final = final_time.as_nanos().as_nanos();
1893            summary.virttime_elapsed = match final_time.elapsed_nanos() {
1894                Some(elapsed) => elapsed.as_nanos(),
1895                None => bail!(
1896                    "Internal invariant violated! Global time {} is before its epoch baseline",
1897                    final_time.as_nanos()
1898                ),
1899            };
1900        }
1901
1902        Ok((summary, info_reprio_descrip))
1903    }
1904}
1905
1906fn log_run_summary(
1907    banner: &str,
1908    summary: &RunSummary,
1909    info_reprio_descrip: Option<&str>,
1910    recording_destination: Option<&std::path::Path>,
1911) {
1912    info!("\n{}\n{}", banner, summary.info(info_reprio_descrip));
1913    debug!(
1914        replayed_events = summary.schedevent_replayed,
1915        ?recording_destination,
1916        "Run recording/replay bookkeeping"
1917    );
1918}
1919
1920#[reverie::global_tool]
1921impl GlobalTool for GlobalState {
1922    type Config = Config;
1923
1924    /// A request asks the scheduler to perform an RPC, which includes multiple kinds of
1925    /// actions, and, most importantly, permission to acquire resources and run the guest thread.
1926    ///
1927    /// Irrespective of which method we execute, we can "tick" our local component of the
1928    /// global time in the process.
1929    type Request = (DetTime, MmId, GlobalRequest);
1930
1931    /// Response from the global portion of the Detcore instrumentation tool.
1932    /// The exact form of the response depends on which method was executed.
1933    ///
1934    /// Irrespective of which method was called, the global handling may have consumed
1935    /// logical time, in which case the scheduler can send a new thread-local time back to
1936    /// the caller.  Unfortunately, information is lost as this is collapsed to a flat
1937    /// scalar instead of a rich `DetTime`.
1938    type Response = (Option<LogicalTime>, GlobalResponse);
1939
1940    /// Called once during startup.
1941    async fn init_global_state(cfg: &Config) -> GlobalState {
1942        // A backend whose guest thread IDs are not host tasks never reads a
1943        // host task's `/proc` signal state for them (`read_kernel_signal_state`).
1944        crate::syscalls::refuse_host_signal_state_reads(&cfg.backend);
1945        GlobalState::initialize(cfg, true)
1946    }
1947
1948    fn install_inherited_input(&mut self, input: reverie::InheritedInputLease) {
1949        // Called once by the launcher before this global state is published.
1950        // All fallible endpoint/lease creation happened before initialization.
1951        *self.inherited_input.get_mut().unwrap() = Some(PendingInheritedInput {
1952            lease: input,
1953            root: None,
1954        });
1955    }
1956
1957    fn install_backend_signal_control(
1958        &self,
1959        control: Option<reverie::BackendSignalControl>,
1960    ) -> Result<reverie::BackendSignalControlMode, reverie::Error> {
1961        self.sched
1962            .lock()
1963            .unwrap()
1964            .install_signal_control(control, self.cfg.sequentialize_threads)
1965    }
1966
1967    /// Dequeues carry real-timer signals only in a run that installed the
1968    /// backend's control; any other run leaves them to the guest kernel.
1969    fn observe_signal_dequeues(&self, mode: reverie::BackendSignalControlMode) -> bool {
1970        mode == reverie::BackendSignalControlMode::ToolControlled
1971    }
1972
1973    fn authorize_backend_signal_boundary(
1974        &self,
1975        task: reverie::SignalTaskIdentity,
1976    ) -> Result<Option<reverie::SignalDeliveryPermit>, reverie::Error> {
1977        self.sched.lock().unwrap().authorize_signal_boundary(task)
1978    }
1979
1980    async fn on_backend_signal_boundary(
1981        &self,
1982        receipt: reverie::SignalBoundaryReceipt,
1983    ) -> Result<(), reverie::Error> {
1984        self.sched.lock().unwrap().consume_signal_boundary(receipt)
1985    }
1986
1987    fn on_backend_process_retired(
1988        &self,
1989        event: reverie::BackendProcessRetirement,
1990    ) -> Result<(), reverie::Error> {
1991        let (result, wakes) = {
1992            let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
1993            let result = sched.consume_process_retirement(event);
1994            (result, sched.take_signal_failure_wakes())
1995        };
1996        for wake in wakes {
1997            let _ = wake.send(());
1998        }
1999        result
2000    }
2001
2002    /// A backend whose process exits complete asynchronously reports each
2003    /// physical exit here; see [`GlobalState::complete_physical_process_exit`].
2004    fn on_backend_process_exited(&self, pid: i32) {
2005        if self.cfg.backend.reports_child_exit_publication {
2006            // The kernel has published this process's exit to its parent. It
2007            // is not a physical-exit barrier report on this backend.
2008            let released = self
2009                .sched
2010                .lock()
2011                .unwrap()
2012                .complete_child_exit_publication(DetPid::from_raw(pid));
2013            if released {
2014                trace!("[detcore, dpid {}] backend published the child exit", pid);
2015            }
2016        } else {
2017            self.complete_physical_process_exit(pid);
2018        }
2019    }
2020
2021    /// The processes held between their exit grant and their physical exit,
2022    /// for the backend's watchdog.
2023    fn backend_pending_process_exits(&self) -> Vec<i32> {
2024        self.sched
2025            .lock()
2026            .unwrap()
2027            .pending_async_process_exits()
2028            .into_iter()
2029            .map(|detpid| detpid.as_raw())
2030            .collect()
2031    }
2032
2033    fn on_fatal_signal_exit(&self, exit: &reverie::FatalSignalExit) {
2034        if let Some(capture) = &self.cfg.fatal_core_capture {
2035            crate::fatal_core::capture_and_log(capture, exit);
2036        }
2037    }
2038
2039    fn report_backend_failure(&self, event: reverie::BackendFailure) {
2040        let (wake, deferred) = {
2041            let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
2042            (
2043                sched.report_backend_failure(event),
2044                sched.take_signal_failure_wakes(),
2045            )
2046        };
2047        for wake in deferred {
2048            let _ = wake.send(());
2049        }
2050        if let Some(wake) = wake {
2051            // No waiter can begin consuming cleanup until the scheduler has
2052            // closed its selected transaction under the grant/commit mutex.
2053            let _ = wake.send(());
2054        }
2055    }
2056
2057    async fn wait_for_backend_failure(&self) {
2058        let wake = self.sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failure_waiter();
2059        wake.await
2060            .expect("GlobalState owns the failure sender until publication");
2061    }
2062
2063    async fn on_backend_child_wait_event(
2064        &self,
2065        event: reverie::BackendChildWaitEvent,
2066    ) -> Result<(), reverie::Error> {
2067        // KVM polls this future through its first suspension before exposing
2068        // waitability. The helper's first poll performs the complete
2069        // generation-bound publication under the scheduler mutex, then
2070        // self-wakes and returns Pending; its second poll consumes the typed
2071        // result and releases the stage-2 control barrier.
2072        crate::scheduler::signal_control::ChildExitPublicationFuture::new(self.sched.clone(), event)
2073            .await
2074    }
2075
2076    async fn receive_rpc(&self, from: Tid, gr: Self::Request) -> Self::Response {
2077        // Intercept even malformed counted envelopes before taking a deadline
2078        // hint. Native controls belong to the already owned exec cut.
2079        if native_exec::is_native_exec_control(&gr.2) {
2080            return self.dispatch_native_exec_control(from, gr);
2081        }
2082        // The deadline hint of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121
2083        // rides on whichever reply resumes the thread after its grant: an
2084        // ordinary or parked resource grant, a futex wake, a parent's
2085        // continuation, thread start, the exec continuation. Clearing on
2086        // arrival means a reply carries only a hint recorded while its own
2087        // request was pending (a grant, or a timer the request armed).
2088        // Only a request whose reply resumes the thread from a grant, or arms
2089        // a timer, touches the hint: control messages sent on another task's
2090        // behalf must neither consume nor carry it.
2091        if !resumes_from_grant(&gr.2) {
2092            return self.dispatch_rpc(from, gr).await;
2093        }
2094        let dtid = DetTid::from_raw(from.as_raw());
2095        self.sched.lock().unwrap().take_deadline_hint(dtid);
2096        let (time, response) = self.dispatch_rpc(from, gr).await;
2097        let hint = self.sched.lock().unwrap().take_deadline_hint(dtid);
2098        match hint {
2099            Some(remaining)
2100                if response != GlobalResponse::ThreadExited
2101                    && response != GlobalResponse::Retired =>
2102            {
2103                (
2104                    time,
2105                    GlobalResponse::WithDeadline(remaining, Box::new(response)),
2106                )
2107            }
2108            _ => (time, response),
2109        }
2110    }
2111}
2112
2113impl GlobalState {
2114    async fn dispatch_rpc(
2115        &self,
2116        from: Tid,
2117        gr: <Self as GlobalTool>::Request,
2118    ) -> <Self as GlobalTool>::Response {
2119        // This entry is also used directly. The strict native cut must precede
2120        // ordinary forwarding drain/checks and all sender-clock accounting.
2121        if native_exec::is_native_exec_control(&gr.2) {
2122            return self.dispatch_native_exec_control(from, gr);
2123        }
2124        // Records an in-guest Tool forwarded before sending this request are queued,
2125        // and the sender's are written now if it runs alone (the order rule at
2126        // `detlog::set_forwarded_source`).
2127        crate::detlog::drain_forwarded_at_request(from.as_raw());
2128        type R = GlobalResponse;
2129        let dtid = DetTid::from_raw(from.into()); // TODO(T78538674): FIXME
2130        let (guest_time, request_mm, request) = gr;
2131        let request = match request {
2132            GlobalRequest::WithForwardedCount(produced, request) => {
2133                crate::detlog::check_forwarded_count(from.as_raw(), produced);
2134                *request
2135            }
2136            request => request,
2137        };
2138        let time_from_guest = guest_time.as_nanos();
2139        // Exec transfer messages authenticate both incarnations before ordinary
2140        // sender-clock accounting. The carried clock still belongs to the former
2141        // thread until the successful reconnect commits.
2142        match &request {
2143            GlobalRequest::ReconnectExec { former, process } => {
2144                return self
2145                    .recv_exec_transfer(from, guest_time, request_mm, *former, *process)
2146                    .await;
2147            }
2148            GlobalRequest::RetireExec { thread, signaled } => {
2149                return self
2150                    .recv_retire_exec_transfer(
2151                        from,
2152                        guest_time,
2153                        request_mm,
2154                        thread.clone(),
2155                        *signaled,
2156                    )
2157                    .await;
2158            }
2159            _ => {}
2160        }
2161        // A committed SIGKILL victim's requests that return before ordinary
2162        // admission (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). Exec
2163        // transfers above, the child-exit SIGCHLD control (sent in the
2164        // sender's own turn, which a committed victim no longer gets, or by
2165        // the tracer at a signal stop) and the consuming `SignalDequeued` keep
2166        // their own answers. Shared open file control is in-guest LiteInst
2167        // transport, never sent on ptrace, where alone a SIGKILL is retired
2168        // at the commit. Observations and loss notices are still recorded,
2169        // since dropping one only loses information, but not answered. A
2170        // SIGALRM ledger change from a thread that is already logically dead
2171        // would land at a host-chosen time: it is refused, and not answered
2172        // either.
2173        let early_victim_request = match &request {
2174            GlobalRequest::RecordHostInput { .. }
2175            | GlobalRequest::RecordHostMutation { .. }
2176            | GlobalRequest::RecordDeterminismLoss(_)
2177            | GlobalRequest::Sigalrm(_) => self
2178                .sched
2179                .lock()
2180                .unwrap()
2181                .is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim(dtid),
2182            _ => false,
2183        };
2184        if early_victim_request && matches!(&request, GlobalRequest::Sigalrm(_)) {
2185            return (None, R::Retired);
2186        }
2187        // An observation for `hermit run --verify`, answered before any clock
2188        // or scheduler accounting: it carries no logical time, changes no
2189        // scheduler state, and its answer carries no time back.
2190        if let GlobalRequest::RecordHostInput {
2191            path,
2192            syscall,
2193            identity,
2194        } = request
2195        {
2196            self.host_inputs.lock().unwrap().push(HostInputRecord {
2197                path,
2198                dtid: dtid.as_raw() as u64,
2199                syscall,
2200                identity,
2201            });
2202            if early_victim_request {
2203                return (None, R::Retired);
2204            }
2205            return (None, R::RecordHostInput(()));
2206        }
2207        if let GlobalRequest::RecordHostMutation { path } = request {
2208            self.host_mutations.lock().unwrap().insert(path);
2209            if early_victim_request {
2210                return (None, R::Retired);
2211            }
2212            return (None, R::RecordHostMutation(()));
2213        }
2214        // A determinism loss is recorded where verification reads it, and,
2215        // like the observations above, moves no clock: whether the host made
2216        // a guest-side handler lose determinism must not change guest time.
2217        if let GlobalRequest::RecordDeterminismLoss(reason) = request {
2218            crate::detlog::write_loss_notice(&reason);
2219            if early_victim_request {
2220                return (None, R::Retired);
2221            }
2222            return (None, R::RecordDeterminismLoss(()));
2223        }
2224        // Control traffic for a shared open file description: like the
2225        // observations above, it carries no logical time, changes no
2226        // scheduler state, and its answer carries no time back.
2227        if let GlobalRequest::SharedOpenFile(control) = request {
2228            return (
2229                None,
2230                R::SharedOpenFile(self.shared_open_file_control(dtid, control)),
2231            );
2232        }
2233        // A SIGALRM ledger control message: like the messages above, it
2234        // carries no logical time and its answer carries none back. It reads
2235        // or records ledger state, which changes only at scheduler commits,
2236        // in the sender's own turn.
2237        if let GlobalRequest::Sigalrm(control) = request {
2238            let refused = self.sched.lock().unwrap().sigalrm_control(dtid, control);
2239            return (None, R::Sigalrm(refused));
2240        }
2241        // A child-exit SIGCHLD control message: like the SIGALRM ledger's, it
2242        // carries no logical time and its answer carries none back. It
2243        // records an exit status in the sender's own turn, or answers at a
2244        // signal stop, which no scheduler state waits for.
2245        if let GlobalRequest::ChildExitSigchld(control) = request {
2246            let answer = self
2247                .sched
2248                .lock()
2249                .unwrap()
2250                .child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(dtid, control);
2251            return (None, R::ChildExitSigchld(answer));
2252        }
2253        // A discarded-at-send record message
2254        // (`scheduler::discarded_at_send`): like the child-exit ledger's, it
2255        // carries no logical time and its answer carries none back. It records
2256        // a send in the sender's own turn, or a consumption at a signal stop.
2257        if let GlobalRequest::DiscardedSignal(control) = request {
2258            let answer = self
2259                .sched
2260                .lock()
2261                .unwrap()
2262                .discarded_signal_control(dtid, control);
2263            return (None, R::DiscardedSignal(answer));
2264        }
2265        if let GlobalRequest::SignalDequeued {
2266            detpid,
2267            identity,
2268            dequeue,
2269        } = &request
2270        {
2271            return self
2272                .recv_signal_dequeued(dtid, request_mm, guest_time, *detpid, *identity, *dequeue)
2273                .await;
2274        }
2275
2276        // A vfork child registers itself while the parent is kernel-blocked.
2277        // Reopening a former exec worker's TID requires that exact pending
2278        // parent grant and its address-space lineage, not an ordinary RPC.
2279        if let GlobalRequest::CreateVforkChildThread(parent, process, child, _, flags, ..) =
2280            &request
2281        {
2282            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2283            if sched.transferred_exec_tid_requires_registration(dtid) {
2284                if *child != dtid
2285                    || !flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_VFORK)
2286                    || !sched.pending_vfork_registration_matches(
2287                        *parent,
2288                        *process,
2289                        *child,
2290                        request_mm,
2291                        flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_VM),
2292                    )
2293                {
2294                    return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2295                }
2296                sched.register_reused_transferred_exec_tid(dtid, request_mm);
2297            }
2298        }
2299
2300        // Ptrace may deliver a newborn's startup before the parent's clone
2301        // callback registers it. A former exec worker's reused Linux TID must
2302        // wait for that authenticated registration, not inherit the old
2303        // incarnation or turn a premature refusal into a silent exit(0).
2304        // No clock or scheduler request is published while it waits.
2305        if matches!(&request, GlobalRequest::StartNewThread(child, ..) if *child == dtid) {
2306            loop {
2307                {
2308                    let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2309                    if !sched.transferred_exec_tid_requires_registration(dtid)
2310                        || sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid)
2311                    {
2312                        break;
2313                    }
2314                }
2315                yield_once().await;
2316            }
2317        }
2318
2319        let is_deregister = matches!(&request, GlobalRequest::DeregisterThread(_));
2320        let consuming_cleanup =
2321            is_deregister || matches!(&request, GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(_));
2322        // What a committed SIGKILL victim may still send and be answered
2323        // (`Scheduler::is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim`): its consuming cleanup,
2324        // and the failure reports that end a run.
2325        let answered_for_sigkill_victim = consuming_cleanup
2326            || matches!(
2327                &request,
2328                GlobalRequest::ParkedProtocolFailure(_)
2329                    | GlobalRequest::UnrecoverableShutdown
2330                    | GlobalRequest::PolicyRefusal(_)
2331            );
2332
2333        let (exec_reconnect, is_exec_caller_after_local_mm_swap) = {
2334            let pending = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap();
2335            let reconnect = match &request {
2336                GlobalRequest::CreateChildThread(child, process, _, None, _, _, _)
2337                    if *child == dtid && *child == *process =>
2338                {
2339                    pending.get(process).cloned()
2340                }
2341                _ => None,
2342            };
2343            let is_exec_caller_after_local_mm_swap = pending.values().any(|state| {
2344                state.caller == dtid && state.mm.for_exec(state.process) == request_mm
2345            });
2346            (reconnect, is_exec_caller_after_local_mm_swap)
2347        };
2348
2349        // Retired incarnations cannot publish clocks. A transferred former TID
2350        // reopens only through fresh child registration; successful exec binds
2351        // the surviving leader separately. Hold admission through clock
2352        // accounting so logical teardown cannot linearize between the two.
2353        let mut tombstoned_deregistration = None;
2354        {
2355            let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(consuming_cleanup).await;
2356            if exec_reconnect.is_none()
2357                && !is_exec_caller_after_local_mm_swap
2358                && !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dtid, request_mm)
2359            {
2360                debug!(
2361                    "[detcore, dtid {}] rejecting {:?} RPC from retired exec incarnation {:?}",
2362                    dtid, request, request_mm,
2363                );
2364                return if is_deregister {
2365                    (None, R::DeregisterThread(()))
2366                } else {
2367                    (None, R::ThreadExited)
2368                };
2369            }
2370            if let GlobalRequest::DeregisterThread(owner) = &request {
2371                assert_eq!(
2372                    owner.dettid, dtid,
2373                    "deregistration must belong to its sender"
2374                );
2375                assert_eq!(owner.mm, request_mm, "deregistration must retain its MmId");
2376                // DBT can reject StartNewThread before parent registration.
2377                // Its tombstone still needs the existing final accounting path.
2378                if !sched.thread_was_registered(dtid) && !sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid) {
2379                    assert!(
2380                        sched.backend_failed() || !owner.thread_start_entered,
2381                        "a started thread must have a scheduler registration before deregistration"
2382                    );
2383                    // The backend still consumes this constructed ThreadState,
2384                    // but no guest start/registration happened. Acknowledge its
2385                    // cleanup without creating a clock, tree entry or admission.
2386                    return (None, R::DeregisterThread(()));
2387                }
2388            }
2389            let child = match &request {
2390                GlobalRequest::CreateChildThread(child, ..)
2391                | GlobalRequest::CreateVforkChildThread(_, _, child, ..) => Some(*child),
2392                _ => None,
2393            };
2394            if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid) && exec_reconnect.is_none() {
2395                trace!(
2396                    "[detcore, dtid {}] rejecting RPC after permanent logical-thread removal",
2397                    dtid
2398                );
2399                if let GlobalRequest::DeregisterThread(deregistration) = &request {
2400                    tombstoned_deregistration = Some(deregistration.clone());
2401                } else {
2402                    return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2403                }
2404            }
2405            if !answered_for_sigkill_victim && sched.is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim(dtid) {
2406                trace!(
2407                    "[detcore, dtid {}] leaving a SIGKILLed thread's request unanswered",
2408                    dtid
2409                );
2410                return (None, R::Retired);
2411            }
2412            if child.is_some_and(|child| sched.thread_is_logically_killed(child))
2413                && exec_reconnect.is_none()
2414            {
2415                trace!(
2416                    "[detcore, dtid {}] rejecting registration that reuses a tombstoned child TID",
2417                    dtid
2418                );
2419                return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2420            }
2421
2422            if let GlobalRequest::ResumeExec(process) = &request
2423                && (dtid != *process
2424                    || sched.registered_process(dtid) != Some(*process)
2425                    || !sched.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid))
2426            {
2427                return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2428            }
2429
2430            // An admitted ordinary request under the new identity proves the
2431            // Tool received the transfer acknowledgment and rebound its state.
2432            self.acknowledge_exec_transfer(dtid, request_mm);
2433
2434            let is_thread_reconnect = matches!(
2435                &request,
2436                GlobalRequest::StartNewThread(child_dettid, ..) if *child_dettid == dtid
2437            ) && self.global_time.lock().unwrap().contains_thread(dtid);
2438
2439            // This portion of the time updates "asynchronously", and we can tick it on every rpc:
2440            // TODO: eventually the vector clock should be in shared memory, and
2441            // the local clocks should update truly asynchrously.  Therefore it
2442            // SHOULD be safe to always push through this update on any rpc.
2443            if tombstoned_deregistration.is_none()
2444                && exec_reconnect.is_none()
2445                && !is_thread_reconnect
2446            {
2447                self.global_time.lock().unwrap().update_global_time(
2448                    dtid,
2449                    time_from_guest,
2450                    guest_time.inherited_nanos(),
2451                );
2452            }
2453        }
2454        if let Some(deregistration) = tombstoned_deregistration {
2455            self.recv_deregister_thread(from, deregistration).await;
2456            return (None, R::DeregisterThread(()));
2457        }
2458
2459        // RPC boilerplate. (Hard to generate systematically now though, because of the
2460        // time payload piggy-backing on each rpc. Maybe eventually once ticking a
2461        // threads' own clock happens through shared memory.)
2462        #[allow(clippy::unit_arg)]
2463        let resp = match request {
2464            GlobalRequest::PrepareNativeExec(_)
2465            | GlobalRequest::SealNativeExecStats { .. }
2466            | GlobalRequest::IssueNativeExec { .. }
2467            | GlobalRequest::CancelNativeExec { .. }
2468            | GlobalRequest::CompleteNativeExec { .. } => {
2469                unreachable!("native controls handled before ordinary admission")
2470            }
2471            GlobalRequest::ReconnectExec { .. } | GlobalRequest::RetireExec { .. } => {
2472                unreachable!("exec transfer handled before ordinary admission")
2473            }
2474            GlobalRequest::WithForwardedCount(..) => {
2475                unreachable!("a counted request is unwrapped on arrival")
2476            }
2477            GlobalRequest::ResumeExec(process) => {
2478                let mut resources = Resources::new(dtid);
2479                resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(process), Permission::RW);
2480                let (response, duration) = self
2481                    .recv_request_resources(from, process, resources, Some(request_mm))
2482                    .await;
2483                match response {
2484                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(status) => R::ResumeExec(status, duration),
2485                    SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited => R::ThreadExited,
2486                }
2487            }
2488            GlobalRequest::SignalDequeued { .. } => {
2489                unreachable!("consuming path handled before ordinary cancellation")
2490            }
2491            GlobalRequest::RecordHostInput { .. } | GlobalRequest::RecordHostMutation { .. } => {
2492                unreachable!("host-input observation answered before clock accounting")
2493            }
2494            GlobalRequest::SharedOpenFile(_) => {
2495                unreachable!("shared open file control answered before clock accounting")
2496            }
2497            GlobalRequest::Sigalrm(_) => {
2498                unreachable!("SIGALRM ledger control answered before clock accounting")
2499            }
2500            GlobalRequest::ChildExitSigchld(_) => {
2501                unreachable!("child-exit SIGCHLD control answered before clock accounting")
2502            }
2503            GlobalRequest::DiscardedSignal(_) => {
2504                unreachable!("discarded-at-send control answered before clock accounting")
2505            }
2506            GlobalRequest::RecordDeterminismLoss(_) => {
2507                unreachable!("determinism loss answered before clock accounting")
2508            }
2509            GlobalRequest::ParkedRequest(rs, pid, capability) => {
2510                let (response, _) = self
2511                    .recv_resources_with_origin(
2512                        from,
2513                        pid,
2514                        rs,
2515                        Some(request_mm),
2516                        RpcOrigin::DirectRequestResources,
2517                        capability,
2518                    )
2519                    .await;
2520                match response {
2521                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(r) => R::ParkedRequest(r),
2522                    SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited => R::ThreadExited,
2523                }
2524            }
2525            GlobalRequest::ResumeParkedRequest {
2526                ticket,
2527                current_site,
2528            } => {
2529                self.recv_resume_parked(from, request_mm, ticket, current_site)
2530                    .await
2531            }
2532            GlobalRequest::FinishParkedObservation {
2533                wait,
2534                lease,
2535                site,
2536                finish,
2537            } => {
2538                let ack = Ivar::new();
2539                let intent = ControlIntent::Finish {
2540                    wait,
2541                    lease,
2542                    site,
2543                    finish,
2544                    ack: ack.clone(),
2545                };
2546                let posted = self
2547                    .sched
2548                    .lock()
2549                    .unwrap()
2550                    .post_control(dtid, request_mm, intent);
2551                if let Err(error) = posted {
2552                    self.sched.lock().unwrap().fail_parked(dtid, error);
2553                    return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2554                }
2555                R::FinishParkedObservation(ack.await)
2556            }
2557            GlobalRequest::ParkedProtocolFailure(error) => {
2558                self.sched.lock().unwrap().fail_parked(dtid, error);
2559                return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2560            }
2561
2562            GlobalRequest::RequestResources(rs, pid) => {
2563                let (response, _endtime) = self
2564                    .recv_request_resources(from, pid, rs, Some(request_mm))
2565                    .await;
2566                match response {
2567                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(response) => R::RequestResources(response),
2568                    SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited => R::ThreadExited,
2569                }
2570            }
2571            GlobalRequest::ReleaseResources(rs) => {
2572                R::ReleaseResources(self.recv_release_resources(from, rs).await)
2573            }
2574            GlobalRequest::ReleaseAllResources => {
2575                R::ReleaseAllResources(self.recv_release_all_resources(from).await)
2576            }
2577            GlobalRequest::PolicyRefusal(reason) => {
2578                self.policy_refusal.lock().unwrap().get_or_insert(reason);
2579                R::PolicyRefusal(())
2580            }
2581            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-643): Review run-wide unsupported-syscall aggregation.
2582            GlobalRequest::ReportUnsupportedSyscall(name) => {
2583                let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2584                let inserted = self
2585                    .unsupported_syscalls
2586                    .lock()
2587                    .unwrap()
2588                    .insert(name.clone());
2589                if inserted
2590                    && let Some(report) = &self.unsupported_syscall_report_fd
2591                    && let Err(error) = writeln!(report.lock().unwrap(), "{name}")
2592                {
2593                    warn!("failed to append unsupported-syscall report: {error}");
2594                }
2595                R::ReportUnsupportedSyscall(())
2596            }
2597            GlobalRequest::PrepareExec(process, mm, fd_blocking) => {
2598                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2599                if mm != request_mm
2600                    || fd_blocking.initialize_inherited_stdio
2601                    || fd_blocking.initial_input.is_some()
2602                {
2603                    return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2604                }
2605                if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !sched.prepare_exec_teardown(dtid, process, mm)
2606                {
2607                    return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2608                }
2609                trace!(
2610                    "[detcore, dtid {}] preparing exec for process {} with mm {:?} and logically blocking descriptors {:?}",
2611                    dtid, process, mm, fd_blocking,
2612                );
2613                self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().insert(
2614                    process,
2615                    PendingExecState {
2616                        caller: dtid,
2617                        process,
2618                        mm,
2619                        fd_blocking: *fd_blocking,
2620                    },
2621                );
2622                R::PrepareExec(())
2623            }
2624            GlobalRequest::CancelExec(process) => {
2625                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2626                let mut pending = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap();
2627                if pending
2628                    .get(&process)
2629                    .is_some_and(|state| state.caller == dtid)
2630                {
2631                    let prepared = pending.remove(&process).unwrap();
2632                    sched.finish_exec_teardown(prepared.caller, process, prepared.mm, false);
2633                }
2634                R::CancelExec(())
2635            }
2636            GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(detpid, signal_identity, kernel_image) => {
2637                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;

2639                // the identity-transfer RPC. This successful-exec edge still
2640                // commits the frozen sibling cohort in scheduler order.
2641                let prepared = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().get(&dtid).cloned();
2642                if sched.signal_control_installed() {
2643                    let result = (|| {
2644                        let identity = signal_identity.ok_or(ProtocolFailure::Identity)?;
2645                        let pid = sched
2646                            .registered_process(dtid)
2647                            .ok_or(ProtocolFailure::Identity)?;
2648                        let mut pending = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap();
2649                        if let Some(prepared) = pending.get(&pid) {
2650                            if prepared.caller != dtid || prepared.process != pid {
2651                                return Err(ProtocolFailure::Identity);
2652                            }
2653                            sched.complete_signal_exec(
2654                                pid,
2655                                dtid,
2656                                prepared.mm,
2657                                request_mm,
2658                                identity,
2659                            )?;
2660                            pending.remove(&pid);
2661                        } else {
2662                            // A backend that re-enters thread-start already bound
2663                            // the new image. A lifecycle notification alone cannot
2664                            // authorize a new address space or backend generation.
2665                            sched
2666                                .real_timers
2667                                .validate_task(pid, dtid, request_mm, identity)?;
2668                        }
2669                        Ok(())
2670                    })();
2671                    if let Err(error) = result {
2672                        sched.fail_parked(dtid, error);
2673                        return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2674                    }
2675                }
2676                // The exec caller still owns its turn: delete process-owned
2677                // POSIX deadlines before the replacement image can yield or run.
2678                // Failed exec takes CancelExec and never reaches this point.
2679                sched.delete_exec_posix_timers(detpid);
2680                // The exec resets the process's exit signal to SIGCHLD and turns
2681                // its existing children's notifications into SIGCHLD.
2682                sched.record_successful_exec(detpid);
2683                // Reloading backends consumed the preparation in their
2684                // registration reconnect; state-preserving leaders consume it
2685                // here after the terminal exec notification was authenticated.
2686                if let Some(prepared) = &prepared
2687                    && self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
2688                    && prepared.caller == dtid
2689                    && prepared.process == dtid
2690                    && prepared.mm.for_exec(dtid) == request_mm
2691                {
2692                    // Only a reloading backend (DBT) carries owner-death
2693                    // wakes with its preparation, and it delivered them at
2694                    // its reconnect; ptrace delivers its own after the exec
2695                    // (Claude review of
2696                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4352, F5).
2697                    assert!(
2698                        prepared.fd_blocking.robust_wakes.is_empty(),
2699                        "a state-preserving exec carried robust-list wakes to the coordinator"
2700                    );
2701                    sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
2702                        caller: dtid,
2703                        new_leader: dtid,
2704                        detpid: dtid,
2705                        pre_exec_mm: prepared.mm,
2706                        post_exec_mm: request_mm,
2707                        child_tid_addr: 0,
2708                        reconnect_priority: None,
2709                    });
2710                    self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().remove(&dtid);
2711                    // Native-only lifecycle receipt: the actual same-leader
2712                    // Mark edge has now installed this ticket's new mm. This
2713                    // hook grants no turn and performs no clock accounting.
2714                    if let Some(registry) = self.native_exec_registry.get()
2715                        && registry
2716                            .lock()
2717                            .unwrap()
2718                            .mark_past_first_exec(dtid, request_mm)
2719                            .is_err()
2720                    {
2721                        return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2722                    }
2723                }
2724                self.past_first_execve.store(true, SeqCst);
2725                let first_image = !self.initial_descriptor_image_complete.swap(true, SeqCst);
2726                let mut overrides = self
2727                    .post_exec_fd_blocking
2728                    .lock()
2729                    .unwrap()
2730                    .remove(&dtid)
2731                    .unwrap_or_default();
2732                trace!(
2733                    "[detcore, dtid {}] restoring logically blocking descriptors after exec: {:?}",
2734                    dtid, overrides,
2735                );
2736                overrides.initialize_inherited_stdio =
2737                    first_image && self.cfg.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table;
2738                // The image the exec ran: a reloading backend carried it in the
2739                // preparation it reconnected with (above); a state-preserving
2740                // one left the preparation to this edge. The registered root's
2741                // first image is the one its launch named, which a backend
2742                // whose launcher loads the guest (SaBRe) never execs.
2743                // Without sequentialized threads, sibling execs may prepare
2744                // concurrently and the preparation this edge consumed may be
2745                // another thread's, which the launcher check cannot tell
2746                // apart: no prepared record is kept (a launched run then
2747                // refuses the link by name).
2748                if !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads {
2749                    overrides.exe = None;
2750                } else if overrides.exe.is_none() {
2751                    overrides.exe = prepared
2752                        .filter(|prepared| prepared.caller == dtid)
2753                        .and_then(|prepared| prepared.fd_blocking.exe);
2754                }
2755                if self.root_dettid.get() == Some(&dtid)
2756                    && !self.root_image_marked.swap(true, SeqCst)
2757                    && let Some(launch) = &self.cfg.launch_image
2758                {
2759                    overrides.exe = launch.exe.as_deref().and_then(|exe| {
2760                        crate::exec_record::ExecRecord::at(std::path::Path::new("/"), exe)
2761                    });
2762                }
2763                // A record stands only where the kernel's own link, which the
2764                // new image read (`kernel_image`), names the recorded file or
2765                // the launcher the run declared: Detcore's resolution looked the
2766                // path up in its own view, which a binfmt_misc handler, another
2767                // filesystem view or a racing exec can make wrong. Where the
2768                // tool cannot read the link (KVM), the record stands.
2769                if let Some(kernel) = kernel_image {
2770                    overrides.exe = overrides.exe.filter(|record| {
2771                        record.identity() == kernel || self.launcher_identity() == Some(kernel)
2772                    });
2773                }
2774                // The launcher itself is never the guest's image (a link to it
2775                // resolved, as the kernel's link names it).
2776                overrides.exe = overrides
2777                    .exe
2778                    .filter(|record| Some(record.identity()) != self.launcher_identity());
2779                {
2780                    let mut images = self.exec_images.lock().unwrap();
2781                    match &overrides.exe {
2782                        Some(record) => images.insert(detpid, record.clone()),
2783                        None => images.remove(&detpid),
2784                    };
2785                }
2786                if self.cfg.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table {
2787                    let mut input = self.inherited_input.lock().unwrap();
2788                    if input
2789                        .as_ref()
2790                        .is_some_and(|input| input.root == Some((dtid, request_mm)))
2791                    {
2792                        // Only this registered root/image consumes the launch
2793                        // seed. A descendant or later exec cannot acquire it.
2794                        // Drop the temporary reader at this handoff; the actual
2795                        // root's descriptor remains live until local validation.
2796                        overrides.initial_input =
2797                            input.take().map(|input| input.lease.identity().clone());
2798                    }
2799                }
2800                R::MarkPastFirstExecve(Box::new(overrides))
2801            }
2802            // Requested by the parent thread:
2803            GlobalRequest::CreateChildThread(
2804                dettid,
2805                parent_detpid,
2806                ctid,
2807                flags,
2808                exit_signal,
2809                physical_ids,
2810                priority,
2811            ) => {
2812                if let Some(prepared) = &exec_reconnect {
2813                    let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
2814                    let (mut pending, post_exec_mm) = {
2815                        let mut states = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap();
2816                        let Some(pending) = states.remove(&parent_detpid) else {
2817                            return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2818                        };
2819                        assert_eq!(&pending, prepared);
2820                        let post_exec_mm = pending.mm.for_exec(pending.process);
2821                        (pending, post_exec_mm)
2822                    };
2823                    assert_eq!(pending.process, parent_detpid);
2824                    if let Some((physical_pid, physical_tid)) = physical_ids
2825                        && let Err(open_error) = sched.register_physical_thread(
2826                            dettid,
2827                            post_exec_mm,
2828                            physical_pid,
2829                            physical_tid,
2830                        )
2831                    {
2832                        error!(
2833                            "[detcore, dtid {}] failed to register post-exec host process {} thread {}: {}",
2834                            dettid, physical_pid, physical_tid, open_error,
2835                        );
2836                        return (None, R::ThreadExited);
2837                    }
2838                    let retired = sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
2839                        caller: pending.caller,
2840                        new_leader: dettid,
2841                        detpid: parent_detpid,
2842                        pre_exec_mm: pending.mm,
2843                        post_exec_mm,
2844                        child_tid_addr: ctid,
2845                        reconnect_priority: priority,
2846                    });

2849                            .lock()
2850                            .unwrap()

2852                    }
2853                    // Linux marked the old thread group's robust-list words
2854                    // during the exec, which this message from the new image
2855                    // follows, and the reconnect has retired the threads the
2856                    // exec killed. Wake one waiter per marked word now, under
2857                    // the same lock: the scheduler commits no turn between the
2858                    // exec's grant and this reconnect, and the admissions are
2859                    // drained in canonical order
2860                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4268).
2861                    let robust_wakes = std::mem::take(&mut pending.fd_blocking.robust_wakes);

3437            GlobalRequest::ProcessImage(process) => {
3438                let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3439                // `/proc/<tid>/exe` names a thread's process's image.
3440                let process = sched
3441                    .registered_process(DetTid::from_raw(process.as_raw()))
3442                    .unwrap_or(process);
3443                R::ProcessImage(
3444                    self.exec_images
3445                        .lock()
3446                        .unwrap()
3447                        .get(&process)
3448                        .cloned()
3449                        .map(Box::new),
3450                )
3451            }
3452            GlobalRequest::GroupOrSession(pid, session) => R::GroupOrSession(
3453                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3454                    .await
3455                    .group_or_session_of(pid, session),
3456            ),
3457            GlobalRequest::SetsidDecision(process) => R::SetsidDecision(
3458                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3459                    .await
3460                    .setsid_decision(process)
3461                    .map_err(|errno| errno.into_raw()),
3462            ),
3463            GlobalRequest::SetpgidDecision(caller, pid, pgid) => R::SetpgidDecision(
3464                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3465                    .await
3466                    .setpgid_decision(caller, pid, pgid)
3467                    .map_err(|errno| errno.into_raw()),
3468            ),
3469            GlobalRequest::ProcfsTask(named, thread) => {
3470                let existence = self
3471                    .lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3472                    .await
3473                    .procfs_task(named, thread);
3474                R::ProcfsTask(
3475                    self.inodes
3476                        .lock()
3477                        .unwrap()
3478                        .procfs_task_answer(named, thread, existence),
3479                )
3480            }
3481            GlobalRequest::RenderedFileState(inode, change) => R::RenderedFileState(
3482                self.inodes
3483                    .lock()
3484                    .unwrap()
3485                    .rendered_file_state(inode, change),
3486            ),
3487            GlobalRequest::LocalPid(caller, task) => R::LocalPid(
3488                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3489                    .await
3490                    .thread_tree
3491                    .pid_namespaces
3492                    .localize_for(caller, task),
3493            ),
3494            GlobalRequest::SignalTargetProcess(named) => R::SignalTargetProcess(
3495                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3496                    .await
3497                    .signal_target_process(named),
3498            ),
3499            GlobalRequest::PosixTimerThread(process, named) => R::PosixTimerThread(
3500                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3501                    .await
3502                    .posix_timer_thread(process, named),
3503            ),
3504            GlobalRequest::SetSigchldDisposition(process, ignored, nocldwait) => {
3505                R::SetSigchldDisposition(
3506                    self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3507                        .await
3508                        .thread_tree
3509                        .set_sigchld_disposition(process, ignored, nocldwait),
3510                )
3511            }
3512            GlobalRequest::SetChildSubreaper(process, on) => R::SetChildSubreaper(
3513                self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false)
3514                    .await
3515                    .thread_tree
3516                    .set_child_subreaper(process, on),
3517            ),
3518            GlobalRequest::UnrecoverableShutdown => {
3519                self.force_shutdown_with_error();
3520                R::UnrecoverableShutdown(())
3521            }
3522            GlobalRequest::Network(request) => {
3523                let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3524                let mut engine = self
3525                    .network
3526                    .as_ref()
3527                    .expect("network request without a network trace mode")
3528                    .lock()
3529                    .unwrap();
3530                let now = self.global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
3531                R::Network(engine.apply(now, request))
3532            }
3533            GlobalRequest::RequestPort(open_file_id) => {
3534                let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3535                let mut mut_used_ports = self.used_ports.lock().unwrap();
3536                self.update_port_range();
3537                let total_available =
3538                    self.port_end_range.load(SeqCst) - self.port_start_range.load(SeqCst);
3539                let mut index = 0;
3540                while (*mut_used_ports).contains(&self.next_port.load(SeqCst))
3541                    && index < total_available
3542                {
3543                    self.next_port.fetch_add(1, SeqCst);
3544                    if self.next_port.load(SeqCst) > self.port_end_range.load(SeqCst) {
3545                        self.next_port
3546                            .store(self.port_start_range.load(SeqCst), SeqCst);
3547                    }
3548                    index += 1;
3549                }
3550                if index == total_available {
3551                    R::PortFull
3552                } else {
3553                    (*mut_used_ports).insert(self.next_port.load(SeqCst));
3554                    let mut open_file_to_port = self.open_file_to_port.lock().unwrap();
3555                    open_file_to_port.insert(open_file_id, self.next_port.load(SeqCst));
3556                    R::RequestPort(self.next_port.load(SeqCst))
3557                }
3558            }
3559            GlobalRequest::AddUsedPort(port, open_file_id) => {
3560                let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3561                let mut used_ports = self.used_ports.lock().unwrap();
3562                used_ports.insert(port);
3563                let mut open_file_to_port = self.open_file_to_port.lock().unwrap();
3564                open_file_to_port.insert(open_file_id, port);
3565                R::AddUsedPort
3566            }
3567            GlobalRequest::ReleasePort(open_file_id) => {
3568                let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3569                let mut used_ports = self.used_ports.lock().unwrap();
3570                let mut open_file_to_port = self.open_file_to_port.lock().unwrap();
3571                let port = open_file_to_port.remove(&open_file_id);
3572                if let Some(port) = port {
3573                    used_ports.remove(&port);
3574                }
3575                R::ReleasePort(port)
3576            }
3577        };
3578
3579        // Awaited scheduler operations may have raced logical teardown. Never return their
3580        // operation-specific response after the sender acquired a permanent tombstone.
3581        // A SIGKILL committed meanwhile leaves the request unanswered, whatever
3582        // its operation-specific response, ThreadExited included.
3583        let (sender_became_terminal, sender_sigkill_retired) =
3584            if is_deregister || exec_reconnect.is_some() || is_exec_caller_after_local_mm_swap {
3585                (false, false)
3586            } else {
3587                let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(consuming_cleanup).await;
3588                (
3589                    sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid)
3590                        || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dtid, request_mm),
3591                    !answered_for_sigkill_victim && sched.is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim(dtid),
3592                )
3593            };
3594        if sender_sigkill_retired {
3595            return (None, R::Retired);
3596        }
3597        if resp == R::ThreadExited || sender_became_terminal {
3598            return (None, R::ThreadExited);
3599        }
3600
3601        let time_from_sched = self.global_time.lock().unwrap().threads_time(dtid);
3602        let time_update = match time_from_sched.cmp(&time_from_guest) {
3603            Ordering::Equal => None,
3604            Ordering::Less => {
3605                panic!(
3606                    "internal error: thread time should never go down, only monotonically up: time in sched {}, thread local time was {}",
3607                    time_from_sched, time_from_guest
3608                )
3609            }
3610            Ordering::Greater => Some(time_from_sched),
3611        };
3612        (time_update, resp)
3613    }
3614
3615    async fn recv_resources_with_origin(
3616        &self,
3617        from: Tid,
3618        detpid: DetPid,
3619        rs: Resources,
3620        request_mm: Option<MmId>,
3621        rpc: RpcOrigin,
3622        capability: ControlCapability,
3623    ) -> (SchedulerRpcResult<ResourceReply>, Option<LogicalTime>) {
3624        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(from.into()); // TODO(T78538674): FIXME
3625
3626        let resp2 = {
3627            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3628            if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
3629                || request_mm.is_some_and(|mm| !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm))
3630            {
3631                return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3632            }
3633            // A host-timed request (a background operation's rejoin) can pass
3634            // admission just before a SIGKILL commit retires its thread. The
3635            // handler's response exit turns this into an unanswered request.
3636            if sched.is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim(dettid) {
3637                return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3638            }
3639            let Some(nextturn) = sched.next_turns.get(&dettid).cloned() else {
3640                panic!(
3641                    "Detcore internal error: no entry for dettid {} in next_turns during resource request.",
3642                    dettid
3643                );
3644            };
3645            trace!(
3646                "[detcore, dtid {}] ResourceRequest, filling request into {}",
3647                &dettid, &nextturn.req
3648            );
3649            if let Some(mm) = request_mm
3650                && let Err(error) = sched.install_resource_origin(
3651                    dettid,
3652                    ResourceOrigin {
3653                        rpc,
3654                        mm,
3655                        control: capability,
3656                    },
3657                )
3658            {
3659                sched.fail_parked(dettid, error);
3660                return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3661            }
3662            sched.request_put(&nextturn.req, rs.clone(), &self.global_time);
3663            nextturn.resp
3664        };
3665        trace!(
3666            "[detcore, dtid {}] waiting on {} for resources: {:?}",
3667            dettid, &resp2, rs
3668        );
3669        let answer = resp2.get().await; // Block on the scheduler allowing our guest to proceed.
3670        self.finish_resource_response(from, detpid, rs, request_mm, answer)
3671            .await
3672    }
3673
3674    async fn finish_resource_response(
3675        &self,
3676        from: Tid,
3677        detpid: DetPid,
3678        rs: Resources,
3679        request_mm: Option<MmId>,
3680        answer: SchedResponse,
3681    ) -> (SchedulerRpcResult<ResourceReply>, Option<LogicalTime>) {
3682        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(from.as_raw());
3683        let request_became_stale = {
3684            let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3685            sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
3686                || request_mm.is_some_and(|mm| !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm))
3687        };
3688        if request_became_stale {
3689            // `logically_kill_thread` wakes an already-pending request with a
3690            // signal response.  Treat that wake-up as terminal: otherwise a
3691            // caller that ignores `ResumeStatus::Signaled` can inject the
3692            // original syscall after the thread was logically removed.
3693            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1023): Review pending SaBRe resource-request cancellation.
3694            trace!(
3695                "[detcore, dtid {}] terminating pending request after logical removal",
3696                dettid
3697            );
3698            return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3699        }
3700        if matches!(answer, SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm) {
3701            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3702            if !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
3703                || !sched.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(dettid, detpid, request_mm, &rs)
3704            {
3705                sched.fail_parked(dettid, ProtocolFailure::UnexpectedControl);
3706                return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3707            }
3708            return (
3709                SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::Grant(ResumeStatus::InGuestFatalAlarm)),
3710                None,
3711            );
3712        }
3713        // A control spends only this response transport, not the resource
3714        // operation. It must precede exit-group or normal grant side effects.
3715        if let SchedResponse::ObserveSignal(control) = answer {
3716            return (
3717                SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::ObserveSignal(control)),
3718                None,
3719            );
3720        }
3721        if let Some((true, process, mm)) = rs.exit_identity() {
3722            info!(
3723                "Scheduler authorized an exit-group scenario, from dettid {} / detpid {}",
3724                dettid, detpid
3725            );
3726            // Before allowing an `exit_group` to physically proceed, we
3727            // deregister the other threads in the thread group to reflect the
3728            // fact that they will not receive further logical turns.
3729            //
3730            // We trust the kernel to physically kill them irrespective of what they're
3731            // blocked on, including us having blocked them in the `futex_waiters` list.
3732            {
3733                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3734                if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
3735                    || request_mm.is_some_and(|mm| !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm))
3736                {
3737                    return (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None);
3738                }
3739                for tid in sched.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&dettid) {
3740                    // We don't need to do anything extra for our own thread. That can use the
3741                    // same mechanics as a normal exit:
3742                    if tid != dettid {
3743                        sched.logically_kill_thread(&tid, &process, mm);
3744                    }
3745                }
3746            }
3747        }
3748
3749        match answer {
3750            SchedResponse::ObserveSignal(_) | SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm => {
3751                self.sched
3752                    .lock()
3753                    .unwrap()
3754                    .fail_parked(dettid, ProtocolFailure::UnexpectedControl);
3755                (SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited, None)
3756            }
3757            // In this context, SchedValue
3758            SchedResponse::Go(Some(schedval)) => {
3759                trace!(
3760                    "[dtid {}] resources granted, resuming normally: {:?}",
3761                    dettid, rs
3762                );
3763
3764                let endtime_update = match schedval {
3765                    // Only syscalls timeout, and they don't need to update guest timeslice end.
3766                    // Nor does a futex requeue's answer, which a resource grant never carries.
3767                    SchedValue::TimeOut | SchedValue::Signaled(_) | SchedValue::Requeued { .. } => {
3768                        None
3769                    }
3770                    SchedValue::Value(timeslice) => Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(timeslice)),
3771                };
3772                (
3773                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::Grant(ResumeStatus::Normal)),
3774                    endtime_update,
3775                )
3776            }
3777            SchedResponse::GoAlone(schedval) => {
3778                trace!(
3779                    "[dtid {}] resources granted, and nothing else can run",
3780                    dettid
3781                );
3782                let endtime_update = match schedval {
3783                    Some(SchedValue::Value(timeslice)) => Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(timeslice)),
3784                    _ => None,
3785                };
3786                (
3787                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::Grant(
3788                        ResumeStatus::NothingElseCanRun,
3789                    )),
3790                    endtime_update,
3791                )
3792            }
3793            SchedResponse::Go(None) => {
3794                trace!(
3795                    "[dtid {}] resources granted but no timeslice specified",
3796                    dettid,
3797                );
3798                (
3799                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::Grant(ResumeStatus::Normal)),
3800                    None,
3801                )
3802            }
3803            SchedResponse::Signaled(signal) => {
3804                trace!(
3805                    "[dtid {}] resources granted but interrupted by signal",
3806                    dettid,
3807                );
3808                (
3809                    SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(ResourceReply::Grant(ResumeStatus::Signaled(
3810                        signal,
3811                    ))),
3812                    None,
3813                )
3814            }
3815        }
3816    }

3820        trace!("[detcore] Resources released to pid {}: {:?}", from, rs);

3823    async fn recv_release_all_resources(&self, from: Tid) {
