3828    /// Global portion of parent-forking-child protocol.  Called by the parent
3829    /// thread for an ordinary clone, or by the child itself for a vfork whose
3830    /// parent is blocked inside the kernel (`parent_is_kernel_blocked`).
3831    async fn recv_create_child_thread(
3832        &self,
3833        rpc_sender: Tid,
3834        request_mm: MmId,
3835        registration: ChildRegistration,
3836    ) -> SchedulerRpcResult<()> {
3837        let ChildRegistration {
3838            parent_dettid,
3839            parent_detpid,
3840            child_dettid,
3841            child_tid_addr: ctid,
3842            flags,
3843            exit_signal,
3844            physical_ids,
3845            maybe_priority,
3846            parent_is_kernel_blocked,
3847        } = registration;
3848        let initial_priority = if let Some(pr) = &self.preemptions_to_replay {
3849            assert!(maybe_priority.is_none());
3850            let prio = pr
3851                .thread_initial_priority(&child_dettid)
3852                .unwrap_or_else(|| {
3853                    warn!(
3854                        "Child thread {} not found in preemption history to replay",
3855                        child_dettid
3856                    );
3857                    DEFAULT_PRIORITY
3858                });
3859            if !is_ordinary_priority(prio) {
3860                panic!(
3861                    "Read a bad initial_prority from file: {}\nFull file: {}",
3862                    prio,
3863                    pr.load_all(),
3864                );
3865            }
3866            prio
3867        } else {
3868            let prio = maybe_priority.expect(
3869                "create_child_thread must take an initial priority unless replaying preemptions",
3870            );
3871            if !is_ordinary_priority(prio) {
3872                panic!(
3873                    "recv_create_child_thread received a bad prority argument : {}",
3874                    prio,
3875                );
3876            }
3877            prio
3878        };
3879
3880        {
3881            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
3882            let sender = DetTid::from_raw(rpc_sender.into());
3883            if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(sender)
3884                || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(sender, request_mm)
3885                || sched.thread_is_logically_killed(child_dettid)
3886            {
3887                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
3888            }
3889            // A process the backend already reported physically gone must not
3890            // be admitted: the scheduler would wait for a request it can never
3891            // send. A forked child is its own process.
3892            let child_detpid =
3893                if flags.is_some_and(|flags| flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_THREAD)) {
3894                    parent_detpid
3895                } else {
3896                    DetPid::from_raw(child_dettid.as_raw())
3897                };
3898            if self.cfg.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
3899                && sched.process_physically_gone(child_detpid)
3900            {
3901                drop(sched);
3902                self.report_backend_failure(reverie::BackendFailure {
3903                    pid: reverie::Pid::from_raw(child_detpid.as_raw()),
3904                    tid: Tid::from_raw(child_dettid.as_raw()),
3905                    phase: "a process was already physically gone when it was registered",
3906                });
3907                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
3908            }
3909
3910            if parent_is_kernel_blocked && self.cfg.sequentialize_threads {
3911                sched.complete_vfork_registration(parent_dettid, child_dettid);
3912            }
3913
3914            let child_mm = MmId::for_clone(
3915                request_mm,
3916                child_dettid,
3917                flags.is_some_and(|flags| flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_VM)),
3918            );
3919            sched.register_reused_transferred_exec_tid(child_dettid, child_mm);
3920            sched.record_thread_mm(child_dettid, child_mm);
3921            // The guest's procfs paths name a task by its thread ID in the
3922            // guest's PID namespace, which is the raw value of its DetTid.
3923            self.inodes
3924                .lock()
3925                .unwrap()
3926                .count_incarnation(child_dettid.as_raw());
3927
3928            // A new thread on a reused tid has not exited.
3929            sched.forget_committed_exit(child_dettid);
3930            // Don't fill in the request, as the child will do it:
3931            let _entry = sched
3932                .next_turns
3933                .entry(child_dettid)
3934                .or_insert_with(|| ThreadNextTurn {
3935                    dettid: child_dettid,
3936                    child_tid_addr: ctid,
3937                    req: Ivar::new(),
3938                    resp: Ivar::new(),
3939                    protocol: Default::default(),
3940                });
3941
3942            {
3943                let is_group_leader = if let Some(f) = flags {
3944                    !f.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_THREAD)
3945                } else {
3946                    true // root thread
3947                };
3948                sched.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
3949                    parent_dettid,
3950                    child_dettid,
3951                    is_group_leader,
3952                    flags.is_some_and(|flags| flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_PARENT)),
3953                    exit_signal,
3954                );
3955                if is_group_leader {
3956                    sched.forget_previous_process_exit(child_dettid);
3957                    // The child's exit signal is posted to its parent at a
3958                    // host-timed moment: that pair stops being observable now,
3959                    // before the child can run (4262 design §3.4).
3960                    sched.child_ends_timer_observability(child_dettid);
3961                }
3962                let new_pid_namespace = is_group_leader
3963                    && flags.is_some_and(|flags| flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWPID));
3964                if new_pid_namespace {
3965                    sched.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(child_dettid);
3966                    sched.thread_tree.mark_pid_namespace_init(child_dettid);
3967                }
3968                // A nested task's pid in each namespace is fixed now, in its
3969                // creator's turn, before either runs again
3970                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155).
3971                let pid_namespaces = &mut sched.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
3972                let mut chain = pid_namespaces.chain_of(parent_dettid);
3973                if new_pid_namespace {
3974                    chain.push(child_dettid);
3975                }
3976                if let Some(reason) = pid_namespaces.untranslatable(parent_dettid) {
3977                    let reason = format!("its creator {parent_dettid}: {reason}");
3978                    pid_namespaces.mark_untranslatable(child_dettid, reason);
3979                } else if chain.is_empty() {
3980                    pid_namespaces.forget(child_dettid);
3981                } else {
3982                    let recorded =
3983                        crate::scheduler::pid_namespaces::read_nspid(child_detpid, child_dettid)
3984                            .and_then(|nspid| {
3985                                pid_namespaces
3986                                    .record(child_dettid, &chain, &nspid)
3987                                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
3988                            });
3989                    if let Err(reason) = recorded {
3990                        error!(
3991                            "[detcore, dtid {}] cannot record its pids in its PID namespaces: {}",
3992                            child_dettid, reason
3993                        );
3994                        pid_namespaces.mark_untranslatable(child_dettid, reason);
3995                    } else if is_group_leader {
3996                        sched.note_member_of_ended_namespace(child_dettid);
3997                    }
3998                }
3999                if is_group_leader && flags.is_some() {
4000                    // A new process runs its creator's image until it execs.
4001                    let mut images = self.exec_images.lock().unwrap();
4002                    match images.get(&parent_detpid).cloned() {
4003                        Some(image) => images.insert(child_dettid, image),
4004                        None => images.remove(&child_dettid),
4005                    };
4006                    drop(images);
4007                    sched.inherit_real_time_records(parent_detpid, child_dettid);
4008                }
4009            }
4010
4011            if let Some((physical_pid, physical_tid)) = physical_ids {
4012                let child_is_thread =
4013                    flags.is_some_and(|flags| flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_THREAD));
4014                let child_detpid = if child_is_thread {
4015                    parent_detpid
4016                } else {
4017                    child_dettid
4018                };
4019                if let Err(open_error) = sched.register_physical_thread(
4020                    child_dettid,
4021                    child_mm,
4022                    physical_pid,
4023                    physical_tid,
4024                ) {
4025                    error!(
4026                        "[detcore, dtid {}] cannot bind host process {} thread {} during child registration: {}",
4027                        child_dettid, physical_pid, physical_tid, open_error,
4028                    );
4029                    sched.logically_kill_thread(&child_dettid, &child_detpid, child_mm);
4030                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4031                }
4032            }
4033
4034            // Bind only the existing root self-registration, after its
4035            // registration has succeeded. An arbitrary descendant's first
4036            // completion cannot claim a launcher-created input endpoint.
4037            if flags.is_none()
4038                && parent_dettid == child_dettid
4039                && parent_detpid == child_dettid
4040                && let Some(input) = self.inherited_input.lock().unwrap().as_mut()
4041                && input.root.is_none()
4042            {
4043                input.root = Some((child_dettid, child_mm));
4044            }
4045            // The same root self-registration names the thread whose first
4046            // image `Config::launch_image` describes.
4047            if flags.is_none() && parent_dettid == child_dettid && parent_detpid == child_dettid {
4048                let _ = self.root_dettid.set(child_dettid);
4049            }
4050
4051            // Record this thread in deterministic creation order so a
4052            // happens-before anchor addressed by `spawn_ordinal` resolves to it.
4053            sched.hb_note_spawn(child_dettid);
4054
4055            if self.cfg.replay_schedule_from.is_none() {
4056                // Give the thread an initial priority
4057                let old_prio = sched.priorities.insert(child_dettid, initial_priority);
4058                assert!(old_prio.is_none());
4059            } else {
4060                // In replay mode the schedule decides the thread's priority
4061                // (`Scheduler::replay_registration_priority`).
4062                if sched.replay_registration_priority(child_dettid, initial_priority) {
4063                    warn!(
4064                        "[detcore, dtid {}] registered before the replayed schedule switched to it, created by process {}; it takes its starting priority {}",
4065                        child_dettid, parent_detpid, initial_priority
4066                    );
4067                }
4068            }
4069
4070            if let Some(pr) = &mut sched.preemption_writer {
4071                pr.register_thread(child_dettid, initial_priority);
4072            }
4073
4074            // Describe *how* the admission side is chosen, but do not resolve it
4075            // (and in particular do not draw the post-fork PRNG) here: this
4076            // handler runs on whichever backend worker fielded the RPC, so on an
4077            // asynchronous backend (e.g. DBT, where the child self-registers
4078            // outside a scheduler turn) resolving the side now would consume the
4079            // PRNG draw in host RPC order. `admit_to_run_queue` resolves the
4080            // intent at the step2 drain -- which under ptrace is post-commit, in
4081            // schedule order, unchanged. Read its "What this does and does not
4082            // make deterministic" section before relying on that word: the drain
4083            // is a deterministic *point* and resolution within one drain is
4084            // `DetTid`-ordered, but on an asynchronous backend which drain a
4085            // given admission lands in is not itself schedule-determined unless
4086            // that admission is anchored (ordinary clone is, via the parent's
4087            // `ParentContinue`; vfork is, via `step2a`'s barrier). When threads
4088            // are not sequentialized, or the
4089            // parent is already kernel-blocked (vfork), the child takes the tail
4090            // and no PRNG is consumed.
4091            let intent = if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !parent_is_kernel_blocked {
4092                AdmitIntent::PostFork(self.cfg.runs_post_fork)
4093            } else {
4094                AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)
4095            };
4096            sched.admit_to_run_queue(child_dettid, intent);
4097            debug!(
4098                "[detcore] CreateChildThread with dtid {}: admit child via {:?}.",
4099                child_dettid, intent,
4100            );
4101            sched.started_up.try_put(());
4102        }
4103        // The child queue position above determines which equal-priority side
4104        // gets the first turn when the parent requests ParentContinue.
4105        // A vfork parent is already blocked by the kernel and is not in the run
4106        // queue, so it must not issue a ParentContinue request here.
4107        if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !parent_is_kernel_blocked {
4108            let mut rs = Resources::new(parent_detpid);
4109            rs.insert(
4110                ResourceID::ParentContinue {
4111                    parent: parent_dettid,
4112                    child: child_dettid,
4113                },
4114                Permission::W,
4115            );
4116            if matches!(
4117                self.recv_grant_resources(
4118                    rpc_sender,
4119                    parent_detpid,
4120                    rs,
4121                    Some(request_mm),
4122                    RpcOrigin::ParentContinue
4123                )
4124                .await
4125                .0,
4126                SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited
4127            ) {
4128                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4129            }
4130        }
4131        SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(())
4132    }
4133
4134    /// Called by the child thread upon startup.
4135    /// Returns a thread-preemption history for the new guest thread (if --replay-preemptions-from
4136    /// is used).
4137    async fn recv_start_new_thread(
4138        &self,
4139        from: Tid,
4140        dettid: DetTid,
4141        detpid: DetPid,
4142        request_mm: MmId,
4143        physical_ids: Option<(i32, i32)>,
4144        signal_identity: Option<reverie::SignalTaskIdentity>,
4145    ) -> SchedulerRpcResult<Option<ThreadHistory>> {
4146        let mut tries: u64 = 0;
4147        // TODO: eliminate this loop. Could instead signal with an ivar.
4148        let response_ivar = loop {
4149            yield_once().await;
4150            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4151            if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4152                || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, request_mm)
4153            {
4154                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4155            }
4156            if self.cfg.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
4157                && sched.process_physically_gone(detpid)
4158            {
4159                drop(sched);
4160                self.report_backend_failure(reverie::BackendFailure {
4161                    pid: reverie::Pid::from_raw(detpid.as_raw()),
4162                    tid: Tid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()),
4163                    phase: "a process was already physically gone when it started",
4164                });
4165                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4166            }
4167            if self.cfg.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals && physical_ids.is_none() {
4168                error!(
4169                    "[detcore, dtid {}] backend requires a host thread ID at StartNewThread",
4170                    dettid,
4171                );
4172                sched.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, request_mm);
4173                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4174            }
4175            // The resources that must be held for the fresh thread to run:
4176            let rsrcs = {
4177                let mut s = HashMap::new();
4178                s.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(detpid), Permission::RW); // TODO(T78055411): track mem aliasing.
4179                Resources {
4180                    tid: dettid,
4181                    resources: s,
4182                    poll_attempt: 0,
4183                    fyi: String::new(),
4184                    signal_interrupt_errno: None,
4185                    backend_runtime_bootstrap: false,
4186                    blocked_signal_mask: None,
4187                    blocked_signal_mask_unknown: false,
4188                    replay_served_from_log: false,
4189                    reads_signalfd: false,
4190                    read_fd: None,
4191                    polls_guest_state_only: false,
4192                    waits_until_nothing_else_can_run: false,
4193                    previous_attempt_made_progress: false,
4194                    upgraded_from_attempt: 0,
4195                    polls_channel: None,
4196                    poll_deadline: None,
4197                    in_guest_sleep_sigalrm: None,
4198                    signal_state_task: None,
4199                    decides_signal_interruption_itself: false,
4200                }
4201            };
4202            let nextturn = match sched.next_turns.entry(dettid) {
4203                Entry::Vacant(_entry) => {
4204                    // CreateChildThread on the parent hasn't run yet.
4205
4206                    // TODO: We could try to populate the entry since we get here
4207                    // first, but currently we lack the information right here to
4208                    // populate the child_tid_addr field.
4209                    if tries == 0 {
4210                        trace!(
4211                            "[detcore, dtid {}] thread showed up early, no queue entry yet.  Waiting...",
4212                            dettid
4213                        );
4214                    }
4215                    tries += 1;
4216                    continue;
4217                }
4218                Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
4219                    trace!(
4220                        "[detcore, dtid {}] handling StartNewThread rpc.  Found next_turns entry (after {} tries)",
4221                        from, tries
4222                    );
4223                    entry.get().clone()
4224                }
4225            };
4226            if let Some((physical_pid, physical_tid)) = physical_ids
4227                && let Err(open_error) =
4228                    sched.register_physical_thread(dettid, request_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
4229            {
4230                error!(
4231                    "[detcore, dtid {}] cannot bind host process {} thread {} for exact signal delivery: {}",
4232                    dettid, physical_pid, physical_tid, open_error,
4233                );
4234                sched.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, request_mm);
4235                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4236            }
4237            if sched.signal_control_installed() {
4238                let binding = signal_identity
4239                    .ok_or(TimerFailure::Identity)
4240                    .and_then(|identity| {
4241                        if from.as_raw() != dettid.as_raw()
4242                            || sched.registered_process(dettid) != Some(detpid)
4243                        {
4244                            return Err(TimerFailure::Identity);
4245                        }
4246                        sched.real_timers.bind(detpid, dettid, request_mm, identity)
4247                    });
4248                if let Err(error) = binding {
4249                    sched.fail_parked(dettid, ProtocolFailure::Timer(error));
4250                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4251                }
4252            }
4253            if let Err(error) = sched.install_resource_origin(
4254                dettid,
4255                ResourceOrigin {
4256                    rpc: RpcOrigin::ThreadStart,
4257                    mm: request_mm,
4258                    control: ControlCapability::None,
4259                },
4260            ) {
4261                sched.fail_parked(dettid, error);
4262                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4263            }
4264            sched.request_put(&nextturn.req, rsrcs, &self.global_time);
4265            break nextturn.resp;
4266        };
4267        debug!(
4268            "[detcore, dtid {}] New thread will now wait for response on {}...",
4269            &dettid, &response_ivar
4270        );
4271        let answer = response_ivar.get().await;
4272        if matches!(
4273            answer,
4274            SchedResponse::ObserveSignal(_) | SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm
4275        ) {
4276            self.sched
4277                .lock()
4278                .unwrap()
4279                .fail_parked(dettid, ProtocolFailure::UnexpectedControl);
4280            return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4281        }
4282        let request_became_stale = {
4283            let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4284            sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4285                || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, request_mm)
4286        };
4287        if request_became_stale {
4288            return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4289        }
4290        info!(
4291            "[detcore, dtid {}] New thread given go-ahead to proceed via {}",
4292            &dettid, &response_ivar
4293        );
4294        if let Some(pr) = &self.preemptions_to_replay {
4295            let (history, old_prio) = {
4296                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4297                if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4298                    || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, request_mm)
4299                {
4300                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4301                }
4302                let history = pr.extract_thread_record(&dettid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
4303                    warn!(
4304                        "Replaying preemptions, but no record found for thread {}",
4305                        dettid
4306                    );
4307                    ThreadHistory::new()
4308                });
4309                let old_prio = sched.priorities.insert(dettid, history.initial_priority());
4310                (history, old_prio)
4311            };
4312            debug!(
4313                "[replay-preemption] Enqueing new thread at priority {:?} (changed from {:?})",
4314                history.initial_priority(),
4315                old_prio,
4316            );
4317            SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(Some(history))
4318        } else {
4319            SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(None)
4320        }
4321    }
4322
4323    /// Warning: this happens completely asynchronously, whenever the guest exit hook fires.
4324    /// Its timing is not coordinated by the scheduler.
4325    async fn recv_deregister_thread(&self, _from: Tid, mut deregistration: ThreadDeregistration) {
4326        // Keep the same scheduler -> pending-exec lock order as reconnect.
4327        let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
4328        let ThreadDeregistration {
4329            dettid, detpid, mm, ..
4330        } = &deregistration;
4331        // A fatal signal can tear down the caller after its local state has advanced to the
4332        // candidate exec image but before the successful reconnect (or failed-exec cancel).
4333        // Retire that one-shot preparation before scheduler-incarnation admission rejects the
4334        // candidate image's final cleanup RPC.
4335        let mut pending = self.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap();
4336        if pending.get(detpid).is_some_and(|state| {
4337            state.caller == *dettid && (*mm == state.mm || *mm == state.mm.for_exec(state.process))
4338        }) {
4339            let prepared = pending.remove(detpid).unwrap();
4340            // Unlike a recoverable failure (CancelExec), the caller's old image
4341            // deregistered before any reconnect: its group is dying, and Linux
4342            // walks every robust list of the group, in the exec or in each
4343            // thread's exit. On DBT this takes a fatal signal during the exec.
4344            // An exec whose target the kernel cannot load does not get here:
4345            // DynamoRIO's own exec succeeds, the new image reconnects and its
4346            // wakes are queued there, and the run then hangs on that image's
4347            // unretired death (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362).
4348            // Hold turns until the kernel has ended the group, as an
4349            // exit_group's grant does, and wake the prepared waiters now, while
4350            // the caller's outstanding exec request still withholds every turn;
4351            // they run at the drain after the hold. A group that outlives this
4352            // is ended by the exited-thread valve with a named HERMIT_DEADLOCK
4353            // rather than losing the wakes (Codex review of
4354            // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4352, P2).
4355            if !prepared.fd_blocking.robust_wakes.is_empty() {
4356                sched.hold_turns_until_the_group_ends(*detpid);
4357                wake_exec_robust_waiters(
4358                    &mut sched,
4359                    &prepared.fd_blocking.robust_wakes,
4360                    "terminal exec",
4361                );
4362            }
4363            sched.finish_exec_teardown(prepared.caller, *detpid, prepared.mm, false);
4364            // The local caller can have installed its candidate exec MmId
4365            // before cancellation. It still owns the original registration;
4366            // consume that exact prepared incarnation rather than discarding
4367            // cleanup as a stale request after removing the preparation.
4368            deregistration.mm = prepared.mm;
4369        }
4370        drop(pending);
4371
4372        // Invariant: will only be called when sequentialize-threads is on.
4373        assert!(self.cfg.sequentialize_threads);
4374        self.account_deregistered_thread(&mut sched, deregistration);
4375    }
4376
4377    /// Consume final statistics and registration while holding admission closed.
4378    /// Authenticated exec cleanup uses this same once-only accounting path.
4379    fn account_deregistered_thread(
4380        &self,
4381        sched: &mut Scheduler,
4382        deregistration: ThreadDeregistration,
4383    ) {
4384        let ThreadDeregistration {
4385            dettid,
4386            detpid,
4387            mm,
4388            thread_start_entered: _,
4389            timeslice_stats,
4390            syscall_count,
4391            chaos_epochs,
4392        } = deregistration;
4393        if !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm) {
4394            debug!(
4395                "[detcore, dtid {}] ignoring deregistration from retired exec incarnation {:?}",
4396                dettid, mm,
4397            );
4398            return;
4399        }
4400        self.post_exec_fd_blocking.lock().unwrap().remove(&dettid);
4401        // A SIGKILL victim's cleanup is accounted exactly once
4402        // (`scheduler::sigkill_retirement`), also on a backend that otherwise
4403        // accepts a repeated callback.
4404        if !sched.note_deregistration_accounted(dettid)
4405            || sched.sigkill_receipt_already_counted(dettid)
4406        {
4407            trace!(
4408                "[detcore, dtid {}] acknowledging already-accounted deregistration",
4409                dettid
4410            );
4411            return;
4412        }
4413        if let Some(writer) = &mut sched.preemption_writer {
4414            for transition in chaos_epochs {
4415                writer.insert_chaos_epoch(dettid, transition);
4416            }
4417        }
4418        sched.record_timeslice_stats(dettid, timeslice_stats);
4419        sched.record_syscall_count(dettid, syscall_count);
4420        // A SIGKILL victim is retired at its sender's turn, not here
4421        // (`scheduler::sigkill_retirement`): its receipt is accounted above
4422        // and only counted.
4423        if sched.route_sigkill_receipt(dettid)
4424            != crate::scheduler::sigkill_retirement::SigkillReceipt::Ordinary
4425        {
4426            return;
4427        }
4428        sched.retire_deregistered_thread(dettid, detpid, mm);
4429        trace!(
4430            "[detcore, dtid {}] thread deregistered, removed from sched structures.",
4431            dettid
4432        );
4433    }
4434
4435    async fn recv_futex_action(
4436        &self,
4437        caller: RpcIncarnation,
4438        action: FutexAction,
4439        futexid: FutexID,
4440        init_read: i32,
4441        mask: u32,
4442    ) -> Option<SchedValue> {
4443        let RpcIncarnation { dettid, mm } = caller;
4444        trace!("[detcore, dtid {}] Futex action: {:?}", &dettid, action);
4445        let response_iv = {
4446            let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4447            if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4448                || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm)
4449            {
4450                return Some(SchedValue::Value(nix::errno::Errno::EINTR as u64));
4451            }
4452            let Some(resp_iv) = sched
4453                .next_turns
4454                .get(&dettid)
4455                .map(|nextturn| nextturn.resp.clone())
4456            else {
4457                // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4458                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review late RPCs from exit-group siblings.
4459                trace!(
4460                    "[detcore, dtid {}] ignoring futex action after logical thread removal",
4461                    dettid
4462                );
4463                return Some(SchedValue::Value(nix::errno::Errno::EINTR as u64));
4464            };
4465            match action {
4466                FutexAction::WaitRequest(maybe_timeout, signal_watch) => {
4467                    if sched.child_tid_was_cleared(futexid, init_read) {
4468                        trace!(
4469                            "[detcore, dtid {}] late wait on cleared child-TID futex {:?}",
4470                            dettid, futexid
4471                        );
4472                        return Some(SchedValue::Value(0));
4473                    }
4474                    if let Err(error) = sched.install_resource_origin(
4475                        dettid,
4476                        ResourceOrigin {
4477                            rpc: RpcOrigin::FutexAction,
4478                            mm,
4479                            control: ControlCapability::None,
4480                        },
4481                    ) {
4482                        sched.fail_parked(dettid, error);
4483                        return Some(SchedValue::Value(nix::errno::Errno::EINTR as u64));
4484                    }
4485                    sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&dettid, futexid, maybe_timeout, mask, signal_watch);
4486                    // block on ivar, below
4487                }
4488                FutexAction::WaitFinished => {
4489                    return None;
4490                }
4491                FutexAction::WakeRequest(num_threads) => {
4492                    let num = sched.wake_futex_waiters(dettid, futexid, num_threads, mask);
4493                    if self.cfg.yields_after_futex_wake(num) {
4494                        sched.requeue_futex_waker(dettid);
4495                    }
4496                    return Some(SchedValue::Value(num));
4497                }
4498                FutexAction::WakeFinished(_num_threads) => {
4499                    return None;
4500                }
4501                FutexAction::RequeueRequest(to, nr_wake, nr_requeue) => {
4502                    let (woken, moved) = sched.requeue_futex_waiters(
4503                        futexid,
4504                        to,
4505                        nr_wake as usize,
4506                        nr_requeue as usize,
4507                    );
4508                    if self.cfg.yields_after_futex_wake(woken) {
4509                        sched.requeue_futex_waker(dettid);
4510                    }
4511                    return Some(SchedValue::Requeued { woken, moved });
4512                }
4513            }
4514            // Blocking on the FUTEX_WAIT here, remove ourselves:
4515            assert!(sched.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
4516            resp_iv
4517        };
4518        // Wait for wake+scheduler response.
4519        match response_iv.get().await {
4520            // A futex wait never asks for `GoAlone`.
4521            SchedResponse::Go(answer) | SchedResponse::GoAlone(answer) => {
4522                trace!(
4523                    "[detcore, dtid {}] Unblocked from futex_wait! ({})",
4524                    &dettid, &response_iv
4525                );
4526                answer
4527            }
4528            SchedResponse::Signaled(signals) => Some(SchedValue::Signaled(
4529                signals.iter().flatten().fold(0, |set, signal| {
4530                    set | crate::scheduler::kernel_signal_bit(signal.0)
4531                }),
4532            )),
4533            SchedResponse::ObserveSignal(_) | SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm => {
4534                self.sched
4535                    .lock()
4536                    .unwrap()
4537                    .fail_parked(dettid, ProtocolFailure::UnexpectedControl);
4538                self.wait_for_backend_failure().await;
4539                futures::future::pending().await
4540            }
4541        }
4542    }
4543
4544    fn recv_robust_list_wakes(&self, from: DetTid, wakes: Vec<(DetTid, FutexID)>) -> Vec<u64> {
4545        let mut sched = self.sched.lock().unwrap();
4546        if sched.retain_sigkill_victim_wakes(from, &wakes) {
4547            // A SIGKILL victim's batch runs with its cohort; the empty answer
4548            // has no counts, so the victim logs nothing for it.
4549            return Vec::new();
4550        }
4551        sched.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&wakes)
4552    }
4553
4554    /// The epoch as a logical time: the virtual mtime of a file first seen
4555    /// with a non-canonical host mtime.
4556    fn epoch_logical_time(&self) -> LogicalTime {
4557        let nanos = self
4558            .cfg
4559            .epoch
4560            .timestamp_nanos_opt()
4561            .expect("epoch cannot be represented in a timestamp with nanosecond precision")
4562            as u64;
4563        LogicalTime::from_nanos(nanos)
4564    }
4565
4566    async fn recv_determinize_inode(
4567        &self,
4568        from: Tid,
4569        ino: RawInode,
4570        procfs: Option<ProcfsName>,
4571        observed: ObservedMtime,
4572        sighting: InodeSighting,
4573    ) -> (DetInode, LogicalTime) {
4574        let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4575        // Here we establish a policy that when we first see a file its mtime is
4576        // the epoch, unless its host mtime is one of the canonical values in
4577        // `CANONICAL_FILE_MTIME_SECONDS`, which it keeps.
4578        let epoch = self.epoch_logical_time();
4579        let mut pool = self.inodes.lock().unwrap();
4580        if let Some(name) = procfs {
4581            let path = pool.procfs_path_key(&name);
4582            pool.procfs_key(ino, path);
4583        }
4584        let (dino, ns) = pool.add_sighted_inode(ino, observed, epoch, sighting);
4585        drop(pool);
4586        trace!(
4587            "[detcore, dtid {}] resolved (raw) inode {:?} to {:?}, mtime {}",
4588            from, ino, dino, ns
4589        );
4590        (dino, ns)
4591    }

4725    async fn recv_trace_schedevent(
4726        &self,
4727        ev: SchedEvent,
4728        detpid: DetPid,
4729        request_mm: MmId,
4730        command_bootstrap: bool,
4731    ) -> SchedulerRpcResult<TraceSchedEventResponse> {
4732        let ev = {
4733            let sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4734            if !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(ev.dettid, request_mm) {
4735                return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4736            }
4737            // TODO(T124316762): debug address randomization in the tracer and get rid of this hack:
4738            let ev = {
4739                if self.past_first_execve.load(SeqCst) {
4740                    ev
4741                } else {
4742                    info!(
4743                        "Warning: erasing rip of pre-execve sched event! {:?}",
4744                        SchedEventForLog {
4745                            event: &ev,
4746                            command_bootstrap
4747                        }
4748                    );
4749                    SchedEvent {
4750                        end_rip: None,
4751                        start_rip: None,
4752                        ..ev
4753                    }
4754                }
4755            };
4756            // Future trace_schedevent calls will retain their rip values.
4757            if ev.op == Op::Syscall(Sysno::execve, SyscallPhase::Prehook) {
4758                self.past_first_execve.store(true, SeqCst);
4759            }
4760            ev
4761        };
4762
4763        // Yield this guest thread if needed to follow schedule.
4764        let result = if self.cfg.replay_schedule_from.is_some() {
4765            let (consumed, print_stack2) = {
4766                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4767                if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(ev.dettid)
4768                    || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(ev.dettid, request_mm)
4769                {
4770                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4771                }
4772                let consumed = sched.consume_schedevent(&ev);
4773                let print_stack2 = if self.cfg.record_preemptions {
4774                    sched.record_event(&ev)
4775                } else {
4776                    None
4777                };
4778                (consumed, print_stack2)
4779            };
4780            let ConsumeResult {
4781                keep_running,
4782                print_stack,
4783                event_ix: _,
4784                timeslice_remaining: mut end_of_timeslice,
4785            } = consumed;
4786            trace!(
4787                "keep_running :{}, end_of_timeslice: {:?}",
4788                keep_running, end_of_timeslice
4789            );
4790
4791            if !keep_running {
4792                trace!(
4793                    "[detcore, dtid {}] Thread yielding to follow replay schedule",
4794                    &ev.dettid,
4795                );
4796                let tid = reverie::Tid::from(ev.dettid.as_raw()); // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
4797                let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(ev.dettid);
4798                rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::TraceReplay, Permission::RW);
4799                let (response, timeslice) = self
4800                    .recv_grant_resources(
4801                        tid,
4802                        detpid,
4803                        rsrcs,
4804                        Some(request_mm),
4805                        RpcOrigin::TraceSchedEvent,
4806                    )
4807                    .await;
4808                if response == SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited {
4809                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4810                }
4811                end_of_timeslice = timeslice;
4812                trace!(
4813                    "[detcore, dtid {}] Thread reactivated after yielding for replay schedule",
4814                    &ev.dettid,
4815                );
4816            }
4817
4818            TraceSchedEventResponse {
4819                print_stack_strace: print_stack.or(print_stack2),
4820                timeslice: end_of_timeslice,
4821            }
4822        } else {
4823            let print_stack_strace = {
4824                let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4825                if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(ev.dettid)
4826                    || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(ev.dettid, request_mm)
4827                {
4828                    return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4829                }
4830                if self.cfg.record_preemptions {
4831                    sched.record_event(&ev)
4832                } else {
4833                    None
4834                }
4835            };
4836            TraceSchedEventResponse {
4837                print_stack_strace,
4838                timeslice: None,
4839            }
4840        };
4841
4842        if result.print_stack_strace.is_some()
4843            && let Some(sig) = &self.cfg.stacktrace_signal
4844        {
4845            let _sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4846            trace!(
4847                "[dtid {}] signaling thread with {} at the point of stack trace printing.",
4848                ev.dettid, sig.0
4849            );
4850            let tid = Pid::from_raw(ev.dettid.as_raw());
4851            // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
4852            // We send a raw signal here and let the guest pick it up WHENEVER it resumes.
4853            // We don't use the "signal_guest" method because we don't necessarily respect that
4854            // protocol here.
4855            // Alarm/timer signals are guest-chosen and may be realtime, which
4856            // `nix` cannot name; fall through to the raw syscall for those.
4857            match sig.signal() {
4858                Some(named) => signal::kill(tid, named).unwrap(),
4859                None => {
4860                    // SAFETY: `tid` is a live thread this scheduler owns and
4861                    // `sig.raw()` is a signal number the guest already supplied.
4862                    let rc = unsafe { libc::kill(tid.as_raw(), sig.raw()) };
4863                    assert_eq!(rc, 0, "raw kill of signal {} failed", sig.raw());
4864                }
4865            }
4866        }
4867
4868        SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(result)
4869    }

4871    // Ephemeral port range is in file /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range"
4872    // This function reads from the file and returns the range
4873    // Start of range is at index 0, end of range is at index 1.
4874    fn read_port_range() -> Vec<u16> {
4875        let contents = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range")
4876            .expect("File should be present");
4877        let range: Vec<u16> = contents
4878            .split_whitespace()
4879            .filter_map(|number| number.parse().ok())
4880            .collect();
4881        range
4882    }

4884    // Reflect ephemeral port range updated outside of the tracer program internally.
4885    fn update_port_range(&self) {
4886        let range = Self::read_port_range();
4887        self.port_start_range.store(range[0], SeqCst);
4888        self.port_end_range.store(range[1], SeqCst);
4889    }

4913                SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited

4920    /// Register, re-arm, or disarm a POSIX timer in the global scheduler.
4921    /// `notification` is the timer's signal and, for a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID`
4922    /// timer, the thread it notifies.
4923    async fn recv_register_posix_timer(
4924        &self,
4925        detpid: DetPid,
4926        caller: RpcIncarnation,
4927        timer_id: i32,
4928        deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
4929        interval: LogicalTime,
4930        notification: PosixTimerNotification,
4931    ) -> SchedulerRpcResult<()> {
4932        let PosixTimerNotification {
4933            sig,
4934            thread,
4935            value,
4936            deleted,
4937        } = notification;
4938        let RpcIncarnation { dettid, mm } = caller;
4939        let mut sched = self.lock_rpc_scheduler(false).await;
4940        if sched.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid) || !sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(dettid, mm) {
4941            return SchedulerRpcResult::ThreadExited;
4942        }
4943        // A process-directed timer prefers the thread that armed it.
4944        let target = match thread {
4945            Some(thread) => SignalTarget::Thread(thread),
4946            None => SignalTarget::Process(dettid),
4947        };
4948        sched.note_posix_timer_notification(detpid, timer_id, sig.raw(), value, deleted);
4949        sched.register_posix_timer(
4950            detpid,
4951            target,
4952            timer_id,
4953            deadline,
4954            interval,
4955            match sig.signal() {
4956                Some(signal) => signal.into(),
4957                None => crate::scheduler::timed_waiters::TimerSignal::RefuseRealTime(sig.raw()),
4958            },
4959        );
4960        SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(())
4961    }
4962}

4992/// A question about, or a record in, the scheduler's ledger of guest-handled
4993/// SIGALRMs (`Scheduler::sigalrm_control`), sent by a guest's Detcore in the
4994/// calling thread's turn before the call reaches the kernel. Signal phase 1
4995/// refuses each of these with EPERM while it could reach a process that
4996/// handles SIGALRM.
4997#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
4998pub enum SigalrmControl {
4999    /// A send of SIGALRM to the process of this thread.
5000    SendTo(DetTid),
5001    /// A send of SIGALRM to a process the caller cannot name to Detcore: a
5002    /// pidfd with no recorded target (`pidfd_open` records one).
5003    SendToUnnamed,
5004    /// An arming of a kernel producer of SIGALRM that Detcore does not
5005    /// emulate through its alarm path (a POSIX timer, `F_SETSIG` or
5006    /// `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`), or of a file lease, which makes another process's
5007    /// open wait for the lease break with no scheduler admission. Recorded
5008    /// when allowed, so a later handler installation can be refused.
5009    ArmProducer,
5010    /// An arming of a recurring `ITIMER_REAL` (nonzero interval), which phase 1
5011    /// does not model for a handling process.
5012    ArmRecurringTimer,
5013    /// The caller, in a process that handles SIGALRM, is about to run
5014    /// synchronous I/O on inherited stdio, which may sleep with no scheduler
5015    /// admission. Never refused: a SIGALRM already due is recorded as a
5016    /// determinism loss (design closure 1).
5017    UnadmittedStdioIo,
5018    /// Before a guest SIGALRM handler is installed in the caller's process
5019    /// (phase 1 step I3, design section 6): refused once any guest armed a
5020    /// kernel producer of SIGALRM, anywhere in the run.
5021    InstallHandler,
5022    /// Before the caller's process changes its SIGALRM handler to `SIG_DFL`:
5023    /// refused while the process has a pending entry, which would take the
5024    /// default action inside the callback (design section 6).
5025    HandlerToDefault,
5026    /// Whether the caller's process has a pending entry, for `rt_sigpending`
5027    /// ("refused" is true when it has one). Never changes anything.
5028    PendingEntry,
5029    /// Records the caller's process's SIGALRM disposition and the caller's
5030    /// "SIGALRM virtually blocked" bit, after its runtime changed them inside
5031    /// this turn. Never refused.
5032    Publish {
5033        /// Whether the process's SIGALRM disposition is a guest handler.
5034        handled: bool,
5035        /// Whether the caller's virtual mask blocks SIGALRM.
5036        blocked: bool,
5037    },
5038    /// Records the caller's "SIGALRM virtually blocked" bit, after its runtime
5039    /// changed its mask inside this turn. Never refused.
5040    PublishBlocked(bool),
5041    /// Whether the caller's process has an entry that is due for the caller
5042    /// (its SIGALRM not virtually blocked; "refused" is true when it has one).
5043    /// Never changes anything.
5044    DueEntry,
5045    /// Takes the caller's process's entry for delivery to the caller, if it
5046    /// is still pending, handled and due ("refused" is true when taken), in
5047    /// the turn of the delivery's `InboundSignal` request (step I4, design
5048    /// section 4, step 3).
5049    TakeEntry,
5050    /// Records a determinism loss for the caller's process, here in the
5051    /// coordinator, where the verifier reads it: the runtime could not
5052    /// deliver an entry the caller took (or could not tell the caller's
5053    /// virtual mask). The caller then stops the process. Never refused.
5054    DeliveryLost,
5055    /// Records a determinism loss for the caller's process, here in the
5056    /// coordinator: the caller delivers an entry before a syscall that has
5057    /// not run (the I4 addendum's point c), whose handler cannot be shown the
5058    /// registers Linux would show it (Reverie restores rcx and r11 as the
5059    /// `syscall` instruction already wrote them). The delivery goes ahead and
5060    /// the run continues; verification refuses to compare it. Never refused.
5061    EntryDeliveryUnfaithful,
5062}

5067/// without `PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD`) or one thread (tkill, tgkill,

5076    /// The send named one thread.
5077    Thread,
5078}

5113    /// Report a terminal violation of the parked continuation protocol.

5115    /// Report an actual signal removed from this process's pending set.

5129    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-643): Review this new Detcore global RPC request.
5130    /// Add a syscall to the run-wide unsupported-use summary.
5131    ReportUnsupportedSyscall(String),

5592/// Responses from the global object
5593#[allow(missing_docs, clippy::unit_arg)]
5594#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
5595pub enum GlobalResponse {
5596    /// The scheduler permanently removed this raw TID. Guest-side RPC handling retires
5597    /// this task without cancelling a live group-exit issuer or resuming the operation.
5598    ThreadExited,
5599    /// A reply, with the virtual time that remained before the earliest
5600    /// pending deadline when the thread was granted the turn it resumes, or
5601    /// armed a timer (`Scheduler::deadline_remaining_from`). Unwrapped by
5602    /// `send_and_update_time`, which caps the thread's slice there.
5603    WithDeadline(Duration, Box<GlobalResponse>),
5604    RequestResources(ResumeStatus),
5605    ParkedRequest(ResourceReply),
5606    ResumeParkedRequest(ResourceReply),
5607    FinishParkedObservation(Result<FinishAck, ProtocolFailure>),
5608    SignalDequeued {
5609        ack: Result<DequeueAck, TimerFailure>,
5610        terminal: bool,
5611    },
5612    ReleaseResources(()),
5613    ReleaseAllResources(()),
5614    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-643): Review this new Detcore global RPC response.
5615    ReportUnsupportedSyscall(()),
5616    PolicyRefusal(()),
5617    PrepareExec(()),
5618    CancelExec(()),
5619    ReconnectExec(bool),
5620    ResumeExec(ResumeStatus, Option<LogicalTime>),
5621    RetireExec(bool),
5622    MarkPastFirstExecve(Box<ExecFdState>),

5774/// `request`, carrying the number of records this guest thread produced for
5775/// forwarding since its previous counted request when there are any
5776/// (`GlobalRequest::WithForwardedCount`). A thread of a backend whose Tool does
5777/// not forward records never has any, so its requests are unchanged.
5778pub(crate) fn counted_request(request: GlobalRequest) -> GlobalRequest {
5779    match crate::detlog::take_forwarded_since_request() {
5780        0 => request,
5781        produced => GlobalRequest::WithForwardedCount(produced, Box::new(request)),
5782    }
5783}

5785/// The global request that carries one shared open file control message. It
5786/// is answered before any clock accounting, so its clock and address-space
5787/// fields are placeholders. The sender is the thread the backend's transport
5788/// names for the request; for in-guest LiteInst that is the runtime's own
5789/// envelope, checked against the connecting process at admission, on a
5790/// connection the guest cannot write to.
5791pub fn shared_open_file_request(control: OpenFileControl) -> (DetTime, MmId, GlobalRequest) {
5792    (
5793        DetTime::default(),
5794        MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(0)),
5795        GlobalRequest::SharedOpenFile(control),
5796    )
5797}
5798
5799/// The answer to a [`shared_open_file_request`].
5800pub fn shared_open_file_reply(
5801    response: (Option<LogicalTime>, GlobalResponse),
5802) -> Result<OpenFileControlReply, SharedOpenFileError> {
5803    match response {
5804        (None, GlobalResponse::SharedOpenFile(reply)) => reply,
5805        other => Err(SharedOpenFileError(format!(
5806            "unexpected answer to a shared open file control message: {other:?}"
5807        ))),
5808    }
5809}

5825// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5826// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1154): Review the SaBRe exec descriptor-status handoff.
5827/// Notifies the coordinator that `guest` is about to `execve`, recording the
5828/// pre-exec address space `mm` and any file-descriptor blocking overrides. A
5829/// backend that handles `execve` outside Detcore's syscall handler must call
5830/// this before the native syscall so the next image reconnects to the existing
5831/// scheduler identity and logical clock.
5832///
5833/// `robust_wakes` are the owner-death wakes a successful exec makes Linux
5834/// deliver, from [`Detcore::exec_robust_list_wakes`], where the backend runs
5835/// the native execve outside Detcore's handler; the coordinator delivers them
5836/// at the new image's reconnect, or when the caller's thread ends without
5837/// one, and drops them at [`cancel_exec`]. A backend whose execve Detcore handles stages
5838/// them in its own thread state instead and passes none.
5839///
5840/// `exe` is the image the exec runs, where the caller resolved it
5841/// ([`crate::exec_record::ExecRecord::resolve`]); the new image's
5842/// `/proc/<pid>/exe` link answers from it.
5843pub async fn prepare_exec<G, T>(
5844    guest: &mut G,
5845    mm: MmId,
5846    fd_blocking: ExecFdBlockingOverrides,
5847    robust_wakes: Vec<(DetTid, FutexID)>,
5848    exe: Option<crate::exec_record::ExecRecord>,
5849) where
5850    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5851    T: RecordOrReplay,
5852{
5853    let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
5854    let fd_state = ExecFdState {
5855        blocking: fd_blocking,
5856        inherited_reads: guest.thread_state().inherited_reads_for_exec(),
5857        initialize_inherited_stdio: false,
5858        initial_input: None,
5859        robust_wakes,
5860        open_files: guest
5861            .thread_state()
5862            .shared_open_files_for_exec()
5863            .expect("prepared exec descriptors are no longer live"),
5864        channels: Default::default(),
5865        open_file_namespace: None,
5866        exe,
5867    };
5868    // `--pipe-wake-latency` on a backend that rediscovers its descriptors
5869    // after exec: carry the channels, and reserve the old numbering at every
5870    // exec (`crate::pipe_wake`).
5871    let fd_state = if guest.config().pipe_wake_latency_in_effect().is_some()
5872        && guest.config().backend.rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec
5873    {
5874        ExecFdState {
5875            channels: guest.thread_state().pipe_channels_for_exec(),
5876            open_file_namespace: Some(guest.thread_state().open_file_namespace_for_exec()),
5877            ..fd_state
5878        }
5879    } else {
5880        fd_state
5881    };
5882    let (_, response) = send_and_update_time(
5883        guest,
5884        GlobalRequest::PrepareExec(detpid, mm, Box::new(fd_state)),
5885    )
5886    .await;
5887    assert_eq!(response, GlobalResponse::PrepareExec(()));
5888}

5890/// Cancels a matching [`prepare_exec`] after a native exec fails. Call this
5891/// before returning to the old image, preserving its thread state and address
5892/// space identity so frozen siblings can resume without an exec transition.
5893pub async fn cancel_exec<G, T>(guest: &mut G)
5894where
5895    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5896    T: RecordOrReplay,
5897{
5898    let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
5899    let (_, response) = send_and_update_time(guest, GlobalRequest::CancelExec(detpid)).await;
5900    assert_eq!(response, GlobalResponse::CancelExec(()));
5901}

5903pub async fn mark_past_first_execve<G, T>(guest: &mut G)
5904where
5905    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5906    T: RecordOrReplay,
5907{
5908    let controlled =
5909        guest.signal_control_mode() == reverie::BackendSignalControlMode::ToolControlled;
5910    let signal_identity = controlled.then(|| guest.signal_task_identity()).flatten();
5911    let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
5912    // The device and inode of the file the kernel's `exe` link names for the
5913    // new image, which the coordinator checks the exec's record against.
5914    let kernel_image = crate::syscalls::guest_task_procfs(
5915        &guest.config().backend,
5916        guest.tid().as_raw(),
5917        guest
5918            .thread_state()
5919            .changed_root
5920            .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
5921    )
5922    .and_then(|task| std::fs::metadata(task.join("exe")).ok())
5923    .map(|meta| {
5924        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
5925        (meta.dev(), meta.ino())
5926    });
5927    let (_, response) = send_and_update_time(
5928        guest,
5929        GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(detpid, signal_identity, kernel_image),
5930    )
5931    .await;
5932    let mut overrides = match response {
5933        GlobalResponse::MarkPastFirstExecve(overrides) => *overrides,
5934        _ => unreachable!(),
5935    };
5936    if controlled {
5937        guest.thread_state_mut().signal_task_identity = signal_identity;
5938    }
5939    // The new image's `/proc/<pid>/exe` link answers from its record, or
5940    // without one is the kernel's.
5941    guest.thread_state_mut().exe = overrides.exe.take().map(Arc::new);
5942    if !overrides.is_empty() {
5943        if let Some(open_files) = &overrides.open_files {
5944            guest
5945                .thread_state_mut()
5946                .set_open_file_creator(open_files.creator);
5947        } else if let Some((creator, _)) = overrides.open_file_namespace {
5948            // `--pipe-wake-latency`: continue the old numbering, as the
5949            // random-device survivors above do.
5950            guest.thread_state_mut().set_open_file_creator(creator);
5951        }
5952        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
5953        let metadata = Arc::clone(&guest.thread_state().file_metadata);
5954        metadata
5955            .lock()
5956            .unwrap()
5957            .apply_exec_fd_state(
5958                dettid,
5959                overrides,
5960                guest.config().backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table,
5961            )
5962            .expect("prepared exec descriptor provenance no longer matches the guest table");
5963    }
5964}

6130
6131pub async fn send_and_update_time<G, T>(
6132    guest: &mut G,
6133    request: GlobalRequest,
6134) -> (Option<LogicalTime>, GlobalResponse)
6135where
6136    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6137    T: RecordOrReplay,
6138{
6139    // The successful exec callback must bind a surviving worker to its new
6140    // backend TID before issuing ordinary replacement-image requests. In
6141    // particular, a missed reconnect must not turn ThreadExited into exit(0).
6142    // Consuming cancellation and the reconnect itself use their authenticated
6143    // direct RPC paths instead of this ordinary-request helper.
6144    assert_eq!(
6145        DetTid::from_raw(guest.tid().as_raw()),
6146        guest.thread_state().dettid,
6147        "replacement image must reconnect before ordinary RPCs"
6148    );
6149    let mytime = guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time.clone();
6150    let mm = guest.thread_state().mm_id;
6151    let mut resp = guest.send_rpc((mytime, mm, counted_request(request))).await;
6152    let deadline = match resp.1 {
6153        GlobalResponse::WithDeadline(remaining, response) => {
6154            resp.1 = *response;
6155            Some(remaining)
6156        }
6157        _ => None,
6158    };
6159    guest.thread_state_mut().last_grant_deadline = deadline;
6160    cap_timeslice_at_deadline(guest, deadline);
6161    if resp.1 == GlobalResponse::Retired {
6162        // A committed SIGKILL victim (`Scheduler::is_unaccounted_sigkill_victim`):
6163        // this callback never resumes. No error, errno or injection reaches
6164        // the backend; its terminal owner consumes the real death.
6165        trace!(
6166            "[detcore, dtid {}] waiting for the kernel to end a SIGKILLed thread",
6167            guest.thread_state().dettid
6168        );
6169        return std::future::pending().await;
6170    }
6171    if resp.1 == GlobalResponse::ThreadExited {
6172        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6173        // A thread an exit_group killed, on DBT where the exit_group's handler
6174        // walks the group's robust lists after the grant: its own native exit
6175        // would let Linux mark and clear the same words before the walk reads
6176        // them, so it retires only after the walk
6177        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4302).
6178        guest.thread_state().cancel_exit_group_filing();
6179        if !guest
6180            .thread_state()
6181            .wait_for_exit_group_robust_walk(crate::tool_local::EXIT_GROUP_ROBUST_WALK_WAIT)
6182        {
6183            // Retiring now would let this thread's native exit race a walk
6184            // that may still be running, so the run fails instead.
6185            panic!(
6186                "[detcore, dtid {}] EXIT_GROUP_ROBUST_WALK_TIMEOUT: the exit_group's robust-list walk neither finished nor was cancelled within {:?}",
6187                dettid,
6188                crate::tool_local::EXIT_GROUP_ROBUST_WALK_WAIT,
6189            );
6190        }
6191        trace!(
6192            "[detcore, dtid {}] exiting after terminal scheduler cancellation",
6193            dettid
6194        );
6195        // This exact task must never resume, but a sibling may still own the
6196        // winning exit-group commit. Retire only this task; explicit backend
6197        // cancellation could cancel that issuer or lose its later status.
6198        guest.retire_current_thread().await
6199    }
6200    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6201    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review applying the coordinator clock after exec reload.
6202    if let Some(time) = resp.0 {
6203        guest
6204            .thread_state_mut()
6205            .thread_logical_time
6206            .advance_to(time);
6207    }
6208    resp
6209}
6210
6211/// When the thread resumes after a potentially-blocking scheduler request, is it a normal
6212/// continuation of execution, or is it because the thread will now execute a signal handler.
6213/// If the latter, that interrupts logically blocking syscalls that were in progress.
6214#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
6215pub enum ResumeStatus {
6216    Normal,
6217    Signaled(Option<Vec<SigWrapper>>),
6218    /// A validated one-shot SIGALRM wake of this exact in-guest sleep.
6219    InGuestFatalAlarm,
6220    /// Granted, and nothing else can run (`SchedResponse::GoAlone`).
6221    NothingElseCanRun,
6222}
6223
6224/// Internal result of a scheduler operation. Terminal results become
6225/// [`GlobalResponse::ThreadExited`] before returning to the guest-side RPC helper.
6226#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone)]
6227enum SchedulerRpcResult<T> {
6228    Continue(T),
6229    ThreadExited,
6230}
6231
6232/// Wake one waiter per word an exec's owner death marked, for the next
6233/// deterministic drain (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4268).
6234/// The INFO record is not logged on DBT, whose coordinator has no tracing
6235/// subscriber, so there an L2 run compares the guest's output only (Claude
6236/// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4352, F2).
6237fn wake_exec_robust_waiters(sched: &mut Scheduler, wakes: &[(DetTid, FutexID)], at: &str) {
6238    if wakes.is_empty() {
6239        return;
6240    }
6241    let counts = sched.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(wakes);
6242    for ((owner, futex), count) in wakes.iter().zip(counts) {
6243        info!(
6244            "[detcore, dtid {}] robust-list owner death woke {} waiter(s) on futex {:?} at {}",
6245            owner, count, futex, at,
6246        );
6247    }
6248}
6249
6250/// A process pidfd for the host process `pid` (`pidfd_open` with no flags),
6251/// which reports exit only once the whole thread group has exited.
6252pub(crate) fn open_process_pidfd(pid: i32) -> std::io::Result<std::os::fd::OwnedFd> {
6253    // SAFETY: pidfd_open takes no pointers.
6254    let raw = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_open, pid, 0) };
6255    if raw < 0 {
6256        return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
6257    }
6258    // SAFETY: pidfd_open returned a new descriptor owned by this process.
6259    Ok(unsafe { std::os::fd::OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(raw as libc::c_int) })
6260}
6261
6262/// The pidfd that holds a SIGKILL's sender until victim `detpid` is gone, or
6263/// none when there is nothing left to wait for. The sender is never left
6264/// unfenced (Codex design review of
6265/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362 part 2, P2-3):
6266/// - for a kill that named the process (`process_directed`: kill or a pidfd),
6267///   a zombie whose exit the schedule granted: nothing to wait for
6268///   (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411);
6269/// - otherwise the victim's host process is the one registered for `named`,
6270///   the thread the kill named, or else, for a kill that named the process,
6271///   for the victim's lowest registered thread, as when a pidfd names a leader
6272///   that has exited while its siblings run on
6273///   (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411). A thread-directed
6274///   SIGKILL to an exited thread gets no fallback, because Linux does not end
6275///   the group for it (Claude review of
6276///   https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439, R1). With no such
6277///   thread, the run is refused: whether the victim still has a live thread
6278///   cannot decide it, because the kill may already have reached the kernel
6279///   (Claude re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4423, N1);
6280/// - opening the process pidfd fails with ESRCH (or EINVAL, which some older
6281///   kernels gave for a reaped process whose pid number lived on as a process
6282///   group or session id): the process is gone only if that thread's own
6283///   `PIDFD_THREAD` pidfd, held since it registered, reports that it exited;
6284///   otherwise the run is refused;
6285/// - any other open failure, such as EMFILE: the run is refused.
6286fn sigkill_fence_for(
6287    scheduler: &Scheduler,
6288    named: DetTid,
6289    detpid: DetPid,
6290    process_directed: bool,
6291    open: impl Fn(i32) -> std::io::Result<std::os::fd::OwnedFd>,
6292) -> Result<Option<std::os::fd::OwnedFd>, crate::scheduler::sigkill_retirement::UnfencedSigkill> {
6293    let unfenced = |reason: String| crate::scheduler::sigkill_retirement::UnfencedSigkill {
6294        process: detpid,
6295        reason,
6296    };
6297    if process_directed && scheduler.process_exit_granted(detpid) {
6298        return Ok(None);
6299    }
6300    let Some(via) = scheduler.sigkill_victim_registered_thread(named, detpid, process_directed)
6301    else {
6302        return Err(unfenced(if process_directed {
6303            format!(
6304                "neither the thread it named (dettid {named}) nor any other thread of it has a registered host process"
6305            )
6306        } else {
6307            format!(
6308                "the thread it named (dettid {named}) has no registered host process, and a SIGKILL to that thread alone does not end its group"
6309            )
6310        }));
6311    };
6312    let host = scheduler
6313        .physical_process_of(via)
6314        .expect("a registered thread has a host process");
6315    match open(host) {
6316        Ok(pidfd) => Ok(Some(pidfd)),
6317        Err(error)
6318            if matches!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::ESRCH | libc::EINVAL))
6319                && scheduler.registered_thread_has_exited(via) == Some(true) =>
6320        {
6321            Ok(None)
6322        }
6323        Err(error) => Err(unfenced(format!(
6324            "pidfd_open of its host process failed: {error}"
6325        ))),
6326    }
6327}
6328
6329/// `sigkill_fence_for`, ending the run on its refusal before the sender is
6330/// answered.
6331fn fence_or_refuse(
6332    scheduler: &Scheduler,
6333    named: DetTid,
6334    detpid: DetPid,
6335    process_directed: bool,
6336) -> Option<(DetPid, std::os::fd::OwnedFd)> {
6337    match sigkill_fence_for(
6338        scheduler,
6339        named,
6340        detpid,
6341        process_directed,
6342        open_process_pidfd,
6343    ) {
6344        Ok(fence) => fence.map(|pidfd| (detpid, pidfd)),
6345        Err(refusal) => crate::scheduler::exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal),
6346    }
6347}
6348
6349/// Wait until the process behind `pidfd` has exited, for at most `valve`;
6350/// why not, otherwise.
6351async fn wait_for_process_exit(pidfd: std::os::fd::OwnedFd, valve: Duration) -> Result<(), String> {
6352    let fd = tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::with_interest(pidfd, tokio::io::Interest::READABLE)
6353        .map_err(|error| format!("its pidfd cannot be awaited: {error}"))?;
6354    match tokio::time::timeout(valve, fd.readable()).await {
6355        Ok(Ok(_)) => Ok(()),
6356        Ok(Err(error)) => Err(format!("waiting on its pidfd failed: {error}")),
6357        Err(_) => Err(format!("it was not gone within {valve:?}")),
6358    }
6359}
6360
6361/// Whether the reply to `request` can resume its thread from a scheduler grant
6362/// (`Scheduler::unblock_guest`), or answers a timer it armed: the requests
6363/// whose replies carry a deadline hint
6364/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>). Every handler that
6365/// awaits a grant is reached from one of these.
6366fn resumes_from_grant(request: &GlobalRequest) -> bool {
6367    match request {
6368        GlobalRequest::WithForwardedCount(_, request) => resumes_from_grant(request),
6369        GlobalRequest::RequestResources(..)
6370        | GlobalRequest::ParkedRequest(..)
6371        | GlobalRequest::ResumeParkedRequest { .. }
6372        | GlobalRequest::ResumeExec(..)
6373        | GlobalRequest::CreateChildThread(..)
6374        | GlobalRequest::CreateVforkChildThread(..)
6375        | GlobalRequest::StartNewThread(..)
6376        | GlobalRequest::FutexAction(..)
6377        | GlobalRequest::TraceSchedEvent(..)
6378        | GlobalRequest::RegisterAlarm(..)
6379        | GlobalRequest::AlarmRemaining(..)
6380        | GlobalRequest::ReconcileAlarm(..)
6381        | GlobalRequest::RegisterPosixTimer(..) => true,
6382        _ => false,
6383    }
6384}
6385
6386/// End this thread's slice no later than the earliest deadline that was
6387/// pending when it was granted the turn it resumes
6388/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>).
6389///
6390/// A deadline is acted on only at a scheduler turn, and a thread running a
6391/// long slice of cheap syscalls takes none, so without this a sleeper's
6392/// wake-up waits for the whole slice.
6393pub(crate) fn cap_timeslice_at_deadline<G, T>(guest: &mut G, deadline: Option<Duration>)
6394where
6395    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6396    T: RecordOrReplay,
6397{
6398    let Some(remaining) = deadline else {
6399        return;
6400    };
6401    let clock_multiplier = guest.config().clock_multiplier.unwrap_or(1.0);
6402    let schedule_replay = guest.config().replay_schedule_from.is_some();
6403    // A configuration with an invalid turn cost is refused before any guest
6404    // runs; zero here only drops the floor.
6405    let min_slice = Duration::from_nanos(guest.config().scheduler_turn_charge().unwrap_or(0));
6406    guest.thread_state_mut().cap_timeslice_at_deadline(
6407        remaining,
6408        clock_multiplier,
6409        min_slice,
6410        schedule_replay,
6411    );
6412}
6413
6414/// Global method RPC to request to control a resource.
6415///
6416/// Blocking: future returns only when resources are fully acquired.
6417pub async fn resource_request<G, T>(guest: &mut G, mut r: Resources) -> ResumeStatus
6418where
6419    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6420    T: RecordOrReplay,
6421{
6422    // A request made while handling a syscall whose cost the bootstrap window
6423    // withholds carries that fact to the scheduler, which then withholds the
6424    // turn's scheduler time too (see `Scheduler::bump_global_time`). Only a
6425    // backend whose `is_backend_runtime_bootstrap` can return true ever sets it.
6426    r.backend_runtime_bootstrap |=
6427        guest.thread_state().in_uncharged_bootstrap_syscall && guest.is_backend_runtime_bootstrap();
6428    // Any turn of its own is a hand-off under `--pipe-wake-latency`: the
6429    // thread goes back behind the pollers it readied (`crate::pipe_wake`).
6430    guest.thread_state_mut().pipe_handoff_due = None;
6431    if guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
6432        if let Some(lease) = guest.signal_observation_lease() {
6433            if let Some(site) = guest.parked_signal_site() {
6434                return parked::capable_resource_request(
6435                    guest,
6436                    r,
6437                    ControlCapability::PublishOnly { lease, site },
6438                )
6439                .await;
6440            }
6441            parked::terminate_protocol(guest, ProtocolFailure::Identity).await;
6442        }
6443        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6444        let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
6445        trace!(
6446            "[detcore, dtid {}] BLOCKING on resource_request rpc... {:?}",
6447            &dettid, r
6448        );
6449        let resp =
6450            send_and_update_time(guest, GlobalRequest::RequestResources(r.clone(), detpid)).await;
6451        match resp.1 {
6452            GlobalResponse::RequestResources(x) => {
6453                trace!(
6454                    "[detcore, dtid {}] UNBLOCKED, acquired resources: {:?}",
6455                    &dettid, r
6456                );
6457                x
6458            }
6459            _ => unreachable!(),
6460        }
6461    } else {
6462        ResumeStatus::Normal
6463    }
6464}
6465
6466/// Global method RPC to release all held resources.
6467///
6468/// Nonblocking: future may return immediately before the central global object has
6469/// processed the resource release.
6470pub async fn resource_release_all<G, T>(guest: &mut G)
6471where
6472    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6473    T: RecordOrReplay,
6474{
6475    if guest.config().sequentialize_threads {
6476        let resp = send_and_update_time(guest, GlobalRequest::ReleaseAllResources).await;
6477        match resp.1 {
6478            GlobalResponse::ReleaseAllResources(x) => x,
6479            _ => unreachable!(),
6480        }
6481    }
6482}
6483
6484/// Global method RPC to allow a new thread to begin execution, called from the child thread.
6485///
6486/// Blocking: future returns only when the thread execution is truly ready to proceed.
6487///
6488/// Returns: a history of the thread preemptions, for it to play back when --replay-preemptions-from
6489/// is used.
6490pub async fn thread_start_request<G, T>(
6491    cfg: &Config,
6492    guest: &mut G,
6493    detpid: DetPid,
6494) -> Option<ThreadHistory>
6495where
6496    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6497    T: RecordOrReplay,
6498{
6499    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6500    if cfg.sequentialize_threads {
6501        trace!("[detcore, dtid {}] new thread BLOCKING on rpc...", &dettid);
6502        let physical_ids = guest
6503            .thread_state()
6504            .physical_tid
6505            .map(|tid| (guest.pid().as_raw(), tid));
6506        let signal_identity = guest.signal_task_identity();
6507        guest.thread_state_mut().signal_task_identity = signal_identity;
6508        let resp = send_and_update_time(
6509            guest,
6510            GlobalRequest::StartNewThread(dettid, detpid, physical_ids, signal_identity),
6511        )
6512        .await;
6513        match resp.1 {
6514            GlobalResponse::StartNewThread(preempts) => {
6515                trace!("[detcore, dtid {}] new thread UNBLOCKED (post-rpc)", dettid);
6516                preempts
6517            }
6518            _ => unreachable!(),
6519        }
6520    } else {
6521        None
6522    }
6523}
