6525/// Keep only the clone pointer that requests an exit-time clear and wake.
6526/// SETTID alone requests a birth-time store and must not register an exit wake.
6527pub(crate) fn child_tid_clear_address(flags: CloneFlags, address: usize) -> usize {
6528    if flags.contains(CloneFlags::CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID) {
6529        address
6530    } else {
6531        0
6532    }
6533}
6534
6535/// Global method RPC for the parent to add a child-thread to the round-robin pool.
6536///
6537/// Nonblocking: future returning does not guarantee anything about the central scheduler,
6538/// except that it will eventually give a slot to the child.  Then the protocol is that
6539/// child will subsequently make a `thread_start_request` to gate the start of its execution.
6540pub async fn create_child_thread<G, T>(
6541    guest: &mut G,
6542    child_dettid: DetTid,
6543    ctid: usize,
6544    flags: Option<CloneFlags>,
6545    exit_signal: libc::c_int,
6546    physical_ids: Option<(i32, i32)>,
6547) -> Option<MmId>
6548where
6549    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6550    T: RecordOrReplay,
6551{
6552    // Random (or replayed) starting priority in chaos mode, constant priority otherwise.
6553    let starting_priority = if guest.config().replay_preemptions_from.is_some() {
6554        // In preemption replay mode, the initial priority is set on the other
6555        // side of the rpc, in recv_create_child_thread.
6556        None
6557    } else if guest.config().replay_schedule_from.is_some() {
6558        // FIXME!  Find a cleaner way to make the root thread start off high-priority:
6559        if child_dettid <= DetTid::from_raw(3) {
6560            Some(REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY)
6561        } else {
6562            Some(REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY)
6563        }
6564    } else if guest.config().chaos {
6565        let entropy = guest
6566            .thread_state_mut()
6567            .chaos_prng_next_u64("child_priority");
6568        if guest.config().chaos_target_races {
6569            // Targeted chaos: bias a freshly created child to an extreme priority
6570            // so it either runs before the parent resumes or strictly after it,
6571            // instead of landing at a uniformly random priority. This maximizes
6572            // parent/child ordering divergence to surface fork/exec races.
6573            // Reproducible under `--fuzz-seed`/`--sched-seed`.
6574            if entropy.is_multiple_of(2) {
6575                Some(FIRST_PRIORITY)
6576            } else {
6577                Some(LAST_PRIORITY)
6578            }
6579        } else {
6580            Some(entropy_to_priority(entropy))
6581        }
6582    } else {
6583        Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY)
6584    };
6585
6586    let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
6587
6588    let resp = send_and_update_time(
6589        guest,
6590        GlobalRequest::CreateChildThread(
6591            child_dettid,
6592            detpid,
6593            ctid,
6594            flags,
6595            exit_signal,
6596            physical_ids,
6597            starting_priority,
6598        ),
6599    )
6600    .await;
6601    match resp.1 {
6602        GlobalResponse::CreateChildThread(x) => x,
6603        _ => unreachable!(),
6604    }
6605}
6606
6607/// Register a vfork child while its parent is blocked inside `clone(2)`.
6608///
6609/// Unlike an ordinary clone, the parent cannot perform this registration
6610/// because the kernel has blocked it until the child execs or exits. The child
6611/// therefore registers itself, carrying the inherited parent identity, flags,
6612/// and starting priority. The starting priority is derived the same way as an
6613/// ordinary clone so that chaos and replay scheduling stay deterministic.
6614pub async fn create_vfork_child_thread<G, T>(
6615    guest: &mut G,
6616    child_dettid: DetTid,
6617    vfork: crate::tool_local::PendingVfork,
6618) where
6619    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6620    T: RecordOrReplay,
6621{
6622    let starting_priority = if guest.config().replay_preemptions_from.is_some() {
6623        None
6624    } else if guest.config().replay_schedule_from.is_some() {
6625        Some(if child_dettid <= DetTid::from_raw(3) {
6626            REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY
6627        } else {
6628            REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY
6629        })
6630    } else if guest.config().chaos {
6631        Some(entropy_to_priority(vfork.child_priority_entropy.expect(
6632            "vfork child priority entropy missing in chaos mode",
6633        )))
6634    } else {
6635        // POSIX vfork suspends the parent until the child execs or _exits. Give
6636        // the vfork child a strictly higher priority (lower number) than the
6637        // parent's DEFAULT_PRIORITY so the deterministic scheduler always runs
6638        // the child first, rather than round-robining the parent and child at
6639        // equal priority (which leaves fork/exec ordering nondeterministic).
6640        Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY - 1)
6641    };
6642
6643    let resp = send_and_update_time(
6644        guest,
6645        GlobalRequest::CreateVforkChildThread(
6646            vfork.parent_dettid,
6647            vfork.parent_detpid,
6648            child_dettid,
6649            vfork.child_tid_addr,
6650            vfork.flags,
6651            vfork.exit_signal,
6652            starting_priority,
6653        ),
6654    )
6655    .await;
6656    match resp.1 {
6657        GlobalResponse::CreateChildThread(_) => (),
6658        _ => unreachable!(),
6659    }
6660}
6661
6662/// Remove the thread from the scheduler.
6663///
6664/// Nonblocking: the future may return immediately, not guaranteeing the changes to the
6665/// scheduler have been completed.
6666pub(crate) async fn deregister_thread<R>(
6667    threads_time: DetTime,
6668    cfg: &Config,
6669    reverie: &R,
6670    thread: ThreadDeregistration,
6671) where
6672    // Note, this is called from a context where we DON'T have a full, operable `Guest`.
6673    R: GlobalRPC<GlobalState>,
6674{
6675    if cfg.sequentialize_threads {
6676        let mm = thread.mm;
6677        // TODO: void_send_rpc
6678        let resp = reverie
6679            .send_rpc((threads_time, mm, {
6680                // The thread's last count; its slot is free for a later thread.
6681                let request = counted_request(GlobalRequest::DeregisterThread(thread));
6682                crate::detlog::release_forwarded_count();
6683                request
6684            }))
6685            .await;
6686        // We can't update the thread time here.  But it's dead anyway!
6687        match resp.1 {
6688            GlobalResponse::DeregisterThread(x) => x,
6689            _ => unreachable!(),
6690        }
6691    }
6692}
6693
6694/// Account this physical-exit callback's own clock before it joins a staged
6695/// robust-list batch. The empty wake request has no scheduler effects, but its
6696/// ordinary RPC header is admitted and accounted before it is acknowledged.
6697/// A retired incarnation must not contribute to the completed-exit barrier.
6698pub(crate) async fn acknowledge_robust_list_exit_time<R>(
6699    threads_time: DetTime,
6700    reverie: &R,
6701    mm: MmId,
6702) -> bool
6703where
6704    R: GlobalRPC<GlobalState>,
6705{
6706    let response = reverie
6707        .send_rpc((threads_time, mm, GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(Vec::new())))
6708        .await;
6709    match response.1 {
6710        GlobalResponse::RobustListWakes(counts) => {
6711            assert!(
6712                counts.is_empty(),
6713                "an empty exit-clock acknowledgement woke a waiter"
6714            );
6715            true
6716        }
6717        GlobalResponse::ThreadExited => false,
6718        _ => unreachable!(),
6719    }
6720}
6721
6722/// Deliver owner-death wakes from an exit callback that no longer has guest
6723/// memory access. The callback runs only after ptrace has observed physical
6724/// exit, so Linux's atomic robust-list word update is already complete.
6725pub(crate) async fn robust_list_wakes_after_exit<R>(
6726    threads_time: DetTime,
6727    reverie: &R,
6728    mm: MmId,
6729    wakes: Vec<(DetTid, RobustListWake)>,
6730) -> Vec<u64>
6731where
6732    R: GlobalRPC<GlobalState>,
6733{
6734    if wakes.is_empty() {
6735        return Vec::new();
6736    }
6737    let response = reverie
6738        .send_rpc((
6739            threads_time,
6740            mm,
6741            GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(
6742                wakes
6743                    .into_iter()
6744                    .map(|(owner, wake)| (owner, wake.futex))
6745                    .collect(),
6746            ),
6747        ))
6748        .await;
6749    match response.1 {
6750        GlobalResponse::RobustListWakes(counts) => counts,
6751        _ => unreachable!(),
6752    }
6753}

6785/// Which actions we can take before/after a futex system call.
6786#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
6787pub enum FutexAction {
6788    /// Check in before a FUTEX_WAIT, including an optional timeout and, on a backend
6789    /// that reports the kernel's signal state, the waiter's mask and where the
6790    /// scheduler reads its dispositions when it commits a wake. With `None`, as
6791    /// before, a scheduler-sent signal wakes the waiter and a cross-task signal
6792    /// does not.
6793    WaitRequest(Option<LogicalTime>, Option<FutexSignalWatch>),
6794    /// Check in after a FUTEX_WAIT
6795    WaitFinished,
6796    /// Check in before a FUTEX_WAKE, parameterized by the number of threads woken.
6797    WakeRequest(i32),
6798    /// Check in after a FUTEX_WAKE, parameterized by the number of threads woken.
6799    WakeFinished(i32),
6800    /// Check in for a plain FUTEX_REQUEUE or FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE of the request's
6801    /// futex onto the given one, waking up to the first count and moving up to
6802    /// the second (`Scheduler::requeue_futex_waiters`). Both counts are already
6803    /// checked to be non-negative, and the futex word already compared for
6804    /// FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE. Answers with the number woken plus the number moved,
6805    /// and is followed by a `WakeFinished`, as a wake is.
6806    RequeueRequest(FutexID, u32, u32),
6807}
6808
6809/// Ask scheduler for permission to proceed before/after futex operation.
6810/// Returns true if the operation completed normally, and false if it timed out.
6811pub async fn futex_action<G, T>(
6812    guest: &mut G,
6813    futex_action: FutexAction,
6814    futexid: &FutexID,
6815    init_read: i32,
6816    mask: u32,
6817) -> Option<SchedValue>
6818where
6819    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6820    T: RecordOrReplay,
6821{
6822    assert!(guest.config().sequentialize_threads);
6823    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6824    let req = GlobalRequest::FutexAction(dettid, futex_action, *futexid, init_read, mask);
6825    trace!(
6826        "BLOCKING on futex_action: sending request to scheduler: {:?}",
6827        req
6828    );
6829    // Update local time from potentially blocking operation:
6830    let resp = send_and_update_time(guest, req.clone()).await;
6831    match resp.1 {
6832        GlobalResponse::FutexAction(answer) => {
6833            trace!("UNBLOCKING after futex_action. Request was: {:?}", req);
6834            answer
6835        }
6836        _ => unreachable!(),
6837    }
6838}

7149/// Writes a structured json backtrace to a given file
7150fn write_backtrace<G, T>(guest: &mut G, m_path: Option<&PathBuf>)
7151where
7152    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7153    T: RecordOrReplay,
7154{
7155    if let Some(backtrace) = guest.backtrace() {
7156        if let Some(path) = m_path {
7157            let file = File::create(path).expect("Failed to open preemption stacktrace log file");
7158            serde_json::to_writer(file, &backtrace.force_pretty()).unwrap();
7159        } else {
7160            crate::util::capped_eprintln!("{}", backtrace.force_pretty());
7161        }
7162    } else {
7163        warn!("Could not read backtrace!");
7164    }
7165}

7167/// Additional instructions to a guest after shed events is consumed by global tool
7168#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
7169pub struct TraceSchedEventResponse {
7170    print_stack_strace: MaybePrintStack,
7171    timeslice: Option<LogicalTime>,
7172}
7173
7174struct SchedEventForLog<'a> {
7175    event: &'a SchedEvent,
7176    command_bootstrap: bool,
7177}
7178
7179struct CommandBootstrapInstructionPointer(NonZeroUsize);
7180
7181impl std::fmt::Debug for CommandBootstrapInstructionPointer {
7182    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
7183        write!(f, "{}", crate::logdiff::host_addr(self.0.get()))
7184    }
7185}
7186
7187impl std::fmt::Debug for SchedEventForLog<'_> {
7188    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
7189        if !self.command_bootstrap {
7190            return std::fmt::Debug::fmt(self.event, f);
7191        }
7192        f.debug_struct("SchedEvent")
7193            .field("dettid", &self.event.dettid)
7194            .field("op", &self.event.op)
7195            .field("count", &self.event.count)
7196            .field(
7197                "start_rip",
7198                &self.event.start_rip.map(CommandBootstrapInstructionPointer),
7199            )
7200            .field(
7201                "end_rip",
7202                &self.event.end_rip.map(CommandBootstrapInstructionPointer),
7203            )
7204            .field("end_time", &self.event.end_time)
7205            .finish()
7206    }
7207}
7208
7209/// Record an event in the schedule trace, OR check the event on replay.
7210/// This also prints the backtrace of the schedevent, if indicated.
7211///
7212/// Arguments:
7213/// - tag_end_rip: read the current guest registers to fill in the `end_rip` on the event with the
7214///   current instruction pointer.
7215pub async fn trace_schedevent<G, T>(guest: &mut G, ev: SchedEvent, tag_end_rip: bool)
7216where
7217    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7218    T: RecordOrReplay,
7219{
7220    assert!(guest.config().sequentialize_threads);
7221
7222    // trace_schedevent is called AFTER the event is complete, and the rip is resting just after it.
7223    let ev = if tag_end_rip {
7224        let end_rip = if let Some(r) = ev.end_rip {
7225            r
7226        } else {
7227            // While a SIGALRM delivery's signal pipeline runs at a syscall's
7228            // completion, the registers are its completed projection.
7229            let regs = match guest.thread_state().signal_register_projection {
7230                Some(projection) => projection,
7231                None => guest.regs().await,
7232            };
7233            NonZeroUsize::new(regs.rip.try_into().unwrap()).unwrap()
7234        };
7235        SchedEvent {
7236            end_rip: Some(end_rip),
7237            ..ev
7238        }
7239    } else {
7240        ev
7241    };
7242
7243    if tracing::enabled!(tracing::Level::TRACE)
7244        && let Some(rip) = ev.end_rip
7245    {
7246        let rip_addr = AddrMut::<u16>::from_raw(rip.into()).unwrap();
7247        // These bytes are diagnostic, not part of the recorded event. A guest
7248        // may legitimately make its memory unreadable (PR_SET_DUMPABLE), so
7249        // preserve that observation without unwinding the live run owner.
7250        let rip_contents = guest.memory().read_value(rip_addr);
7251        trace!(
7252            "Tracing sched event, after which rip is {}, next two instruction bytes {:?}",
7253            rip, rip_contents
7254        );
7255    }
7256
7257    let detpid = guest.thread_state().detpid.expect("detpid unset");
7258    let command_bootstrap = guest.is_command_bootstrap();
7259    let resp = send_and_update_time(
7260        guest,
7261        GlobalRequest::TraceSchedEvent(ev, detpid, command_bootstrap),
7262    )
7263    .await;
7264
7265    trace!("trace_schedevent result: {:?}", resp);
7266    match resp {
7267        (
7268            _,
7269            GlobalResponse::TraceSchedEvent(TraceSchedEventResponse {
7270                print_stack_strace,
7271                timeslice,
7272            }),
7273        ) => {
7274            if let Some(m_path) = print_stack_strace {
7275                trace!("[trace_schedevent] writing stacktrace via Reverie...");
7276                write_backtrace(guest, m_path.as_ref());
7277            }
7278
7279            if let Some(timeslice) = timeslice
7280                && guest.thread_state().past_global_first_execve
7281            {
7282                let end_of_timeslice =
7283                    guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time.as_nanos() + timeslice;
7284                trace!(
7285                    "[detcore][dettid {}] setting end_of_timeslice to {:?} as instructed by replayer",
7286                    guest.thread_state().dettid,
7287                    end_of_timeslice
7288                );
7289                guest.thread_state_mut().end_of_timeslice = Some(end_of_timeslice);
7290                if guest.config().max_timeslice.is_some() {
7291                    guest.thread_state_mut().max_timeslice_end = Some(end_of_timeslice);
7292                }
7293            }
7294        }
7295        _ => {
7296            unreachable!()
7297        }
7298    }
7299}

7432/// Whether a `clone3` `set_tid` naming `dettid` is refused: a task of this
7433/// run had that id, and it is not the pid of a zombie child of the caller's
7434/// process (`Scheduler::id_is_a_zombie_child_of`). "Had" is a registration with
7435/// the scheduler, which is never removed, or a clock component in the global
7436/// time (which exec reassignment can move away from an id that stays
7437/// registered). Such a zombie's pid is left to the kernel, which answers
7438/// EEXIST, and only the caller's own process can release it. Any other used id is
7439/// refused, a live task's included: whether a live thread is still alive when
7440/// the kernel runs the call can depend on host timing (a thread killed
7441/// without a granted exit deregisters when the host says), and a freed id
7442/// given to a new task would merge two tasks' state, keyed by that id, in
7443/// Detcore (`Detcore::clone3_set_tid_refusal`,
7444/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4370).
7445pub(crate) async fn thread_id_refused<G, T>(guest: &mut G, dettid: DetTid) -> bool
7446where
7447    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7448    T: RecordOrReplay,
7449{
7450    let response = send_and_update_time(guest, GlobalRequest::ThreadIdRefused(dettid)).await;
7451    match response.1 {
7452        GlobalResponse::ThreadIdRefused(refused) => refused,
7453        _ => unreachable!(),
7454    }
7455}

7727/// Wait without requesting a scheduler turn for a backend's physical-exit report.
7728pub async fn await_exact_child_physical_exit<G, T>(
7729    guest: &mut G,
7730    child: DetPid,
7731) -> ExactChildWaitState
7732where
7733    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7734    T: RecordOrReplay,
7735{
7736    let mut state = exact_child_wait_state(guest, child).await;
7737    if matches!(
7738        state,
7739        ExactChildWaitState::PhysicalExitPending | ExactChildWaitState::PhysicallyExited
7740    ) {
7741        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
7742        let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
7743        resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child), Permission::R);
7744        resources.fyi("wait-child-physical-exit");
7745        let _ = resource_request(guest, resources).await;
7746        state = exact_child_wait_state(guest, child).await;
7747    }
7748    state
7749}

7886/// Reserve the victims of the SIGKILL the calling thread is about to send to
7887/// `target`'s process (`scheduler::sigkill_retirement`). `None` keeps the
7888/// ordinary path.
7889pub async fn reserve_sigkill<G, T>(
7890    guest: &mut G,
7891    target: DetTid,
7892) -> Option<crate::scheduler::sigkill_retirement::SigkillReservation>
7893where
7894    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7895    T: RecordOrReplay,
7896{
7897    // Backends that cannot retire at the kill turn send no extra RPC.
7898    if !crate::scheduler::sigkill_retirement::retires_sigkill_at_the_kill_turn(
7899        &guest.config().backend,
7900    ) {
7901        return None;
7902    }
7903    let sender = guest.thread_state().dettid;
7904    // Read before the send, while the target certainly exists.
7905    let uid =
7906        crate::syscalls::real_uid(target.as_raw()).unwrap_or_else(|| unsafe { libc::getuid() });
7907    let response =
7908        send_and_update_time(guest, GlobalRequest::ReserveSigkill(sender, target, uid)).await;
7909    match response.1 {
7910        GlobalResponse::ReserveSigkill(token) => token,
7911        _ => unreachable!(),
7912    }
7913}

8251/// Whether guest task `caller`, naming `tid` (and thread group `tgid`, for the
8252/// calls that name one), names one of Hermit's own tasks: a thread of the
8253/// process Detcore's global state runs in (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4066>).
8254/// Under ptrace that is Hermit's, the container init, PID 1 of the guest's PID
8255/// namespace. Under DBT the global state runs in the root guest process, whose
8256/// guest ids are virtual and are not host tasks descended from it, so the
8257/// answer there is always no, as for KVM below.
8258///
8259/// Hermit's tasks are identified directly, as its own thread group, not as
8260/// "not a registered guest task": a guest task Detcore has not registered yet
8261/// (a newborn, before its parent's `clone` returns) is not Hermit's. The
8262/// thread-group test is `tgkill(hermit, tid, 0)`, which sends nothing.
8263///
8264/// Only a caller that is a host process descended from Hermit, in Hermit's
8265/// own PID namespace, can name Hermit's tasks:
8266/// - a caller in a nested PID namespace names tasks by that namespace's ids,
8267///   where Hermit's tasks are not visible;
8268/// - a backend whose guest tasks are not host tasks (KVM, whose guest ids may
8269///   equal the ids of Hermit's own threads) never reaches Hermit by a pid;
8270/// - a caller that is one of Hermit's threads, or whose `/proc` entry cannot
8271///   be read, is not such a host task: a guest task in a system call is alive.
8272pub fn hermit_task_named(caller: DetTid, tgid: Option<i32>, tid: i32) -> bool {
8273    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
8274    let hermit = std::process::id() as i32;
8275    if tid <= 0 || tgid.is_some_and(|tgid| tgid != hermit) {
8276        return false;
8277    }
8278    // SAFETY: signal 0 to a thread of this process only checks it exists.
8279    let in_hermits_group =
8280        tid == hermit || unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_tgkill, hermit, tid, 0) } == 0;
8281    if !in_hermits_group || !descends_from(caller.as_raw(), hermit) {
8282        return false;
8283    }
8284    let namespace = |path: String| fs::metadata(path).map(|meta| (meta.dev(), meta.ino()));
8285    match (
8286        namespace(format!("/proc/{}/ns/pid", caller.as_raw())),
8287        namespace("/proc/self/ns/pid".to_owned()),
8288    ) {
8289        (Ok(callers), Ok(hermits)) => callers == hermits,
8290        _ => false,
8291    }
8292}
8293
8294/// Whether host task `task`'s process is a descendant of process `ancestor`,
8295/// following parent pids in `/proc` (field 4 of `stat`, the process's parent
8296/// for any of its threads). A task that cannot be read is not.
8297fn descends_from(task: i32, ancestor: i32) -> bool {
8298    let parent = |pid: i32| -> Option<i32> {
8299        let stat = fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")).ok()?;
8300        // The command name may hold spaces and parentheses: fields resume
8301        // after the last ')', as state, ppid.
8302        stat.rsplit_once(')')?
8303            .1
8304            .split_whitespace()
8305            .nth(1)?
8306            .parse()
8307            .ok()
8308    };
8309    let mut pid = task;
8310    // Bounded by the depth of any real process tree; a reparenting race
8311    // cannot make it loop.
8312    for _ in 0..4096 {
8313        match parent(pid) {
8314            Some(next) if next == ancestor => return true,
8315            Some(next) if next > 0 => pid = next,
8316            _ => return false,
8317        }
8318    }
8319    false
8320}

8343/// separate axis from the notification defect this change fixes, so the
8344/// conversion is asserted here rather than silently widened — a realtime timer
8345/// signal would be a NEW capability, not a regression of an existing one.

8392/// Signal an unrecoverable error that exits the entire container.
8393/// Such exits are not determinizable (see "quasi-determinism").
8394///
8395/// ⚠️ `status` IS NOT A DEFAULTABLE PARAMETER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. This
8396/// function has four callers and they do not all mean the same thing: three are
8397/// fail-closed policy refusals (`HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`) and one is an
8398/// operator interrupt (`HERMIT_SIGINT_DEATH_EXIT`). While the status was baked in
8399/// here, every caller inherited whatever the last edit chose, so the SIGINT path
8400/// reported "hermit refused this run" for a run hermit did not refuse. Making it
8401/// an argument turns the meaning into a visible claim at each call site, which is
8402/// the same rule `scripts/check-exit-status-class.rs` enforces on the test side:
8403/// a status you can read is worth less than a status that says which channel
8404/// produced it.
8405///
8406/// Adding a caller means choosing; there is deliberately no default to fall into.
8407pub async fn unrecoverable_shutdown<G, T>(guest: &G, status: i32) -> !
8408where
8409    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
8410    T: RecordOrReplay,
8411{
8412    if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
8413        let mytime = guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time.clone();
8414        let mm = guest.thread_state().mm_id;
8415        // TODO: void_send_rpc
8416        let _ = guest
8417            .send_rpc((mytime, mm, GlobalRequest::UnrecoverableShutdown))
8418            .await;
8419    }
8420
8421    // In this scenario a backtrace doesn't really help us.
8422    //
8423    // ⚠️ THE STATUS IS THE ONLY THING THAT CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY, SO IT HAS TO
8424    // CARRY THE MEANING. This is a DELIBERATE, policy-driven shutdown: the run
8425    // hit an operation it cannot service under a fail-closed configuration and
8426    // hermit chose to stop. The parent sees only a container child that exited,
8427    // and its classifier treats an exit it cannot account for as unchosen — so
8428    // exiting 1 here made `classify_container_result` report
8429    // `class=container-child-exit` and 125, i.e. "hermit broke", for a shutdown
8430    // that worked exactly as designed. `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT` is the
8431    // agreed value for "hermit refused"; see its doc for why it is not 1.
8432    //
8433    // ⚠️ AND WHICH VALUE IS THE CALLER'S TO SAY, NOT THIS FUNCTION'S. Baking one
8434    // in here is what made an operator's Ctrl-C report as a policy refusal: the
8435    // condition differs per caller and only the caller knows it.
8436    //
8437    // The RPC above is `cfg!(debug_assertions)`-only, so it cannot be the
8438    // signal — in a release build the parent would learn nothing.
8439    std::process::exit(status);
8440}
8441
8442#[cfg(test)]
8443mod tests {
8444    /// Hermit's tasks are exactly its own thread group, named from its own PID
8445    /// namespace (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4066>). The test
8446    /// process stands in for Hermit.
8447    #[test]
8448    fn only_hermits_own_thread_group_is_hermits() {
8449        use super::hermit_task_named;
8450        use crate::types::DetTid;
8451        let me = std::process::id() as i32;
8452        // A child process stands in for a guest task.
8453        let mut guest = std::process::Command::new("sleep")
8454            .arg("30")
8455            .spawn()
8456            .unwrap();
8457        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(guest.id() as i32);
8458        assert!(hermit_task_named(caller, None, me));
8459        assert!(hermit_task_named(caller, Some(me), me));
8460        // One of Hermit's own threads is not a guest task, and names nothing
8461        // of Hermit's (KVM guest ids can equal them).
8462        // SAFETY: gettid has no preconditions.
8463        let own_thread = DetTid::from_raw(unsafe { libc::gettid() });
8464        assert!(!hermit_task_named(own_thread, None, me));
8465        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
8466        let (stop, stopped) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
8467        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
8468            // SAFETY: as above.
8469            send.send(unsafe { libc::gettid() }).unwrap();
8470            let _ = stopped.recv();
8471        });
8472        let other_thread = receive.recv().unwrap();
8473        assert!(hermit_task_named(caller, None, other_thread));
8474        assert!(hermit_task_named(caller, Some(me), other_thread));
8475        let guest_pid = guest.id() as i32;
8476        assert!(!hermit_task_named(caller, None, guest_pid));
8477        assert!(!hermit_task_named(caller, Some(guest_pid), guest_pid));
8478        assert!(!hermit_task_named(caller, Some(guest_pid), other_thread));
8479        assert!(!hermit_task_named(caller, None, 0));
8480        assert!(!hermit_task_named(caller, None, -1));
8481        // A caller that is not a host task descended from Hermit names nothing
8482        // of Hermit's: one that cannot be read, or Hermit's own parent.
8483        assert!(!hermit_task_named(DetTid::from_raw(i32::MAX), None, me));
8484        // SAFETY: getppid has no preconditions.
8485        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(unsafe { libc::getppid() });
8486        assert!(!hermit_task_named(parent, None, me));
8487        guest.kill().unwrap();
8488        guest.wait().unwrap();
8489        stop.send(()).unwrap();
8490        thread.join().unwrap();
8491    }

8493    /// The DBT SIGKILL fence waits on a process pidfd: a live victim keeps it
8494    /// waiting to the valve, and a dead one, even unreaped, releases it
8495    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362).
8496    #[test]
8497    fn the_dbt_sigkill_fence_waits_until_the_victim_process_is_gone() {
8498        use super::open_process_pidfd;
8499        use super::wait_for_process_exit;
8500        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
8501            .enable_all()
8502            .build()
8503            .unwrap();
8504        let mut victim = std::process::Command::new("sleep")
8505            .arg("30")
8506            .spawn()
8507            .unwrap();
8508        let pid = victim.id() as i32;
8509        let live = open_process_pidfd(pid).expect("a live child has a pidfd");
8510        let waited = runtime.block_on(wait_for_process_exit(
8511            live,
8512            std::time::Duration::from_millis(50),
8513        ));
8514        assert!(waited.unwrap_err().contains("not gone within"));
8515        let dying = open_process_pidfd(pid).expect("a live child has a pidfd");
8516        victim.kill().unwrap();
8517        assert_eq!(
8518            runtime.block_on(wait_for_process_exit(
8519                dying,
8520                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30)
8521            )),
8522            Ok(())
8523        );
8524        victim.wait().unwrap();
8525        assert!(open_process_pidfd(pid).is_err());
8526    }
8527
8528    /// The DBT SIGKILL fence never leaves the sender unfenced while the victim
8529    /// may still be running: an open failure refuses, and an ESRCH counts as
8530    /// the victim gone only once the thread the kill named has exited, as its
8531    /// registration pidfd shows (Codex design review of
8532    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362 part 2, P2-3).
8533    #[test]
8534    fn the_dbt_sigkill_fence_refuses_rather_than_leave_the_sender_unfenced() {
8535        use super::sigkill_fence_for;
8536        use crate::scheduler::Scheduler;
8537        use crate::types::DetPid;
8538        use crate::types::DetTid;
8539        use crate::types::MmId;
8540        let config = crate::config::Config::default()
8541            .with_backend(|backend| *backend = reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT);
8542        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
8543        let me = std::process::id() as i32;
8544        let errno = |code| move |_: i32| Err(std::io::Error::from_raw_os_error(code));
8545        // A live registered thread: EMFILE and an unconfirmed ESRCH refuse.
8546        let live = DetTid::from_raw(41);
8547        let live_process = DetPid::from_raw(41);
8548        // SAFETY: gettid has no preconditions.
8549        let my_tid = unsafe { libc::gettid() };
8550        scheduler
8551            .register_physical_thread(live, MmId::initial(live_process), me, my_tid)
8552            .unwrap();
8553        let refusal = sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, live, live_process, true, errno(libc::EMFILE))
8554            .unwrap_err();
8555        assert_eq!(refusal.process, live_process);
8556        assert!(refusal.reason.contains("pidfd_open"), "{}", refusal.reason);
8557        assert!(
8558            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, live, live_process, true, errno(libc::ESRCH)).is_err()
8559        );
8560        assert!(
8561            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, live, live_process, true, errno(libc::EINVAL)).is_err()
8562        );
8563        assert!(
8564            sigkill_fence_for(
8565                &scheduler,
8566                live,
8567                live_process,
8568                true,
8569                super::open_process_pidfd
8570            )
8571            .unwrap()
8572            .is_some()
8573        );
8574        // A registered thread that has exited: an ESRCH means the victim is gone.
8575        let gone = DetTid::from_raw(43);
8576        let gone_process = DetPid::from_raw(43);
8577        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
8578        let (stop, stopped) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
8579        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
8580            // SAFETY: as above.
8581            send.send(unsafe { libc::gettid() }).unwrap();
8582            let _ = stopped.recv();
8583        });
8584        let gone_tid = receive.recv().unwrap();
8585        scheduler
8586            .register_physical_thread(gone, MmId::initial(gone_process), me, gone_tid)
8587            .unwrap();
8588        stop.send(()).unwrap();
8589        thread.join().unwrap();
8590        // pthread_join returns at the CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID wake, before the
8591        // kernel marks the thread exited, so its pidfd can turn readable a
8592        // little later (Claude review of
8593        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4423, F1).
8594        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
8595        while scheduler.registered_thread_has_exited(gone) != Some(true) {
8596            assert!(
8597                std::time::Instant::now() < deadline,
8598                "the joined thread's pidfd never reported its exit"
8599            );
8600            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
8601        }
8602        assert!(
8603            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, gone, gone_process, true, errno(libc::EINVAL))
8604                .unwrap()
8605                .is_none()
8606        );
8607        assert!(
8608            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, gone, gone_process, true, errno(libc::ESRCH))
8609                .unwrap()
8610                .is_none()
8611        );
8612        assert!(
8613            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, gone, gone_process, true, errno(libc::EMFILE)).is_err()
8614        );
8615        // A named thread with no registration refuses, even when the victim
8616        // seems to have no live thread left: that can be its threads' exits
8617        // racing this notice after the kill reached the kernel (Claude
8618        // re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4423, N1).
8619        let unregistered = DetTid::from_raw(47);
8620        let empty = DetPid::from_raw(47);
8621        let refusal = sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, unregistered, empty, true, errno(libc::EMFILE))
8622            .unwrap_err();
8623        assert!(
8624            refusal.reason.contains("has a registered host process"),
8625            "{}",
8626            refusal.reason
8627        );
8628        // A zombie whose exit the schedule granted needs no fence
8629        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
8630        scheduler.grant_exit_for_test(empty);
8631        assert!(
8632            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, unregistered, empty, true, errno(libc::EMFILE))
8633                .unwrap()
8634                .is_none()
8635        );
8636        // A named leader that has exited while a sibling runs on: the fence
8637        // goes through the sibling's registration, and an ESRCH counts as gone
8638        // only once that sibling has exited
8639        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
8640        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(51);
8641        let process = DetPid::from_raw(51);
8642        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(52);
8643        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
8644        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, sibling, false);
8645        // SAFETY: as above.
8646        let my_tid = unsafe { libc::gettid() };
8647        scheduler
8648            .register_physical_thread(sibling, MmId::initial(process), me, my_tid)
8649            .unwrap();
8650        assert!(
8651            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, leader, process, true, super::open_process_pidfd)
8652                .unwrap()
8653                .is_some()
8654        );
8655        assert!(sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, leader, process, true, errno(libc::ESRCH)).is_err());
8656        // A thread-directed SIGKILL (tgkill, tkill, rt_tgsigqueueinfo) to the
8657        // exited leader gets no fallback and refuses; Linux does not end the
8658        // group for it (Claude review of
8659        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439, R1). Nor does a
8660        // thread-directed kill to a zombie skip the fence.
8661        assert!(
8662            sigkill_fence_for(
8663                &scheduler,
8664                leader,
8665                process,
8666                false,
8667                super::open_process_pidfd
8668            )
8669            .is_err()
8670        );
8671        assert!(
8672            sigkill_fence_for(&scheduler, unregistered, empty, false, errno(libc::EMFILE)).is_err()
8673        );
8674        // An exited leader whose surviving sibling has since exited too: an
8675        // ESRCH counts as gone, confirmed through the sibling's own
8676        // registration pidfd, not the leader's (Claude review of 4439, R2).
8677        let late_leader = DetTid::from_raw(61);
8678        let late_process = DetPid::from_raw(61);
8679        let late_sibling = DetTid::from_raw(62);
8680        scheduler
8681            .thread_tree
8682            .add_child(late_leader, late_leader, true);
8683        scheduler
8684            .thread_tree
8685            .add_child(late_leader, late_sibling, false);
8686        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
8687        let (stop, stopped) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
8688        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
8689            // SAFETY: as above.
8690            send.send(unsafe { libc::gettid() }).unwrap();
8691            let _ = stopped.recv();
8692        });
8693        let sibling_tid = receive.recv().unwrap();
8694        scheduler
8695            .register_physical_thread(late_sibling, MmId::initial(late_process), me, sibling_tid)
8696            .unwrap();
8697        stop.send(()).unwrap();
8698        thread.join().unwrap();
8699        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
8700        while scheduler.registered_thread_has_exited(late_sibling) != Some(true) {
8701            assert!(
8702                std::time::Instant::now() < deadline,
8703                "the joined thread's pidfd never reported its exit"
8704            );
8705            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
8706        }
8707        assert!(
8708            sigkill_fence_for(
8709                &scheduler,
8710                late_leader,
8711                late_process,
8712                true,
8713                errno(libc::ESRCH)
8714            )
8715            .unwrap()
8716            .is_none()
8717        );
8718    }

8720    /// DBT publishes READY_IMAGE between creating the scheduler future and
8721    /// polling it, so the announcement must already be logged when
8722    /// `run_external_scheduler` returns:
8723    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3463>.
8724    #[test]
8725    fn external_scheduler_announces_before_its_future_is_polled() {
8726        #[derive(Clone, Default)]
8727        struct Capture(std::sync::Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>);
8728        struct Visitor(String);
8729        impl tracing::field::Visit for Visitor {
8730            fn record_debug(&mut self, field: &tracing::field::Field, value: &dyn std::fmt::Debug) {
8731                if field.name() == "message" {
8732                    use std::fmt::Write;
8733                    write!(self.0, "{value:?}").unwrap();
8734                }
8735            }
8736        }
8737        impl tracing::Subscriber for Capture {
8738            fn enabled(&self, metadata: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
8739                *metadata.level() == tracing::Level::INFO
8740            }
8741            fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
8742                tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
8743            }
8744            fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
8745            fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8746            fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
8747                let mut visitor = Visitor(String::new());
8748                event.record(&mut visitor);
8749                self.0.lock().unwrap().push(visitor.0);
8750            }
8751            fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8752            fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8753        }
8754        let config = Config {
8755            sequentialize_threads: true,
8756            ..Config::default()
8757        };
8758        let state = GlobalState::init_for_external_scheduler(&config);
8759        let captured = Capture::default();
8760        let scheduler = tracing::subscriber::with_default(captured.clone(), || {
8761            state.run_external_scheduler(std::sync::Arc::new(|_| {}))
8762        });
8763        let announcement = "[scheduler] daemon task starting up, waiting for guest thread start..";
8764        assert_eq!(*captured.0.lock().unwrap(), [announcement]);
8765        drop(scheduler);
8766    }

8796    #[test]
8797    fn summary_preemption_views_keep_counts_full_report_and_single_flush() {
8798        let (_config, state, tid, _) = cancellation_test_state();
8799        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
8800        let path = directory.path().join("recording");
8801        let mut writer = crate::preemptions::PreemptionWriter::new(Some(path.clone()));
8802        writer.register_thread(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
8803        writer.insert_reprioritization(tid, LogicalTime::from_nanos(100), 10, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, 20);
8804        let mut scheduler = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
8805        scheduler.preemption_writer = Some(writer);
8806        let (summary, info_description) = scheduler
8807            .generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(Some(&path))
8808            .unwrap();
8809        assert!(scheduler.preemption_writer.is_none());
8810        let recorded = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
8811        let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&recorded).unwrap();
8812        assert_eq!(
8813            parsed["per_thread"][tid.to_string()]["prio_changes"],
8814            serde_json::json!([[100, DEFAULT_PRIORITY]])
8815        );
8816        let count_line = "Record of 1 preemption and reprioritization events:\n";
8817        assert_eq!(info_description.as_deref(), Some(count_line));
8818        assert_eq!(
8819            summary.reprio_descrip.as_deref(),
8820            Some(format!("{count_line}  (Writing to file {path:?})\n").as_str())
8821        );
8822        let full = summary.to_string();
8823        let json = serde_json::to_vec(&summary).unwrap();
8824        let info = summary.info(info_description.as_deref()).to_string();
8825        assert!(info.contains(count_line));
8826        assert!(!info.contains("Writing to file"));
8827        assert!(full.contains(&format!("Writing to file {path:?}")));
8828        // Formatting and another empty summary do not flush the consumed writer again.
8829        let _ = scheduler.generate_partial_run_summary(None).unwrap();
8830        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), recorded);
8831        assert_eq!(summary.to_string(), full);
8832        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_vec(&summary).unwrap(), json);
8833    }

8899    #[test]
8900    fn run_summary_info_keeps_semantics_and_debug_retains_bookkeeping() {
8901        #[derive(Clone)]
8902        struct Capture(std::sync::Arc<Mutex<Vec<(tracing::Level, String)>>>);
8903        struct Visitor(String);
8904        impl tracing::field::Visit for Visitor {
8905            fn record_debug(&mut self, field: &tracing::field::Field, value: &dyn std::fmt::Debug) {
8906                use std::fmt::Write;
8907                write!(self.0, "{}={value:?};", field.name()).unwrap();
8908            }
8909        }
8910        impl tracing::Subscriber for Capture {
8911            fn enabled(&self, _: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
8912                true
8913            }
8914            fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
8915                tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
8916            }
8917            fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
8918            fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8919            fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
8920                let mut visitor = Visitor(String::new());
8921                event.record(&mut visitor);
8922                self.0
8923                    .lock()
8924                    .unwrap()
8925                    .push((*event.metadata().level(), visitor.0));
8926            }
8927            fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8928            fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
8929        }
8930        let summary = super::RunSummary {
8931            sched_turns: 4,
8932            schedevent_recorded: 11,
8933            schedevent_replayed: 11,
8934            schedevent_desynced: 2,
8935            desync_descrip: Some("two real desyncs\n".into()),
8936            num_processes: 1,
8937            num_threads: 1,
8938            threads_descrip: "[3]".into(),
8939            syscalls: Some(3),
8940            virttime_elapsed: 2_512_380,
8941            virttime_final: 2_512_380,
8942            timeslice_stats: TimesliceStats {
8943                count: 1,
8944                sum_ns: 512_380,
8945                min_ns: 512_380,
8946                max_ns: 512_380,
8947            },
8948            ..Default::default()
8949        };
8950        let description = "Record of 7 preemption and reprioritization events:\n";
8951        let captured = Capture(Default::default());
8952        tracing::subscriber::with_default(captured.clone(), || {
8953            super::log_run_summary(
8954                "report",
8955                &summary,
8956                Some(description),
8957                Some(std::path::Path::new("/host/recording")),
8958            );
8959        });
8960        let events = captured.0.lock().unwrap();
8961        assert_eq!(events.len(), 2);
8962        assert_eq!(events[0].0, tracing::Level::INFO);
8963        assert_eq!(events[1].0, tracing::Level::DEBUG);
8964        let info = &events[0].1;
8965        for text in [
8966            "1 group leaders of 1 thread(s)",
8967            "3 syscalls",
8968            "4 turns, recorded 11 events (2 desynced)",
8969            "two real desyncs",
8970            "Record of 7 preemption",
8971            "2_512_380ns",
8972            "min=512380ns max=512380ns mean=512380ns count=1",
8973        ] {
8974            assert!(info.contains(text), "missing semantic field {text}: {info}");
8975        }
8976        assert!(!info.contains("/host/recording"));
8977        assert!(!info.contains("replayed"));
8978        assert!(events[1].1.contains("replayed_events=11"));
8979        assert!(events[1].1.contains("/host/recording"));
8980        let baseline = summary.info(Some(description)).to_string();
8981        let mutations: [fn(&mut super::RunSummary); 8] = [
8982            |s| s.sched_turns += 1,
8983            |s| s.schedevent_recorded += 1,
8984            |s| s.schedevent_desynced += 1,
8985            |s| s.num_threads += 1,
8986            |s| s.syscalls = Some(4),
8987            |s| s.virttime_elapsed += 1,
8988            |s| s.timeslice_stats.count += 1,
8989            |s| s.threads_descrip.push_str(",4"),
8990        ];
8991        for mutate in mutations {
8992            let mut changed = summary.clone();
8993            mutate(&mut changed);
8994            assert_ne!(changed.info(Some(description)).to_string(), baseline);
8995        }
8996        assert_ne!(
8997            summary
8998                .info(Some(
8999                    "Record of 8 preemption and reprioritization events:\n"
9000                ))
9001                .to_string(),
9002            baseline
9003        );
9004    }

9061    #[test]
9062    fn fdinfo_mount_ids_preserve_raw_equivalence_and_distinctness() {
9063        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 20, 30], true, &[]);
9064        // Numbered in first-observation order, not by row position: 20 is
9065        // the second captured row but the first ID the guest observes.
9066        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, None), Some(1));
9067
9068        // Unlisted nsfs, anon_inodefs, and pidfs IDs are distinct even when
9069        // their descriptors have the same broad Detcore FdType.
9070        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(700, None), Some(2));
9071        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(701, None), Some(3));
9072        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(702, None), Some(4));
9073        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(701, None), Some(3));
9074        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, None), Some(1));
9075    }

9077    #[test]
9078    fn fdinfo_mount_ids_seed_from_low_level_snapshot_and_refuse_drift() {
9079        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[], false, &[]);
9080        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, Some(&[10, 20, 30])), Some(1));
9081        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(700, Some(&[10, 20, 30])), Some(2));
9082        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, Some(&[10, 20, 30])), Some(1));
9083        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, Some(&[10, 99, 30])), None);
9084        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, Some(&[10, 20])), None);
9085        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(20, Some(&[10, 20, 30, 40])), None);
9086    }

9088    /// The compat/lsof divergence: a run's namespace starts as a copy of the
9089    /// host's, so unrelated host mounts (here 25, 26, 27, as one loop mount
9090    /// propagated to three peers) can change the row count between two runs
9091    /// of the same guest. The IDs the guest observes must not move.
9092    #[test]
9093    fn mount_ids_do_not_depend_on_rows_the_guest_never_observed() {
9094        let observe = |mut pool: MountIdPool, visible: &[u64]| {
9095            vec![
9096                pool.determinize(700, None),
9097                pool.determinize(701, None),
9098                pool.determinize(20, None),
9099            ]
9100            .into_iter()
9101            .chain(
9102                pool.resolve_mountinfo(visible, visible)
9103                    .unwrap()
9104                    .into_iter()
9105                    .map(Some),
9106            )
9107            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
9108        };
9109        let quiet = observe(
9110            MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 20, 30], true, &[]),
9111            &[10, 30],
9112        );
9113        let churned = observe(
9114            MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 20, 25, 26, 27, 30], true, &[]),
9115            &[10, 30],
9116        );
9117        assert_eq!(quiet, [Some(1), Some(2), Some(3), Some(4), Some(5)]);
9118        assert_eq!(quiet, churned);
9119
9120        // Uncaptured runs validate each fdinfo read against a tracer-side
9121        // snapshot of the same namespace; the snapshot's size is irrelevant.
9122        let mut quiet = MountIdPool::from_config(&[], false, &[]);
9123        let mut churned = MountIdPool::from_config(&[], false, &[]);
9124        assert_eq!(quiet.determinize(700, Some(&[10, 20, 30])), Some(1));
9125        assert_eq!(
9126            churned.determinize(700, Some(&[10, 20, 25, 26, 27, 30])),
9127            Some(1)
9128        );
9129        assert_eq!(quiet.determinize(701, Some(&[10, 20, 30])), Some(2));
9130        assert_eq!(
9131            churned.determinize(701, Some(&[10, 20, 25, 26, 27, 30])),
9132            Some(2)
9133        );
9134    }

9137    fn mountinfo_views_keep_earlier_numbers_and_number_the_rest_in_row_order() {

9143            Some(vec![3, 4, 1])

9146            pool.resolve_mountinfo(&[20, 40], &[20, 40]),

9152        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(701, None), Some(6));

9156    /// One chroot view: row 20 whose parent 10 is outside the view. The
9157    /// captured namespace may list 10 before 20 or after it, which the guest
9158    /// cannot see. The view's canonical order follows the capture, but the
9159    /// numbers must follow the view: row 20 first, then parent 10.
9160    #[test]
9161    fn captured_namespace_order_never_decides_mountinfo_numbers() {
9162        let mut parent_first = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 20, 9], true, &[]);
9163        let mut parent_last = MountIdPool::from_config(&[20, 10], true, &[]);
9164        assert_eq!(
9165            parent_first.resolve_mountinfo(&[10, 20], &[20, 10]),
9166            Some(vec![1, 2])
9167        );
9168        assert_eq!(
9169            parent_last.resolve_mountinfo(&[20, 10], &[20, 10]),
9170            Some(vec![1, 2])
9171        );
9172        assert_eq!(parent_first.determinize(10, None), Some(2));
9173        assert_eq!(parent_last.determinize(10, None), Some(2));
9174    }

9177    fn mountinfo_observation_order_must_name_exactly_the_canonical_ids() {
9178        for (canonical, observation) in [
9179            (&[10, 20][..], &[20][..]),
9180            (&[10, 20][..], &[20, 30][..]),
9181            (&[10, 20][..], &[20, 20][..]),
9182            (&[10, 20][..], &[10, 20, 30][..]),
9183        ] {
9184            let mut captured = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 20, 30], true, &[]);
9185            assert_eq!(captured.resolve_mountinfo(canonical, observation), None);
9186            assert_eq!(captured.determinize(30, None), Some(1));

9188            // A refused uncaptured view must not seed the namespace order.
9189            let mut uncaptured = MountIdPool::from_config(&[], false, &[]);
9190            assert_eq!(uncaptured.resolve_mountinfo(canonical, observation), None);
9191            assert!(matches!(uncaptured, MountIdPool::Uninitialized));
9192        }
9193    }

9227    #[test]
9228    fn fdinfo_mount_ids_refuse_malformed_configured_provenance() {
9229        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 10], true, &[]);
9230        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(10, None), None);
9231        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10], true, &[700, 700]);
9232        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(10, None), None);

9234        // validate later views against.

9236        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(700, Some(&[10])), None);
9237        assert!(pool.provenance().is_err());
9238        // No recording numbers raw 0 unless mountinfo named it: an fdinfo zero
9239        // is the anonymous class, and a mountinfo zero must pass validation.
9240        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10], true, &[0]);
9241        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(10, None), None);
9242        assert!(pool.provenance().is_err());
9243        let mut pool = MountIdPool::from_config(&[10, 0], true, &[10, 0]);
9244        assert_eq!(pool.resolve_mountinfo(&[10, 0], &[10, 0]), Some(vec![1, 2]));
9245        assert_eq!(pool.determinize(0, None), Some(0));

9260    #[tokio::test]
9261    async fn completing_an_unreported_exit_retires_it_and_records_determinism_loss() {
9262        if !crate::scheduler::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
9263            module_path!(),
9264            "completing_an_unreported_exit_retires_it_and_records_determinism_loss",
9265        ) {
9266            return;
9267        }
9268        use std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt;
9269
9270        use super::open_process_pidfd;
9271        use super::wait_for_process_exit;
9272
9273        struct Reap(std::process::Child);
9274        impl Drop for Reap {
9275            fn drop(&mut self) {
9276                let _ = self.0.kill();
9277                let _ = self.0.wait();
9278            }
9279        }
9280        let mut child = Reap(
9281            std::process::Command::new("sleep")
9282                .arg("30")
9283                .spawn()
9284                .unwrap(),
9285        );
9286        let physical_pid = child.0.id() as i32;
9287        let pidfd = open_process_pidfd(physical_pid).expect("a live child has a process pidfd");
9288        let config = Config {
9289            sequentialize_threads: true,
9290            ..Config::default()
9291        }
9292        .with_backend(|backend| {
9293            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
9294            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
9295        });
9296        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
9297        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(41);
9298        let mm = MmId::initial(dettid);
9299        assert_ne!(dettid.as_raw(), physical_pid);
9300        let pending_request = {
9301            let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9302            sched.thread_tree.add_child(dettid, dettid, true);
9303            sched.record_thread_mm(dettid, mm);
9304            sched
9305                .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, physical_pid, physical_pid)
9306                .unwrap();
9307            sched.next_turns.insert(
9308                dettid,
9309                crate::scheduler::ThreadNextTurn {
9310                    dettid,
9311                    child_tid_addr: 0,
9312                    req: Ivar::new(),
9313                    resp: Ivar::new(),
9314                    protocol: Default::default(),
9315                },
9316            );
9317            sched.next_turns[&dettid].req.clone()
9318        };
9319        assert!(pending_request.is_empty());
9320        child.0.kill().unwrap();
9321        assert!(
9322            wait_for_process_exit(pidfd, Duration::from_secs(5))
9323                .await
9324                .is_ok()
9325        );
9326
9327        // Physical readiness authenticates death, but cleanup takes the
9328        // registered logical process ID and must not reap the parent's child.
9329        state.complete_physical_process_exit(dettid.as_raw());
9330        assert!(pending_request.get().await.is_err());
9331        let sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9332        assert!(!sched.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid));
9333        assert!(sched.process_physically_gone(DetPid::from_raw(41)));
9334        assert!(!sched.process_physically_gone(DetPid::from_raw(physical_pid)));
9335        drop(sched);
9336        assert_eq!(
9337            crate::detlog::determinism_loss().as_deref(),
9338            Some("process 41 exited without deregistering; its exit was not scheduled")
9339        );
9340        let status = child
9341            .0
9342            .wait()
9343            .expect("cleanup must leave the kernel status for the parent");
9344        assert_eq!(status.signal(), Some(libc::SIGKILL));
9345        assert_eq!(status.code(), None);
9346    }

9348    #[tokio::test]
9349    async fn stale_process_exit_cannot_clear_replacement_and_normal_exit_adds_no_loss() {
9350        if !crate::scheduler::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
9351            module_path!(),
9352            "stale_process_exit_cannot_clear_replacement_and_normal_exit_adds_no_loss",
9353        ) {
9354            return;
9355        }
9356        use nix::fcntl::OFlag;
9357
9358        use super::open_process_pidfd;
9359        use super::wait_for_process_exit;
9360        use crate::fd::DetFd;
9361        use crate::fd::FdType;
9362        use crate::shared_open_files::OpenFileControl;
9363        use crate::types::OpenFileId;
9364
9365        struct Reap(std::process::Child);
9366        impl Drop for Reap {
9367            fn drop(&mut self) {
9368                let _ = self.0.kill();
9369                let _ = self.0.wait();
9370            }
9371        }
9372        let mut child = Reap(
9373            std::process::Command::new("sleep")
9374                .arg("30")
9375                .spawn()
9376                .unwrap(),
9377        );
9378        let physical_pid = child.0.id() as i32;
9379        let pidfd = open_process_pidfd(physical_pid).unwrap();
9380        let config = Config {
9381            sequentialize_threads: true,
9382            backend: reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT,
9383            ..Config::default()
9384        };
9385        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
9386        let process = DetPid::from_raw(41);
9387        let old_mm = MmId::initial(process);
9388        let mm = old_mm.for_exec(process);
9389        let (old, current) = {
9390            let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9391            sched.thread_tree.add_child(process, process, true);
9392            sched.record_thread_mm(process, old_mm);
9393            sched.next_turns.insert(
9394                process,
9395                ThreadNextTurn {
9396                    dettid: process,
9397                    child_tid_addr: 0,
9398                    req: Ivar::new(),
9399                    resp: Ivar::new(),
9400                    protocol: Default::default(),
9401                },
9402            );
9403            sched
9404                .register_physical_thread(process, old_mm, physical_pid, physical_pid)
9405                .unwrap();
9406            let old = sched.arm_process_exit_watch(
9407                process,
9408                old_mm,
9409                physical_pid,
9410                open_process_pidfd(physical_pid).unwrap(),
9411            );
9412            sched.record_thread_mm(process, mm);
9413            sched
9414                .register_physical_thread(process, mm, physical_pid, physical_pid)
9415                .unwrap();
9416            let current = sched.arm_process_exit_watch(
9417                process,
9418                mm,
9419                physical_pid,
9420                open_process_pidfd(physical_pid).unwrap(),
9421            );
9422            (old, current)
9423        };
9424        let pending = PendingExecState {
9425            caller: process,
9426            process,
9427            mm,
9428            fd_blocking: Default::default(),
9429        };
9430        state
9431            .pending_exec_states
9432            .lock()
9433            .unwrap()
9434            .insert(process, pending.clone());
9435        state
9436            .post_exec_fd_blocking
9437            .lock()
9438            .unwrap()
9439            .insert(process, ExecFdState::default());
9440        let id = OpenFileId::new(process, 0);
9441        {
9442            let mut files = state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap();
9443            files
9444                .insert(DetFd::new(3, OFlag::O_RDWR, FdType::Regular, id).model_for_test())
9445                .unwrap();
9446            files
9447                .handle(process, process, OpenFileControl::Take { id })
9448                .unwrap();
9449        }
9450        child.0.kill().unwrap();
9451        assert!(
9452            wait_for_process_exit(pidfd, Duration::from_secs(5))
9453                .await
9454                .is_ok()
9455        );
9456        let cleanup = state.process_exit_cleanup();
9457        {
9458            let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9459            assert_eq!(cleanup.complete_observed_locked(&mut sched, &old), None);
9460            assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&process));
9461            assert_eq!(
9462                state.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().get(&process),
9463                Some(&pending)
9464            );
9465            assert!(
9466                state
9467                    .post_exec_fd_blocking
9468                    .lock()
9469                    .unwrap()
9470                    .contains_key(&process)
9471            );
9472            assert!(state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap().is_leased(id));
9473            assert_eq!(crate::detlog::determinism_loss(), None);
9474
9475            // Model the normal hook winning the same mutex before the
9476            // readiness callback. Its later physical completion is no loss.
9477            state.account_deregistered_thread(
9478                &mut sched,
9479                ThreadDeregistration {
9480                    dettid: process,
9481                    detpid: process,
9482                    mm,
9483                    thread_start_entered: true,
9484                    timeslice_stats: TimesliceStats::default(),
9485                    syscall_count: 0,
9486                    chaos_epochs: Vec::new(),
9487                },
9488            );
9489            assert_eq!(
9490                cleanup.complete_observed_locked(&mut sched, &current),
9491                Some((false, None))
9492            );
9493            assert_eq!(cleanup.complete_observed_locked(&mut sched, &current), None);
9494        }
9495        assert!(state.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
9496        assert!(state.post_exec_fd_blocking.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
9497        assert!(!state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap().is_leased(id));
9498        assert_eq!(crate::detlog::determinism_loss(), None);
9499        assert!(child.0.wait().unwrap().code().is_none());
9500    }

9502    /// An admitted process can die before any registration names it. The
9503    /// production completion callback must then record it physically gone,
9504    /// without panicking on the unknown thread group, so that its late
9505    /// registration is refused (Codex implementation review, HIGH 1).
9506    #[test]
9507    fn completing_a_process_that_never_registered_records_it_gone() {
9508        let config = Config {
9509            sequentialize_threads: true,
9510            ..Config::default()
9511        }
9512        .with_backend(|backend| {
9513            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
9514            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
9515        });
9516        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
9517        state.complete_physical_process_exit(57);
9518        let sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9519        assert!(sched.process_physically_gone(DetPid::from_raw(57)));
9520        assert!(!sched.thread_tree.contains(&DetTid::from_raw(57)));
9521        assert!(!sched.next_turns.contains_key(&DetTid::from_raw(57)));
9522    }

9524    /// Two backends call `GlobalTool::on_backend_process_exited`, for two
9525    /// different events, and Detcore tells them apart only by capability. The
9526    /// ptrace tracer (PTRACE and E9PATCH declare
9527    /// `reports_child_exit_publication`) reports that the kernel published a
9528    /// leader's exit to its parent: that releases the scheduler's publication
9529    /// hold and must leave the physical-exit and exec state alone. In-guest
9530    /// LiteInst (`process_exits_complete_asynchronously`, no publication
9531    /// reports) reports the process's physical exit: that releases its
9532    /// physical-exit barrier and clears its exec state, and is not a
9533    /// publication. Each case starts from the state both paths could touch, so
9534    /// taking the other path fails it.
9535    #[test]
9536    fn backend_exit_reports_take_the_path_the_backend_capabilities_select() {
9537        use reverie::BackendCapabilities;
9538        for (name, backend) in [
9539            ("PTRACE", BackendCapabilities::PTRACE),
9540            ("E9PATCH", BackendCapabilities::E9PATCH),
9541            ("LITEINST_IN_GUEST", BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST),
9542        ] {
9543            let publishes = backend.reports_child_exit_publication;
9544            assert_eq!(publishes, name != "LITEINST_IN_GUEST", "{name}");
9545            let config = Config {
9546                sequentialize_threads: true,
9547                backend,
9548                ..Config::default()
9549            };
9550            let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
9551            let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(43);
9552            let leader = DetTid::from_raw(43);
9553            state.pending_exec_states.lock().unwrap().insert(
9554                detpid,
9555                PendingExecState {
9556                    caller: leader,
9557                    process: detpid,
9558                    mm: MmId::initial(detpid),
9559                    fd_blocking: Default::default(),
9560                },
9561            );
9562            state.post_exec_fd_blocking.lock().unwrap().insert(
9563                leader,
9564                ExecFdState::from([42].into_iter().collect::<ExecFdBlockingOverrides>()),
9565            );
9566            {
9567                let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9568                sched.install_test_child_exit_publication_hold(detpid);
9569                // Only a backend whose exits complete asynchronously (or that
9570                // reports physical exits) installs a physical-exit barrier.
9571                assert_eq!(
9572                    sched.begin_physical_process_exit(detpid),
9573                    !publishes,
9574                    "{name}"
9575                );
9576            }
9577
9578            <GlobalState as GlobalTool>::on_backend_process_exited(&state, detpid.as_raw());
9579
9580            let sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
9581            let exec_state_kept = state
9582                .pending_exec_states
9583                .lock()
9584                .unwrap()
9585                .contains_key(&detpid);
9586            let fd_blocking_kept = state
9587                .post_exec_fd_blocking
9588                .lock()
9589                .unwrap()
9590                .contains_key(&leader);
9591            if publishes {
9592                // The hold is released, not recorded as an early report.
9593                assert_eq!(
9594                    sched.test_child_exit_publication_state(detpid),
9595                    (false, false),
9596                    "{name}"
9597                );
9598                assert!(!sched.process_physically_gone(detpid), "{name}");
9599                assert!(exec_state_kept, "{name}");
9600                assert!(fd_blocking_kept, "{name}");
9601            } else {
9602                assert!(sched.pending_async_process_exits().is_empty(), "{name}");
9603                assert!(sched.process_physically_gone(detpid), "{name}");
9604                assert!(!exec_state_kept, "{name}");
9605                assert!(!fd_blocking_kept, "{name}");
9606                // Not a publication: the hold is neither released nor recorded.
9607                assert_eq!(
9608                    sched.test_child_exit_publication_state(detpid),
9609                    (true, false),
9610                    "{name}"
9611                );
9612            }
9613        }
9614    }

9616    #[test]
9617    fn recorded_assignment_order_rebuilds_the_same_mapping_in_any_replay_order() {
9618        let mut recording = MountIdPool::from_config(&[], false, &[]);
9619        assert_eq!(recording.determinize(700, Some(&[10, 20])), Some(1));
9620        assert_eq!(
9621            recording.resolve_mountinfo(&[10, 20], &[10, 20]),
9622            Some(vec![2, 3])
9623        );
9624        assert_eq!(recording.determinize(701, None), Some(4));
9625        let provenance = recording.provenance().unwrap().unwrap();
9626        assert_eq!(provenance.mountinfo_order, [10, 20]);
9627        assert_eq!(provenance.assignment_order, [700, 10, 20, 701]);
9628
9629        // Replay observes the same raw IDs in a different order and still
9630        // gets every recorded number.
9631        let mut replay = MountIdPool::from_config(
9632            &provenance.mountinfo_order,
9633            true,
9634            &provenance.assignment_order,
9635        );
9636        assert_eq!(replay.determinize(701, None), Some(4));
9637        assert_eq!(replay.resolve_mountinfo(&[20], &[20]), Some(vec![3]));
9638        assert_eq!(replay.determinize(10, None), Some(2));
9639        assert_eq!(replay.determinize(700, None), Some(1));
9640        assert_eq!(
9641            replay.provenance().unwrap().unwrap().assignment_order,
9642            provenance.assignment_order
9643        );
9644    }

9657    async fn check_inherited_input_root_ownership(root: DetTid, child: DetTid) {
9658        use super::ChildRegistration;
9659
9660        let config = Config {
9661            sequentialize_threads: false,
9662            ..Config::default()
9663        }
9664        .with_backend(|backend| backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table = true);
9665        let mut state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
9666        let pipe = reverie::InheritedInput::pipe(0).unwrap();
9667        state.install_inherited_input(pipe.lease().unwrap());
9668        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(root.as_raw() + 2);
9669        let root_mm = MmId::initial(root);
9670        for (parent, task, flags) in [
9671            (root, root, None),
9672            (root, child, Some(CloneFlags::empty())),
9673            (
9674                root,
9675                worker,
9676                Some(CloneFlags::CLONE_VM | CloneFlags::CLONE_SIGHAND | CloneFlags::CLONE_THREAD),
9677            ),
9678        ] {
9679            assert!(matches!(
9680                state
9681                    .recv_create_child_thread(
9682                        Tid::from_raw(parent.as_raw()),
9683                        root_mm,
9684                        ChildRegistration {
9685                            parent_dettid: parent,
9686                            parent_detpid: root,
9687                            child_dettid: task,
9688                            child_tid_addr: 0,
9689                            flags,
9690                            exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
9691                            physical_ids: None,
9692                            maybe_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
9693                            parent_is_kernel_blocked: false,
9694                        },
9695                    )
9696                    .await,
9697                SchedulerRpcResult::Continue(())
9698            ));
9699        }
9700        assert_eq!(
9701            state.inherited_input.lock().unwrap().as_ref().unwrap().root,
9702            Some((root, root_mm))
9703        );
9704
9705        // Neither a descendant nor a sibling sharing the root's exact MmId
9706        // may consume the seed before the root's own completion.
9707        for (task, detpid, mm) in [
9708            (child, child, MmId::initial(child)),
9709            (worker, root, root_mm),
9710        ] {
9711            let response = state
9712                .receive_rpc(
9713                    Tid::from_raw(task.as_raw()),
9714                    (
9715                        DetTime::new(&config),
9716                        mm,
9717                        GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(detpid, None, None),
9718                    ),
9719                )
9720                .await
9721                .1;
9722            let GlobalResponse::MarkPastFirstExecve(non_root_state) = response else {
9723                panic!("{response:?}")
9724            };
9725            assert!(non_root_state.initial_input.is_none());
9726            assert!(state.inherited_input.lock().unwrap().is_some());
9727        }
9728
9729        // Nor can a later root image, even with the correct descriptor slot.
9730        let response = state
9731            .receive_rpc(
9732                Tid::from_raw(root.as_raw()),
9733                (
9734                    DetTime::new(&config),
9735                    root_mm.for_exec(root),
9736                    GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(root, None, None),
9737                ),
9738            )
9739            .await
9740            .1;
9741        // An initial registration has no retired-exec incarnation entry, so
9742        // the existing RPC layer returns an empty completion here. The launch
9743        // lease's stricter root/image binding must still refuse the seed.
9744        assert_eq!(
9745            response,
9746            GlobalResponse::MarkPastFirstExecve(Default::default())
9747        );
9748        assert!(state.inherited_input.lock().unwrap().is_some());
9749
9750        let response = state
9751            .receive_rpc(
9752                Tid::from_raw(root.as_raw()),
9753                (
9754                    DetTime::new(&config),
9755                    root_mm,
9756                    GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(root, None, None),
9757                ),
9758            )
9759            .await
9760            .1;
9761        let GlobalResponse::MarkPastFirstExecve(root_state) = response else {
9762            panic!("{response:?}")
9763        };
9764        assert_eq!(root_state.initial_input.as_ref(), Some(pipe.identity()));
9765        assert!(state.inherited_input.lock().unwrap().is_none());
9766        let response = state
9767            .receive_rpc(
9768                Tid::from_raw(root.as_raw()),
9769                (
9770                    DetTime::new(&config),
9771                    root_mm,
9772                    GlobalRequest::MarkPastFirstExecve(root, None, None),
9773                ),
9774            )
9775            .await
9776            .1;
9777        let GlobalResponse::MarkPastFirstExecve(repeated) = response else {
9778            panic!("{response:?}")
9779        };
9780        assert!(repeated.initial_input.is_none());
9781
9782        // An exec preparation is a return of existing OFD state, not an
9783        // installation channel for copied launch identities.
9784        let response = state
9785            .receive_rpc(
9786                Tid::from_raw(root.as_raw()),
9787                (
9788                    DetTime::new(&config),
9789                    root_mm,
9790                    GlobalRequest::PrepareExec(root, root_mm, root_state),
9791                ),
9792            )
9793            .await
9794            .1;
9795        assert_eq!(response, GlobalResponse::ThreadExited);
9796    }
