14156    /// Ordinary churn reuses one host inode many times. A snapshot lookup
14157    /// must not scan the inode's whole history (codex re-check of
14158    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3849): a snapshot newer than
14159    /// the last retirement is answered without examining any record, and an
14160    /// older one examines about log2 of the history's length, while still
14161    /// naming the file that held the inode when it was taken.
14162    #[test]
14163    fn a_snapshot_lookup_does_not_scan_the_inodes_history() {
14164        use super::InodeSighting::Listed;
14165        use super::InodeSighting::Name;
14166        use crate::types::RawInode;
14167
14168        const GENERATIONS: usize = 4096;
14169        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14170        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14171        let raw = RawInode::new(2049, 12);
14172        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14173        // Each holder is numbered, seen in a snapshot, and retired; the next
14174        // file the host gives the inode is opened by name.
14175        let mut held = Vec::with_capacity(GENERATIONS);
14176        for _ in 0..GENERATIONS {
14177            pool.forget_retired(raw);
14178            let number = pool.add_sighted_inode(raw, seen, t, Name).0;
14179            held.push((pool.retirements, number));
14180            pool.retire(raw);
14181        }
14182        // The current holder, numbered after the last retirement.
14183        pool.forget_retired(raw);
14184        let current = pool.add_sighted_inode(raw, seen, t, Name).0;
14185
14186        pool.listed_probes = 0;
14187        for _ in 0..1000 {
14188            let snapshot = pool.retirements;
14189            assert_eq!(
14190                pool.add_sighted_inode(raw, seen, t, Listed(snapshot)).0,
14191                current
14192            );
14193        }
14194        assert_eq!(
14195            pool.listed_probes, 0,
14196            "a current snapshot examined history records"
14197        );
14198
14199        let bound = (GENERATIONS.ilog2() + 2) as u64;
14200        for step in (0..GENERATIONS).step_by(37) {
14201            let (snapshot, number) = held[step];
14202            pool.listed_probes = 0;
14203            assert_eq!(
14204                pool.add_sighted_inode(raw, seen, t, Listed(snapshot)).0,
14205                number,
14206                "the snapshot taken while holder {step} held the inode"
14207            );
14208            assert!(
14209                pool.listed_probes <= bound,
14210                "holder {step}: {} probes for {GENERATIONS} generations",
14211                pool.listed_probes
14212            );
14213        }
14214    }
14215
14216    /// Retiring and discarding follow host state (a link count, whether the
14217    /// host reused an inode), so they must not consume counter values: files
14218    /// numbered after them get the same numbers either way.
14219    #[test]
14220    fn retiring_and_forgetting_consume_no_counter_values() {
14221        use crate::types::RawInode;
14222
14223        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14224        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14225        let raw = RawInode::new(2049, 12);
14226        let numbers = |retire: bool| {
14227            let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14228            pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t);
14229            if retire {
14230                pool.retire(raw);
14231                pool.forget_retired(raw);
14232                pool.forget_retired(RawInode::new(2049, 77));
14233            }
14234            [RawInode::new(2049, 20), RawInode::new(2049, 21)]
14235                .map(|raw| pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t).0)
14236        };
14237        assert_eq!(numbers(true), numbers(false));
14238    }
14239
14240    /// Whether a host inode is new to the pool depends on host state the guest
14241    /// does not control. In https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2897,
14242    /// `sar` and its child `sadc` each opened one file; in one run another
14243    /// process replaced it between the two opens, so the second open saw a new
14244    /// host inode. Every later file, on every device, came out one number
14245    /// higher, and every `getdents64` chunk of a `/sys` listing differed. Only
14246    /// the file whose host identity differed may change number.
14247    #[test]
14248    fn a_host_dependent_new_inode_does_not_renumber_later_files() {
14249        use crate::types::DetInode;
14250        use crate::types::RawInode;
14251
14252        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14253        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14254        const ROOTFS: u64 = 2049;
14255        const SYSFS: u64 = 22;
14256        let later_files = |pool: &mut super::InodePool| -> Vec<DetInode> {
14257            [
14258                RawInode::new(SYSFS, 76_927),
14259                RawInode::new(SYSFS, 76_925),
14260                RawInode::new(SYSFS, 243_324),
14261                RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 1_311),
14262                RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 1_312),
14263            ]
14264            .into_iter()
14265            .map(|raw| pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t).0)
14266            .collect()
14267        };
14268
14269        // Both opens find the same host file.
14270        let mut unchanged = super::InodePool::new();
14271        unchanged.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 94_136_091), seen, t);
14272        unchanged.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 94_136_091), seen, t);
14273        // The file is replaced between the two opens.
14274        let mut replaced = super::InodePool::new();
14275        replaced.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 94_136_091), seen, t);
14276        replaced.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 94_154_661), seen, t);
14277        assert_eq!(
14278            later_files(&mut unchanged),
14279            later_files(&mut replaced),
14280            "a host-dependent new inode renumbered files minted after it"
14281        );
14282
14283        // The converse: two paths that are one host file (a hard link, or an
14284        // inode the filesystem reused) versus two separate host files.
14285        let mut linked = super::InodePool::new();
14286        linked.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 500), seen, t);
14287        linked.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 500), seen, t);
14288        let mut separate = super::InodePool::new();
14289        separate.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 500), seen, t);
14290        separate.add_inode(RawInode::new(ROOTFS, 501), seen, t);
14291        assert_eq!(
14292            later_files(&mut linked),
14293            later_files(&mut separate),
14294            "a host-dependent reused inode renumbered files minted after it"
14295        );
14296    }
14297
14298    /// Whether an mtime update reaches the pool depends on host state:
14299    /// `utimensat` skips it when the target's host identity changed during the
14300    /// call or the kernel stored an unexpected time. Setting an mtime must not
14301    /// consume a number, so a skipped update cannot renumber later files; and
14302    /// a file that gets its mtime before its number keeps that mtime.
14303    #[test]
14304    fn an_mtime_update_does_not_number_files() {
14305        use crate::types::DetInode;
14306        use crate::types::RawInode;
14307
14308        let epoch = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14309        let set = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
14310        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14311        let touched = RawInode::new(2049, 77);
14312        let later_files = |pool: &mut super::InodePool| -> Vec<DetInode> {
14313            (1_000..1_003)
14314                .map(|ino| pool.add_inode(RawInode::new(2049, ino), seen, epoch).0)
14315                .collect()
14316        };
14317
14318        // The update reached the pool, before and after the file was numbered.
14319        let mut applied = super::InodePool::new();
14320        applied.set_mtime(touched, set);
14321        let (_, mtime) = applied.add_inode(touched, seen, epoch);
14322        assert_eq!(
14323            mtime, set,
14324            "a pending mtime is lost when the file is numbered"
14325        );
14326        applied.set_mtime(touched, set);
14327        // The same calls with the updates skipped.
14328        let mut skipped = super::InodePool::new();
14329        skipped.add_inode(touched, seen, epoch);
14330        assert_eq!(
14331            later_files(&mut applied),
14332            later_files(&mut skipped),
14333            "a host-dependent mtime update renumbered later files"
14334        );
14335    }

14337    /// The serial grant follows the scheduler's real transitions: a granted
14338    /// thread holds it; filing its next request surrenders it; and a grant
14339    /// that releases the thread into a background call does not confer it,
14340    /// although that grant is the last one (`parked.running`).
14341    #[tokio::test]
14342    async fn the_serial_grant_ends_at_the_next_request_and_is_not_a_background_grant() {
14343        let (_config, state, tid, _) = cancellation_test_state();
14344        let first = Ivar::new();
14345        first.put(Ok(Resources::new(tid)));
14346        install_test_registration(&state, tid, first);
14347        assert!(!state.sched.lock().unwrap().holds_serial_grant(tid));
14348
14349        let grant = |state: &GlobalState| {
14350            let (chosen, request, response) =
14351                state.sched.lock().unwrap().select_test_turn().unwrap();
14352            assert_eq!(chosen, tid);
14353            crate::scheduler::finish_selected_turn(
14354                state.sched.clone(),
14355                state.global_time.clone(),
14356                chosen,
14357                request,
14358                response,
14359            )
14360        };
14361        grant(&state).await.unwrap();
14362        assert!(state.sched.lock().unwrap().holds_serial_grant(tid));
14363
14364        // The thread files its next request: a blocking external call.
14365        let next = state.sched.lock().unwrap().next_turns[&tid].req.clone();
14366        let mut background = Resources::new(tid);
14367        background.insert(
14368            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(tid, 1)),
14369            Permission::RW,
14370        );
14371        next.put(Ok(background));
14372        assert!(!state.sched.lock().unwrap().holds_serial_grant(tid));
14373
14374        // The scheduler releases it into the background. A background grant
14375        // unblocks the thread in step 4 and then skips the rest of the turn.
14376        assert!(grant(&state).await.is_err());
14377        let sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
14378        assert!(sched.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&tid));
14379        assert!(!sched.holds_serial_grant(tid));
14380    }
14381
14382    /// Only the thread holding the serial grant reaches a shared open file
14383    /// description. Its control messages move no clock, and the death of the
14384    /// lease holder's process ends the lease. A refused message fails the run.
14385    #[tokio::test]
14386    async fn shared_open_file_control_needs_the_serial_grant() {
14387        use nix::fcntl::OFlag;
14388
14389        use crate::fd::DetFd;
14390        use crate::fd::FdType;
14391        use crate::shared_open_files::OpenFileControl;
14392        use crate::shared_open_files::OpenFileControlReply;
14393        use crate::types::OpenFileId;
14394
14395        let config = Config {
14396            sequentialize_threads: true,
14397            ..Config::default()
14398        };
14399        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
14400        let granted = DetTid::from_raw(21);
14401        let other = DetTid::from_raw(22);
14402        let id = OpenFileId::new(granted, 0);
14403        {
14404            let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
14405            for tid in [granted, other] {
14406                sched.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
14407                sched.next_turns.insert(
14408                    tid,
14409                    ThreadNextTurn {
14410                        dettid: tid,
14411                        child_tid_addr: 0,
14412                        req: Ivar::new(),
14413                        resp: Ivar::new(),
14414                        protocol: Default::default(),
14415                    },
14416                );
14417            }
14418            sched.set_running_for_test(granted);
14419        }
14420        state
14421            .shared_open_files
14422            .lock()
14423            .unwrap()
14424            .insert(DetFd::new(3, OFlag::O_RDWR, FdType::Regular, id).model_for_test())
14425            .unwrap();
14426        let global_before = state.global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14427        let take = |tid: DetTid| {
14428            state.receive_rpc(
14429                reverie::Tid::from_raw(tid.as_raw()),
14430                (
14431                    DetTime::new(&config),
14432                    MmId::initial(tid),
14433                    GlobalRequest::SharedOpenFile(OpenFileControl::Take { id }),
14434                ),
14435            )
14436        };
14437
14438        assert!(matches!(
14439            take(granted).await,
14440            (
14441                None,
14442                GlobalResponse::SharedOpenFile(Ok(OpenFileControlReply::Taken { .. }))
14443            )
14444        ));
14445        assert!(state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap().is_leased(id));
14446        {
14447            let global_time = state.global_time.lock().unwrap();
14448            assert_eq!(global_time.as_nanos(), global_before, "no clock accounting");
14449            assert!(!global_time.contains_thread(granted));
14450        }
14451
14452        state.complete_physical_process_exit(granted.as_raw());
14453        assert!(!state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap().is_leased(id));
14454        assert!(!state.sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failed());
14455
14456        // A thread that does not hold the grant is refused, takes nothing,
14457        // and the refusal is a backend failure.
14458        assert!(matches!(
14459            take(other).await,
14460            (None, GlobalResponse::SharedOpenFile(Err(_)))
14461        ));
14462        assert!(!state.shared_open_files.lock().unwrap().is_leased(id));
14463        assert!(state.sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failed());
14464    }

14466    /// A SIGALRM ledger control message is answered with no logical time and
14467    /// moves no clock, and its answer is the ledger's: a send to a process that
14468    /// handles SIGALRM is refused, one to another process is not.
14469    #[tokio::test]
14470    async fn sigalrm_control_is_answered_before_clock_accounting() {
14471        let config = Config {
14472            sequentialize_threads: true,
14473            ..Config::default()
14474        };
14475        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
14476        let (handler, sender) = (DetTid::from_raw(21), DetTid::from_raw(22));
14477        {
14478            let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
14479            for tid in [handler, sender] {
14480                sched.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
14481                sched.next_turns.insert(
14482                    tid,
14483                    ThreadNextTurn {
14484                        dettid: tid,
14485                        child_tid_addr: 0,
14486                        req: Ivar::new(),
14487                        resp: Ivar::new(),
14488                        protocol: Default::default(),
14489                    },
14490                );
14491            }
14492            sched.set_sigalrm_handled(DetPid::from_raw(21), true);
14493            sched.set_running_for_test(sender);
14494        }
14495        let global_before = state.global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14496        let send_to = |target: DetTid| {
14497            state.receive_rpc(
14498                reverie::Tid::from_raw(sender.as_raw()),
14499                (
14500                    DetTime::new(&config),
14501                    MmId::initial(sender),
14502                    GlobalRequest::Sigalrm(super::SigalrmControl::SendTo(target)),
14503                ),
14504            )
14505        };
14506
14507        assert_eq!(
14508            send_to(handler).await,
14509            (None, GlobalResponse::Sigalrm(true))
14510        );
14511        assert_eq!(
14512            send_to(sender).await,
14513            (None, GlobalResponse::Sigalrm(false))
14514        );
14515        let global_time = state.global_time.lock().unwrap();
14516        assert_eq!(global_time.as_nanos(), global_before, "no clock accounting");
14517        assert!(!global_time.contains_thread(sender));
14518    }

14520    /// A host-input observation, and a report of a path the guest rebound,
14521    /// belong to the run whose global state receives them. Each is answered
14522    /// with no logical time, before any clock accounting,
14523    /// so it cannot move the global clock or the sender's, and the run's
14524    /// records are written with their end line at normal clean-up. The same
14525    /// request reaches this state from every backend: the openat handler sends
14526    /// it over the backend's RPC whether Detcore runs in the tracer or inside
14527    /// the guest.
14528    #[tokio::test]
14529    async fn host_input_observations_are_kept_by_the_run_and_written_at_its_end() {
14530        use detcore_model::host_input::HostFileIdentity;
14531        use detcore_model::host_input::HostInputLogEnd;
14532        use detcore_model::host_input::HostInputRecord;
14533
14534        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
14535        let log = directory.path().join("host-inputs");
14536        let config = Config {
14537            sequentialize_threads: true,
14538            record_host_inputs: true,
14539            host_input_log: Some(log.clone()),
14540            ..Config::default()
14541        };
14542        let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
14543        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(17);
14544        let identity = HostFileIdentity {
14545            dev: 33,
14546            ino: 7,
14547            size: 100,
14548            mtime_sec: 1_700_000_000,
14549            mtime_nsec: 5,
14550        };
14551        let mut sender_time = DetTime::new(&config);
14552        sender_time.add_syscall();
14553        sender_time.add_syscall();
14554        let global_before = state.global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14555        let response = state
14556            .receive_rpc(
14557                reverie::Tid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()),
14558                (
14559                    sender_time.clone(),
14560                    MmId::initial(dettid),
14561                    GlobalRequest::RecordHostInput {
14562                        path: "/etc/ld.so.cache".into(),
14563                        syscall: 12,
14564                        identity,
14565                    },
14566                ),
14567            )
14568            .await;
14569        assert_eq!(response, (None, GlobalResponse::RecordHostInput(())));
14570        for _ in 0..2 {
14571            let response = state
14572                .receive_rpc(
14573                    reverie::Tid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()),
14574                    (
14575                        sender_time.clone(),
14576                        MmId::initial(dettid),
14577                        GlobalRequest::RecordHostMutation {
14578                            path: "/data/F".into(),
14579                        },
14580                    ),
14581                )
14582                .await;
14583            assert_eq!(response, (None, GlobalResponse::RecordHostMutation(())));
14584        }
14585        {
14586            let global_time = state.global_time.lock().unwrap();
14587            assert_eq!(global_time.as_nanos(), global_before, "no clock accounting");
14588            assert!(
14589                !global_time.contains_thread(dettid),
14590                "the sender's clock was not pushed"
14591            );
14592        }
14593        assert!(!log.exists(), "nothing is written while the run goes on");
14594
14595        state.clean_up(false, &None).await;
14596        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&log).unwrap();
14597        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
14598        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 3, "{text}");
14599        assert_eq!(
14600            serde_json::from_str::<HostInputRecord>(lines[0]).unwrap(),
14601            HostInputRecord {
14602                path: "/etc/ld.so.cache".into(),
14603                dtid: 17,
14604                syscall: 12,
14605                identity,
14606            }
14607        );
14608        // A path rebound twice is one line.
14609        assert_eq!(
14610            serde_json::from_str::<detcore_model::host_input::HostMutationRecord>(lines[1])
14611                .unwrap()
14612                .mutated,
14613            "/data/F"
14614        );
14615        assert_eq!(
14616            serde_json::from_str::<HostInputLogEnd>(lines[2]).unwrap(),
14617            HostInputLogEnd { records: 2 }
14618        );
14619    }

14621    /// Two files on different filesystems can share an inode number; they
14622    /// are different files and must get different deterministic inodes, with
14623    /// first-seen mtimes of their own. Keyed by the number alone they shared
14624    /// one, so a guest comparing inode numbers took them for the same file,
14625    /// and the second file reported the first one's mtime.
14626    #[test]
14627    fn files_on_different_devices_with_one_inode_number_stay_distinct() {
14628        use super::ObservedMtime;
14629
14630        let epoch = LogicalTime::from_secs(1_798_761_600);
14631        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14632        // 76927 was /sys/bus/i2c/devices on the host that motivated this.
14633        let sysfs = crate::types::RawInode::new(23, 76_927);
14634        let rootfs = crate::types::RawInode::new(33, 76_927);
14635
14636        let (on_sysfs, sysfs_mtime) = pool.add_inode(sysfs, ObservedMtime::HostSpecific, epoch);
14637        let (on_rootfs, rootfs_mtime) = pool.add_inode(
14638            rootfs,
14639            ObservedMtime::Canonical(LogicalTime::from_secs(1)),
14640            epoch,
14641        );
14642        assert_ne!(on_sysfs, on_rootfs, "different files, different det inodes");
14643        assert_eq!(sysfs_mtime, epoch);
14644        assert_eq!(rootfs_mtime, LogicalTime::from_secs(1), "its own mtime");
14645        assert_eq!(
14646            pool.add_inode(sysfs, ObservedMtime::Unobserved, epoch).0,
14647            on_sysfs
14648        );
14649        assert_eq!(
14650            pool.add_inode(rootfs, ObservedMtime::Unobserved, epoch).0,
14651            on_rootfs
14652        );
14653    }

14655    /// Linux numbers a per-process procfs entry when it builds the entry's
14656    /// dentry, and the host can evict the dentry and build it again under a
14657    /// new number. Two `lsof` listings of `/proc/3/fd` found the same numbers
14658    /// in one `--verify` run and new ones in the other, where the host had
14659    /// rebuilt the entries between the listings. A rebuilt entry reached by
14660    /// its path keeps its number, so the guest sees the same numbers either
14661    /// way.
14662    #[test]
14663    fn a_rebuilt_procfs_entry_keeps_its_number() {
14664        use std::path::PathBuf;
14665
14666        use crate::procfs_inode::DirectoryInodes;
14667        use crate::procfs_inode::ProcfsDirectory;
14668        use crate::types::DetInode;
14669
14670        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14671        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14672        let proc_device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14673        let names: [&[u8]; 4] = [b".", b"..", b"0", b"1"];
14674        // The guest numbers of two listings of `/proc/3/fd`, in which the
14675        // host reports the inode numbers `first` and then `second`, as
14676        // `recv_determinize_inode` numbers them.
14677        let listings = |with_paths: bool, first: [u64; 4], second: [u64; 4]| -> Vec<DetInode> {
14678            let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14679            let directory = with_paths.then(|| ProcfsDirectory::new(PathBuf::from("/3/fd")));
14680            let inodes = DirectoryInodes::new(proc_device, directory);
14681            let mut numbers = Vec::new();
14682            for host in [first, second] {
14683                for (name, ino) in names.iter().zip(host) {
14684                    let (raw, procfs) = inodes.entry_inode(name, ino);
14685                    if let Some(procfs) = procfs {
14686                        let path = pool.procfs_path_key(&procfs);
14687                        pool.procfs_key(raw, path);
14688                    }
14689                    let sighting = super::InodeSighting::Listed(0);
14690                    numbers.push(pool.add_sighted_inode(raw, seen, t, sighting).0);
14691                }
14692            }
14693            numbers
14694        };
14695        let cached = [4_100, 4_000, 4_101, 4_102];
14696        // The open directory pins `.` and `..`; the fd entries were rebuilt.
14697        let rebuilt = [4_100, 4_000, 4_901, 4_902];
14698        assert_eq!(
14699            listings(true, cached, cached),
14700            listings(true, cached, rebuilt),
14701            "a host rebuilding procfs dentries changed guest inode numbers"
14702        );
14703        // The control: by host inode alone, the rebuilt entries were renumbered.
14704        assert_ne!(
14705            listings(false, cached, cached),
14706            listings(false, cached, rebuilt)
14707        );
14708    }
14709
14710    /// One procfs entry reached by two paths, as `/proc/<pid>/net/tcp` and
14711    /// `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/net/tcp` are, is one host inode, so it keeps
14712    /// one number however it is reached, and after the host rebuilds it.
14713    #[test]
14714    fn procfs_aliases_share_one_number() {
14715        use std::path::Path;
14716
14717        use crate::procfs_inode::path_inode;
14718
14719        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14720        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14721        let device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14722        let host = |ino| crate::types::RawInode::new(device, ino);
14723        let net = path_inode(device, Path::new("/3/net/tcp"));
14724        let task = path_inode(device, Path::new("/3/task/3/net/tcp"));
14725        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14726        let mut number = |raw, path| {
14727            pool.procfs_key(raw, path);
14728            pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t).0
14729        };
14730        let listed = number(host(4_100), net);
14731        assert_eq!(number(host(4_100), task), listed, "an alias");
14732        assert_eq!(number(host(4_900), task), listed, "rebuilt, by the alias");
14733        assert_eq!(number(host(4_901), net), listed, "rebuilt again");
14734        let other = number(host(4_200), path_inode(device, Path::new("/3/net/udp")));
14735        assert_ne!(other, listed);
14736    }

14738    /// A rebuilt procfs entry first seen without its path is new to the pool,
14739    /// as it was before paths were named; its path then leads to its new
14740    /// number, which it keeps across the next rebuild.
14741    #[test]
14742    fn a_numbered_host_inode_keeps_its_number_when_its_path_is_named() {
14743        use std::path::Path;
14744
14745        use crate::procfs_inode::path_inode;
14746
14747        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14748        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14749        let device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14750        let host = |ino| crate::types::RawInode::new(device, ino);
14751        let path = path_inode(device, Path::new("/3/fd/0"));
14752        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14753        pool.procfs_key(host(4_100), path);
14754        let first = pool.add_inode(host(4_100), seen, t).0;
14755        let without_path = pool.add_inode(host(4_900), seen, t).0;
14756        assert_ne!(without_path, first);
14757        pool.procfs_key(host(4_900), path);
14758        assert_eq!(pool.add_inode(host(4_900), seen, t).0, without_path);
14759        pool.procfs_key(host(4_901), path);
14760        assert_eq!(pool.add_inode(host(4_901), seen, t).0, without_path);
14761        assert_eq!(pool.add_inode(host(4_100), seen, t).0, first);
14762    }

14764    /// A write to a rebuilt procfs entry, which names the host inode only,
14765    /// sets the mtime of the number the entry kept, whether the descriptor's
14766    /// open named the path before the write (`procfs_key` then `set_mtime`) or
14767    /// after it (a pending mtime).
14768    #[test]
14769    fn a_write_to_a_rebuilt_procfs_entry_sets_the_mtime_of_its_number() {
14770        use std::path::Path;
14771
14772        use crate::procfs_inode::path_inode;
14773
14774        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14775        let written = LogicalTime::from_secs(7);
14776        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14777        let device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14778        let host = |ino| crate::types::RawInode::new(device, ino);
14779        let path = path_inode(device, Path::new("/3/comm"));
14780        for open_first in [true, false] {
14781            let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14782            pool.procfs_key(host(4_100), path);
14783            let (number, mtime) = pool.add_inode(host(4_100), seen, t);
14784            assert_ne!(mtime, written);
14785            if open_first {
14786                pool.procfs_key(host(4_900), path);
14787                pool.set_mtime(host(4_900), written);
14788            } else {
14789                pool.set_mtime(host(4_900), written);
14790                pool.procfs_key(host(4_900), path);
14791            }
14792            assert_eq!(
14793                pool.add_inode(host(4_100), seen, t),
14794                (number, written),
14795                "open_first={open_first}"
14796            );
14797            assert_eq!(pool.add_inode(host(4_900), seen, t), (number, written));
14798        }
14799    }

14801    /// A process ID the kernel gives out again names a new process, whose
14802    /// procfs entries are new files: Linux drops the old process's entries
14803    /// when it exits. The new process's `/proc/<pid>` takes a number of its
14804    /// own and keeps it across rebuilds, while a descriptor still open on
14805    /// the old process's entry keeps the old number.
14806    #[test]
14807    fn a_reused_task_id_names_new_procfs_entries() {
14808        use std::path::Path;
14809
14810        use crate::procfs_inode::ProcfsName;
14811        use crate::types::RawInode;
14812
14813        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14814        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14815        let device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14816        let host = |ino| RawInode::new(device, ino);
14817        let process = ProcfsName::new(device, Path::new("/7"));
14818        let number = |pool: &mut super::InodePool, raw: RawInode| {
14819            let path = pool.procfs_path_key(&process);
14820            pool.procfs_key(raw, path);
14821            pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t).0
14822        };
14823        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14824        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14825        let first = number(&mut pool, host(4_100));
14826        assert_eq!(number(&mut pool, host(4_900)), first, "rebuilt");
14827        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14828        let second = number(&mut pool, host(5_000));
14829        assert_ne!(second, first, "a new process took the old one's number");
14830        assert_eq!(pool.add_inode(host(4_900), seen, t).0, first, "held");
14831        assert_eq!(number(&mut pool, host(5_001)), second, "rebuilt");
14832        // A thread's directory also names the thread's incarnation.
14833        let thread = ProcfsName::new(device, Path::new("/7/task/9/stat"));
14834        assert_eq!(thread.tasks, [7, 9]);
14835        let before = pool.procfs_path_key(&thread);
14836        pool.count_incarnation(9);
14837        assert_ne!(pool.procfs_path_key(&thread), before);
14838    }
14839
14840    /// A pid Detcore gives out again is a new task: each registration of a
14841    /// task ID counts one more incarnation (`count_incarnation`), which the
14842    /// `ProcfsTask` answer reports for the process and the thread, and a file
14843    /// or directory bound to the earlier incarnation no longer names the
14844    /// task holding the numbers (`ProcfsTaskAnswer::still_names`).
14845    #[test]
14846    fn a_reused_pid_is_a_new_incarnation_for_procfs_files() {
14847        use crate::procfs::TaskIncarnation;
14848        use crate::types::DetTid;
14849        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14850        assert_eq!(pool.incarnation(7), 0, "an ID no task has held");
14851        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14852        pool.count_incarnation(9);
14853        assert_eq!((pool.incarnation(7), pool.incarnation(9)), (1, 1));
14854        let (seven, nine) = (DetTid::from_raw(7), DetTid::from_raw(9));
14855        let first = pool.procfs_task_answer(seven, Some(nine), (true, false));
14856        assert_eq!(
14857            first.incarnation(),
14858            TaskIncarnation {
14859                process: 1,
14860                thread: Some(1),
14861            }
14862        );
14863        let bound = first.incarnation();
14864        assert!(first.still_names(bound));
14865        // The process exits and is reaped; a new process takes pid 7.
14866        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14867        let reused = pool.procfs_task_answer(seven, Some(nine), (true, false));
14868        assert_eq!(reused.process_incarnation, 2);
14869        assert_eq!(reused.thread_incarnation, Some(1));
14870        assert!(!reused.still_names(bound), "the file of the old pid 7");
14871        assert!(reused.still_names(reused.incarnation()));
14872        // A thread ID given out again is a new thread of the same process.
14873        pool.count_incarnation(9);
14874        let thread_reused = pool.procfs_task_answer(seven, Some(nine), (true, false));
14875        assert!(!thread_reused.still_names(reused.incarnation()));
14876        // A task that is gone, or a zombie that was reaped, is no task,
14877        // whatever its incarnation.
14878        let gone = pool.procfs_task_answer(seven, None, (false, false));
14879        assert!(!gone.still_names(gone.incarnation()));
14880        // The process's own file names no thread.
14881        assert_eq!(gone.thread_incarnation, None);
14882    }

14884    /// Reading a rendered file's state inserts nothing; a write keeps one
14885    /// entry for that inode only.
14886    #[test]
14887    fn a_read_of_rendered_file_state_keeps_nothing() {
14888        use crate::procfs::listing::RenderedFileChange;
14889        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14890        let read = pool.rendered_file_state(5, RenderedFileChange::Read);
14891        assert_eq!(read, Default::default());
14892        assert!(pool.rendered_file_states.is_empty());
14893        let written = pool.rendered_file_state(5, RenderedFileChange::Mtime(3, 4));
14894        assert_eq!(written.mtime, Some((3, 4)));
14895        let hinted = pool.rendered_file_state(5, RenderedFileChange::WriteHint(2));
14896        assert_eq!((hinted.mtime, hinted.write_hint), (Some((3, 4)), 2));
14897        assert_eq!(
14898            pool.rendered_file_state(6, RenderedFileChange::Read),
14899            Default::default()
14900        );
14901        assert_eq!(pool.rendered_file_states.len(), 1);
14902        assert_eq!(
14903            pool.rendered_file_state(5, RenderedFileChange::Read),
14904            hinted
14905        );
14906    }

14908    /// A directory snapshot returns its entries after it was taken, and a
14909    /// task it lists can exit, and a new thread take its ID, in between. The
14910    /// entry still names the task the snapshot listed: an entry of the old
14911    /// task rebuilt since keeps the old task's number, rather than adopting
14912    /// the new task's.
14913    #[test]
14914    fn a_snapshot_entry_names_the_task_that_held_its_id() {
14915        use std::path::Path;
14916
14917        use crate::procfs_inode::ProcfsName;
14918        use crate::types::RawInode;
14919
14920        let t = LogicalTime::from_nanos(0);
14921        let seen = super::ObservedMtime::Unobserved;
14922        let device = libc::makedev(0, 23);
14923        let host = |ino| RawInode::new(device, ino);
14924        let number = |pool: &mut super::InodePool, raw: RawInode, name: &ProcfsName| {
14925            let path = pool.procfs_path_key(name);
14926            pool.procfs_key(raw, path);
14927            pool.add_inode(raw, seen, t).0
14928        };
14929        let process = ProcfsName::new(device, Path::new("/7"));
14930        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14931        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14932        let first = number(&mut pool, host(4_100), &process);
14933        let listed = process.clone().in_snapshot(pool.threads_counted);
14934        pool.count_incarnation(7);
14935        let second = number(&mut pool, host(5_000), &process);
14936        assert_ne!(second, first, "a new process took the old one's number");
14937        assert_eq!(
14938            number(&mut pool, host(4_900), &listed),
14939            first,
14940            "the listed process's entry, rebuilt"
14941        );
14942        // An ID no thread held when the snapshot was taken names no task.
14943        let unborn = ProcfsName::new(device, Path::new("/8"));
14944        let listed = unborn.clone().in_snapshot(pool.threads_counted);
14945        let unsalted = pool.procfs_path_key(&listed);
14946        assert_eq!(unsalted, pool.procfs_path_key(&unborn));
14947        pool.count_incarnation(8);
14948        assert_eq!(pool.procfs_path_key(&listed), unsalted);
14949        assert_ne!(pool.procfs_path_key(&unborn), unsalted);
14950    }

14952    /// Only an exact whole-second 0 or 1 host mtime is canonical
14953    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3639).
14954    #[test]
14955    fn only_exact_canonical_host_mtimes_are_kept() {
14956        use super::ObservedMtime;
14957
14958        assert_eq!(
14959            ObservedMtime::from_host_mtime(1, 0),
14960            ObservedMtime::Canonical(LogicalTime::from_secs(1))
14961        );
14962        assert_eq!(
14963            ObservedMtime::from_host_mtime(0, 0),
14964            ObservedMtime::Canonical(LogicalTime::from_secs(0))
14965        );
14966        for (secs, nanos) in [(1, 5), (0, 1), (2, 0), (-1, 0), (1_600_000_000, 0)] {
14967            assert_eq!(
14968                ObservedMtime::from_host_mtime(secs, nanos),
14969                ObservedMtime::HostSpecific,
14970                "{secs}.{nanos:09} is a real timestamp, not a canonical one"
14971            );
14972        }
14973    }

14975    /// The first-seen policy is applied at the first stat, whichever syscall
14976    /// minted the inode, and is not re-applied once resolved.
14977    #[test]
14978    fn first_seen_mtime_is_resolved_by_the_first_stat() {
14979        use super::ObservedMtime;
14980
14981        let epoch = LogicalTime::from_secs(1_798_761_600);
14982        let canonical = ObservedMtime::Canonical(LogicalTime::from_secs(1));
14983        let mut pool = super::InodePool::new();
14984
14985        // An ordinary file reports the epoch.
14986        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(
14987            crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 10),
14988            ObservedMtime::HostSpecific,
14989            epoch,
14990        );
14991        assert_eq!(mtime, epoch);
14992        // A canonical file keeps its mtime.
14993        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 11), canonical, epoch);
14994        assert_eq!(mtime, LogicalTime::from_secs(1));
14995
14996        // A read or getdents mints the inode first; the later stat decides.
14997        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(
14998            crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 12),
14999            ObservedMtime::Unobserved,
15000            epoch,
15001        );
15002        assert_eq!(mtime, epoch, "an unresolved mtime reads as the epoch");
15003        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 12), canonical, epoch);
15004        assert_eq!(mtime, LogicalTime::from_secs(1));
15005
15006        // Once resolved, a later observation does not change it.
15007        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 10), canonical, epoch);
15008        assert_eq!(mtime, epoch);
15009        let (_, mtime) = pool.add_inode(
15010            crate::types::RawInode::new(1, 11),
15011            ObservedMtime::HostSpecific,
15012            epoch,
15013        );
15014        assert_eq!(mtime, LogicalTime::from_secs(1));
15015    }
15016}

15018#[cfg(test)]
15019mod robust_exit_clock_tests {

15044
15045    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
15046    struct WakeObservation {
15047        wakes: Vec<(DetTid, FutexID)>,
15048        counts: Vec<u64>,
15049        clocks: serde_json::Value,
15050        turn: u64,
15051    }
15052
15053    #[derive(Debug)]
15054    struct RpcObservation {
15055        sender: DetTid,
15056        kind: &'static str,
15057        accepted: bool,
15058        clocks: serde_json::Value,
15059        queued: Vec<DetTid>,
15060        waiters: usize,
15061        turn: u64,
15062    }
15063
15064    // This is only a sender-bound transport, as in Reverie's WrappedFrom.
15065    // Replies, clock accounting, wakes and deregistration come from GlobalState.
15066    struct ExitRpc<'a> {
15067        state: &'a GlobalState,
15068        sender: DetTid,
15069        observations: &'a Mutex<Vec<WakeObservation>>,
15070        rpc_observations: &'a Mutex<Vec<RpcObservation>>,
15071    }
15072
15073    #[reverie::tool]
15074    impl GlobalRPC<GlobalState> for ExitRpc<'_> {
15075        async fn send_rpc(
15076            &self,
15077            request: <GlobalState as GlobalTool>::Request,
15078        ) -> <GlobalState as GlobalTool>::Response {
15079            let kind = match &request.2 {
15080                GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(wakes) if wakes.is_empty() => "empty-wake",
15081                GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(_) => "wake",
15082                GlobalRequest::DeregisterThread(_) => "deregister",
15083                _ => panic!("unexpected exit RPC: {:?}", request.2),
15084            };
15085            let wakes = match &request.2 {
15086                GlobalRequest::RobustListWakes(wakes) if !wakes.is_empty() => Some(wakes.clone()),
15087                _ => None,
15088            };
15089            let response = self
15090                .state
15091                .receive_rpc(Tid::from_raw(self.sender.as_raw()), request)
15092                .await;
15093            let clocks = serde_json::to_value(&*self.state.global_time.lock().unwrap()).unwrap();
15094            {
15095                let sched = self.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15096                self.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap().push(RpcObservation {
15097                    sender: self.sender,
15098                    kind,
15099                    accepted: !matches!(response.1, GlobalResponse::ThreadExited),
15100                    clocks: clocks.clone(),
15101                    queued: sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect(),
15102                    waiters: sched
15103                        .blocked
15104                        .futex_waiters
15105                        .values()
15106                        .map(Vec::len)
15107                        .sum::<usize>(),
15108                    turn: sched.turn,
15109                });
15110            }
15111            if let Some(wakes) = wakes {
15112                let GlobalResponse::RobustListWakes(counts) = &response.1 else {
15113                    panic!("a complete admitted exit batch was refused: {response:?}");
15114                };
15115                let clocks =
15116                    serde_json::to_value(&*self.state.global_time.lock().unwrap()).unwrap();
15117                let turn = self.state.sched.lock().unwrap().turn;
15118                self.observations.lock().unwrap().push(WakeObservation {
15119                    wakes,
15120                    counts: counts.clone(),
15121                    clocks,
15122                    turn,
15123                });
15124            }
15125            response
15126        }
15127
15128        fn config(&self) -> &Config {
15129            &self.state.cfg
15130        }
15131    }

15133    struct Fixture {
15134        state: GlobalState,
15135        tool: Detcore,
15136        owners: [ThreadState<()>; 2],
15137        initial_clocks: [DetTime; 2],
15138        waiters: [DetTid; 2],
15139        peer: DetTid,
15140        futexes: [FutexID; 2],
15141        observations: Mutex<Vec<WakeObservation>>,
15142        rpc_observations: Mutex<Vec<RpcObservation>>,
15143    }
15144
15145    impl Fixture {
15146        fn new(
15147            reason: RobustListExit,
15148            equal_clocks: bool,
15149            empty_owner: Option<usize>,
15150            needs_rpc_cancellation: bool,
15151        ) -> Self {
15152            let config = Config {
15153                sequentialize_threads: true,
15154                ..Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15155                    backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = needs_rpc_cancellation
15156                })
15157            };
15158            let state = GlobalState::initialize(&config, false);
15159            let parent = DetTid::from_raw(1);
15160            let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
15161            let worker = DetTid::from_raw(18);
15162            let waiters = [DetTid::from_raw(21), DetTid::from_raw(23)];
15163            let peer = DetTid::from_raw(25);
15164            let mm = MmId::initial(leader);
15165            let mut first = ThreadState::new(leader, &config, ());
15166            first.detpid = Some(leader);
15167            let mut second = first.clone();
15168            second.dettid = worker;
15169            let mut inherited = DetTime::new(&config);
15170            inherited.add_syscall_with_cost(1_000);
15171            let first_initial = inherited.clone_for_child();
15172            inherited.add_syscall_with_cost(370);
15173            let second_initial = inherited.clone_for_child();
15174            first.thread_logical_time = first_initial.clone();
15175            second.thread_logical_time = second_initial.clone();
15176            first
15177                .thread_logical_time
15178                .add_syscall_with_cost(if equal_clocks { 407 } else { 37 });
15179            second.thread_logical_time.add_syscall_with_cost(37);
15180            first.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404100));
15181            second.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404200));
15182            let object = SharedMemoryObjectId::Anonymous {
15183                origin: MmId::initial(parent),
15184                sequence: 1,
15185            };
15186            let futexes = [FutexID::shared(object, 0), FutexID::shared(object, 8)];
15187            first.stage_robust_list_wakes(
15188                reason,
15189                vec![
15190                    (
15191                        worker,
15192                        if empty_owner == Some(1) {
15193                            Vec::new()
15194                        } else {
15195                            vec![RobustListWake { futex: futexes[1] }]
15196                        },
15197                    ),
15198                    (
15199                        leader,
15200                        if empty_owner == Some(0) {
15201                            Vec::new()
15202                        } else {
15203                            vec![RobustListWake { futex: futexes[0] }]
15204                        },
15205                    ),
15206                ],
15207            );
15208            {
15209                let mut sched = state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15210                sched.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
15211                sched.thread_tree.add_child(parent, leader, true);
15212                sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
15213                for tid in [waiters[0], waiters[1], peer] {
15214                    sched.thread_tree.add_child(parent, tid, true);
15215                }
15216                for tid in [leader, worker, waiters[0], waiters[1], peer] {
15217                    sched.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15218                    sched.next_turns.insert(
15219                        tid,
15220                        ThreadNextTurn {
15221                            dettid: tid,
15222                            child_tid_addr: 0,
15223                            req: Ivar::new(),
15224                            resp: Ivar::new(),
15225                            protocol: Default::default(),
15226                        },
15227                    );
15228                    sched.install_test_exec_incarnation(
15229                        tid,
15230                        if tid == leader || tid == worker {
15231                            mm
15232                        } else {
15233                            MmId::initial(tid)
15234                        },
15235                    );
15236                }
15237                // Both owners have returned from their last guest turn and
15238                // retain its empty next request until their exit callbacks.
15239                // The independent peer is ready, but cannot pass quiescence.
15240                sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
15241                sched.runqueue_push_back(worker);
15242                sched.runqueue_push_back(peer);
15243                sched.next_turns[&peer].req.put(Ok(Resources::new(peer)));
15244                for (waiter, futex) in waiters.into_iter().zip(futexes) {
15245                    sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
15246                }
15247            }
15248            {
15249                let mut time = state.global_time.lock().unwrap();
15250                for (tid, clock) in [(leader, &first_initial), (worker, &second_initial)] {
15251                    time.update_global_time(tid, clock.as_nanos(), clock.inherited_nanos());
15252                }
15253            }
15254            let tool = Detcore::new(Tid::from_raw(leader.as_raw()), &config);
15255            Self {
15256                state,
15257                tool,
15258                owners: [first, second],
15259                initial_clocks: [first_initial, second_initial],
15260                waiters,
15261                peer,
15262                futexes,
15263                observations: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
15264                rpc_observations: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),

15268        fn assert_clocks(&self, completed: &[usize]) -> serde_json::Value {
15269            let time = self.state.global_time.lock().unwrap();
15270            let snapshot = serde_json::to_value(&*time).unwrap();
15271            let epoch = DetTime::new(&self.state.cfg).as_nanos();
15272            let mut expected = epoch;
15273            for (index, owner) in self.owners.iter().enumerate() {
15274                let clock = if completed.contains(&index) {
15275                    &owner.thread_logical_time
15276                } else {
15277                    &self.initial_clocks[index]
15278                };
15279                assert_eq!(time.threads_time(owner.dettid), clock.as_nanos());
15280                assert_eq!(
15281                    snapshot["inherited_time"][owner.dettid.as_raw().to_string()],
15282                    serde_json::to_value(clock.inherited_nanos()).unwrap()
15283                );
15284                expected = expected + (clock.as_nanos() - epoch - clock.inherited_nanos());
15285            }
15286            assert_eq!(
15287                time.as_nanos(),
15288                expected,
15289                "only each owner's own uninherited work contributes"
15290            );
15291            snapshot
15292        }
15293
15294        async fn exit(&self, index: usize, status: ExitStatus) {
15295            self.exit_thread(self.owners[index].clone(), status).await;
15296        }
15297
15298        async fn exit_thread(&self, thread: ThreadState<()>, status: ExitStatus) {
15299            let rpc = ExitRpc {
15300                state: &self.state,
15301                sender: thread.dettid,
15302                observations: &self.observations,
15303                rpc_observations: &self.rpc_observations,
15304            };
15305            let exit =
15306                self.tool
15307                    .on_exit_thread(Tid::from_raw(rpc.sender.as_raw()), &rpc, thread, status);
15308            let mut exit = std::pin::pin!(exit);
15309            // On the CLI's current-thread ptrace route, Ready on the first
15310            // poll excludes a new queued-observer window inside this callback.
15311            // Multi-thread embeddings still admit concurrent scheduler reads;
15312            // the RPC observations separately check the actual global actions.
15313            assert!(
15314                matches!(futures::poll!(exit.as_mut()), Poll::Ready(Ok(()))),
15315                "exit callback yielded before its accounting and cleanup completed"
15316            );
15317        }
15318
15319        async fn nonmember_exit(&self, raw_tid: i32) {
15320            let mut thread = self.owners[0].clone();
15321            thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(raw_tid);
15322            thread.thread_logical_time = DetTime::new(&self.state.cfg);
15323            let tid = thread.dettid;
15324            {
15325                let mut sched = self.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15326                sched
15327                    .thread_tree
15328                    .add_child(self.owners[0].dettid, tid, false);
15329                sched.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15330                sched.next_turns.insert(
15331                    tid,
15332                    ThreadNextTurn {
15333                        dettid: tid,
15334                        child_tid_addr: 0,
15335                        req: Ivar::new(),
15336                        resp: Ivar::new(),
15337                        protocol: Default::default(),
15338                    },
15339                );
15340                sched.install_test_exec_incarnation(tid, thread.mm_id);
15341                sched.runqueue_push_back(tid);
15342            }
15343            let before = self.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap().len();
15344            self.exit_thread(thread, ExitStatus::Exited(0)).await;
15345            let observations = self.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap();
15346            assert_eq!(
15347                observations.len(),
15348                before + 1,
15349                "a nonmember sent an acknowledgement or wake RPC"
15350            );
15351            assert_eq!(observations[before].sender, tid);
15352            assert_eq!(observations[before].kind, "deregister");
15353            assert!(observations[before].accepted);
15354        }
15355    }

15357    #[tokio::test]
15358    async fn robust_exit_acknowledgements_preserve_global_action_order_and_eligibility() {
15359        for order in [[0, 1], [1, 0]] {
15360            for empty_owner in [0, 1] {
15361                let f = Fixture::new(RobustListExit::ExitGroup, false, Some(empty_owner), false);
15362                f.nonmember_exit(30).await;
15363                assert!(f.observations.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
15364                let queue_before_first: Vec<_> = f
15365                    .state
15366                    .sched
15367                    .lock()
15368                    .unwrap()
15369                    .run_queue
15370                    .tids()
15371                    .copied()
15372                    .collect();
15373                let first_start = f.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap().len();
15374                f.exit(order[0], ExitStatus::Exited(0)).await;
15375                let first_clocks = f.assert_clocks(&[order[0]]);
15376                {
15377                    let observations = f.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap();
15378                    let actions = &observations[first_start..];
15379                    assert_eq!(
15380                        actions.iter().map(|a| a.kind).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15381                        ["empty-wake", "deregister"]
15382                    );
15383                    assert!(actions.iter().all(|a| a.accepted
15384                        && a.sender == f.owners[order[0]].dettid
15385                        && a.clocks == first_clocks
15386                        && a.waiters == 2
15387                        && a.turn == 0));
15388                    assert_eq!(
15389                        actions[0].queued, queue_before_first,
15390                        "empty acknowledgement changed scheduler eligibility"
15391                    );
15392                }
15393                f.nonmember_exit(31).await;
15394                f.assert_clocks(&[order[0]]);
15395                assert!(
15396                    f.observations.lock().unwrap().is_empty(),
15397                    "a nonmember completed the physical-exit barrier"
15398                );
15399                let queue_before_last: Vec<_> = f
15400                    .state
15401                    .sched
15402                    .lock()
15403                    .unwrap()
15404                    .run_queue
15405                    .tids()
15406                    .copied()
15407                    .collect();
15408                let last_start = f.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap().len();
15409                f.exit(order[1], ExitStatus::Exited(0)).await;
15410                let final_clocks = f.assert_clocks(&[0, 1]);
15411                {
15412                    let observations = f.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap();
15413                    let actions = &observations[last_start..];
15414                    assert_eq!(
15415                        actions.iter().map(|a| a.kind).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15416                        ["empty-wake", "wake", "deregister"]
15417                    );
15418                    assert!(actions.iter().all(|a| a.accepted
15419                        && a.sender == f.owners[order[1]].dettid
15420                        && a.clocks == final_clocks
15421                        && a.turn == 0));
15422                    assert_eq!(actions[0].waiters, 2);
15423                    assert_eq!(actions[1].waiters, 1);
15424                    assert_eq!(actions[0].queued, queue_before_last);
15425                    assert_eq!(
15426                        actions[1].queued, queue_before_last,
15427                        "wake bypassed deferred admission"
15428                    );
15429                }
15430                f.nonmember_exit(32).await;
15431                f.assert_clocks(&[0, 1]);
15432                assert_eq!(f.observations.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
15433                let observations = f.rpc_observations.lock().unwrap();
15434                for owner in &f.owners {
15435                    assert_eq!(
15436                        observations
15437                            .iter()
15438                            .filter(|a| a.sender == owner.dettid && a.kind == "empty-wake")
15439                            .count(),
15440                        1,
15441                        "each unique matching owner, including an empty-wake owner, must acknowledge before the batch clears"
15442                    );
15443                }
15444            }
15445        }
15446    }

15448    #[tokio::test]
15449    async fn robust_exit_callbacks_preserve_owner_clocks_across_arrival_orders() {
15450        for reason in [
15451            RobustListExit::ExitGroup,
15452            RobustListExit::Signal(libc::SIGTERM),
15453        ] {
15454            for equal_clocks in [false, true] {
15455                for empty_owner in [None, Some(0), Some(1)] {
15456                    let mut results = Vec::new();
15457                    for order in [[0, 1], [1, 0]] {
15458                        let f = Fixture::new(reason, equal_clocks, empty_owner, false);
15459                        let status = match reason {
15460                            RobustListExit::ExitGroup => ExitStatus::Exited(0),
15461                            RobustListExit::Signal(_) => {
15462                                ExitStatus::Signaled(Signal::SIGTERM, false)
15463                            }
15464                        };
15465                        f.exit(order[0], status).await;
15466                        f.assert_clocks(&[order[0]]);
15467                        assert!(f.observations.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
15468                        {
15469                            let sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15470                            assert_eq!(
15471                                sched
15472                                    .blocked
15473                                    .futex_waiters
15474                                    .values()
15475                                    .map(Vec::len)
15476                                    .sum::<usize>(),
15477                                2
15478                            );
15479                            assert_eq!(sched.turn, 0);
15480                        }
15481                        // An actually runnable peer must still wait for the
15482                        // remaining owner's outstanding next request.
15483                        {
15484                            let last = Err(SkipTurn);
15485                            let turn = crate::scheduler::do_a_turn_blocking(
15486                                f.state.sched.clone(),
15487                                f.state.global_time.clone(),
15488                                &last,
15489                            );
15490                            let mut turn = std::pin::pin!(turn);
15491                            assert!(matches!(futures::poll!(turn.as_mut()), Poll::Pending));
15492                        }
15493                        f.exit(order[0], status).await;
15494                        f.assert_clocks(&[order[0]]);
15495                        assert!(
15496                            f.observations.lock().unwrap().is_empty(),
15497                            "duplicate physical exit released an incomplete group"
15498                        );
15499                        f.exit(order[1], status).await;
15500                        let clocks = f.assert_clocks(&[0, 1]);
15501                        {
15502                            let observations = f.observations.lock().unwrap();
15503                            assert_eq!(observations.len(), 1);
15504                            let expected: Vec<_> = (0..2)
15505                                .filter(|i| Some(*i) != empty_owner)
15506                                .map(|i| (f.owners[i].dettid, f.futexes[i]))
15507                                .collect();
15508                            assert_eq!(observations[0].wakes, expected);
15509                            assert_eq!(observations[0].counts, vec![1; expected.len()]);
15510                            assert_eq!(
15511                                observations[0].clocks, clocks,
15512                                "all owner clocks must be accounted before wake admission"
15513                            );
15514                            assert_eq!(observations[0].turn, 0);
15515                        }
15516                        f.exit(order[1], status).await;
15517                        assert_eq!(f.assert_clocks(&[0, 1]), clocks);
15518                        assert_eq!(
15519                            f.observations.lock().unwrap().len(),
15520                            1,
15521                            "repeated cleanup emitted a second batch"
15522                        );
15523                        {
15524                            let sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15525                            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(f.waiters[0]));
15526                            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(f.waiters[1]));
15527                        }
15528                        // Drive the real step1/step2 drain and one peer turn;
15529                        // no test-only scheduler implementation or reply shim.
15530                        let result = crate::scheduler::do_a_turn_blocking(
15531                            f.state.sched.clone(),
15532                            f.state.global_time.clone(),
15533                            &Err(SkipTurn),
15534                        )
15535                        .await;
15536                        assert!(result.is_ok());
15537                        let sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15538                        assert_eq!(sched.turn, 1);
15539                        let queued: Vec<_> = sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect();
15540                        for (i, waiter) in f.waiters.iter().enumerate() {
15541                            assert_eq!(queued.contains(waiter), Some(i) != empty_owner);
15542                        }
15543                        assert!(queued.contains(&f.peer));
15544                        results.push((
15545                            clocks,
15546                            queued,
15547                            std::mem::take(&mut *f.observations.lock().unwrap()),
15548                        ));
15549                    }
15550                    assert_eq!(
15551                        results[0], results[1],
15552                        "callback order changed final clocks, typed wake observations or the actual scheduler drain"
15553                    );
15554                }
15555            }
15556        }
15557    }

15559    #[tokio::test]
15560    async fn robust_exit_callbacks_keep_rejected_or_mismatched_batches_incomplete() {
15561        for rejection in ["old-mm", "tombstone", "wrong-signal", "normal-exit"] {
15562            let f = Fixture::new(
15563                RobustListExit::Signal(libc::SIGTERM),
15564                false,
15565                None,
15566                rejection == "tombstone",
15567            );
15568            let rejected = f.owners[0].dettid;
15569            let mm = f.owners[0].mm_id;
15570            f.exit(1, ExitStatus::Signaled(Signal::SIGTERM, false))
15571                .await;
15572            let replacement_request = Ivar::new();
15573            if rejection == "old-mm" {
15574                let mut sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15575                sched.install_test_exec_incarnation(rejected, mm.for_exec(rejected));
15576                sched.next_turns.insert(
15577                    rejected,
15578                    ThreadNextTurn {
15579                        dettid: rejected,
15580                        child_tid_addr: 0,
15581                        req: replacement_request.clone(),
15582                        resp: Ivar::new(),
15583                        protocol: Default::default(),
15584                    },
15585                );
15586                let mut replacement_time = f.owners[0].thread_logical_time.clone();
15587                replacement_time.add_syscall_with_cost(500);
15588                f.state.global_time.lock().unwrap().update_global_time(
15589                    rejected,
15590                    replacement_time.as_nanos(),
15591                    replacement_time.inherited_nanos(),
15592                );
15593            } else if rejection == "tombstone" {
15594                // Use the real cancelling backend gate; keep its matching Mm.
15595                let mut sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15596                sched.logically_kill_thread(&rejected, &rejected, mm);
15597            }
15598            let before = serde_json::to_value(&*f.state.global_time.lock().unwrap()).unwrap();
15599            let status = match rejection {
15600                "wrong-signal" => ExitStatus::Signaled(Signal::SIGKILL, false),
15601                "normal-exit" => ExitStatus::Exited(0),
15602                _ => ExitStatus::Signaled(Signal::SIGTERM, false),
15603            };
15604            f.exit(0, status).await;
15605            assert!(
15606                f.observations.lock().unwrap().is_empty(),
15607                "{rejection} released a group"
15608            );
15609            if rejection == "old-mm" || rejection == "tombstone" {
15610                assert_eq!(
15611                    serde_json::to_value(&*f.state.global_time.lock().unwrap()).unwrap(),
15612                    before,
15613                    "rejected acknowledgement changed clock state"
15614                );
15615            }
15616            let sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15617            assert_eq!(
15618                sched
15619                    .blocked
15620                    .futex_waiters
15621                    .values()
15622                    .map(Vec::len)
15623                    .sum::<usize>(),
15624                2,
15625                "rejected group lost a real waiter"
15626            );
15627            assert!(
15628                f.waiters
15629                    .iter()
15630                    .all(|tid| !sched.run_queue.contains_tid(*tid))
15631            );
15632            if rejection == "old-mm" {
15633                assert!(sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(rejected, mm.for_exec(rejected)));
15634                assert_eq!(
15635                    sched.next_turns[&rejected].req, replacement_request,
15636                    "old cleanup destroyed replacement registration"
15637                );
15638            }
15639        }
15640    }

15657    #[tokio::test]
15658    async fn backend_failure_preserves_consuming_robust_exit_clock_accounting() {
15659        for order in [[0, 1], [1, 0]] {
15660            let f = Fixture::new(RobustListExit::ExitGroup, false, None, false);
15661            let selected = {
15662                let mut sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15663                sched.next_turns.get_mut(&f.peer).unwrap().req = Ivar::new();
15664                sched.select_test_turn().unwrap()
15665            };
15666            let responses = {
15667                let sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15668                f.waiters.map(|tid| sched.next_turns[&tid].resp.clone())
15669            };
15670            let mut turn = std::pin::pin!(crate::scheduler::finish_selected_turn(
15671                f.state.sched.clone(),
15672                f.state.global_time.clone(),
15673                selected.0,
15674                selected.1,
15675                selected.2,
15676            ));
15677            assert!(futures::poll!(turn.as_mut()).is_pending());
15678            f.state.report_backend_failure(reverie::BackendFailure {
15679                pid: Tid::from_raw(17),
15680                tid: Tid::from_raw(18),
15681                phase: "native robust cleanup control",
15682            });
15683            for index in order {
15684                f.exit(index, ExitStatus::Exited(0)).await;
15685            }
15686            assert!(matches!(futures::poll!(turn.as_mut()), Poll::Ready(Err(_))));
15687            f.assert_clocks(&[0, 1]);
15688            let observations = f.observations.lock().unwrap();
15689            assert_eq!(observations.len(), 1, "one complete batch");
15690            assert_eq!(observations[0].counts, vec![1, 1]);
15691            assert!(
15692                responses
15693                    .iter()
15694                    .all(|response| response.try_read().is_none())
15695            );
15696            let mut sched = f.state.sched.lock().unwrap();
15697            assert_eq!(sched.turn, 0);
15698            for owner in &f.owners {
15699                assert!(!sched.next_turns.contains_key(&owner.dettid));
15700                assert!(!sched.note_deregistration_accounted(owner.dettid));
15701            }
15702        }
15703    }
